commit_message:
chat: keep subagent progress visible and show models early

## Summary

- Keep late-discovered background agents from remaining generic tools or disappearing into completed-step disclosures, including when a nested worker is still active after its parent finishes.
- Preserve sibling tool content, keyboard focus, and observer cleanup when a completed tool is promoted to the shared subagent pill.
- Show the child's known model at startup rather than waiting for usage or completion. Carry canonical model identity through live progress and restored history so matching models, including BYOK display-name variants, do not produce redundant labels. Preserve Auto routing on configuration-only updates.
- Make synchronous/background progress and navigation parity inspectable with 27 interactive lifecycle fixtures (58 themed variants), using real chat models, pills, child transcripts, and session/chat result links.

## Intended behavior and scope

The clickable pill remains in the response to the request that spawned the child and updates there through startup, follow-ups, and completion. A child first discovered after parent completion is appended to that original response; an existing launch that is reclassified is promoted in place. No pinned activity area or duplicate launch pill is added to later turns. Peer chats and independent sessions retain their structured link presentation.

The separate Autopilot case where task_complete succeeds but the SDK idle/parent turn-complete handoff is missing is not addressed here.

## Validation

- 289 focused cross-layer subagent/background regression tests passed before commit.
- ESLint passed for all 23 changed TypeScript files.
- All 58 themed component captures passed their assertions and disposal checks.
- Browser interaction checks verified pointer/keyboard opening and changing progress in parent and child views, including completed-parent, nested, and retained-worker cases.
- The broader client type check has three previously reproduced SDK baseline errors involving clientInfo and autoTier; no new fixture diagnostics.
- Additional local testing is in progress; this PR is intentionally a draft.

## Manual testing

Start the Component Explorer Server and filter for agent-lifecycle. Compare SynchronousRunning and BackgroundRunning: use Advance Child Progress, click the bordered pill to inspect its live child transcript, advance again, and return with Back to Parent. Also inspect ParentCompleteChildRunning, ChildStartsAfterParentComplete, LateSubagentClassification, RetainedFollowUpLatestTurn, NestedBackgroundChat, and the model-label variants.

Fixes #335638

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

commit_message:
fix: centre the fork tooltip on the fork button

The tooltip's caret sat left of the fork button in the chat checkpoint
toolbar. Three independent causes, each verified by measurement in a
running build.

1. The decorative "·" separator was an in-flow ::before on the fork
   action item, so the item's border box spanned dot + gap + button.
   BaseActionViewItem anchors the managed hover to that element and
   HoverWidget centres a pointer hover on its rect, putting the tooltip
   3.8px left. The same box drives the click listeners, so the dot was
   also a live target for Fork. Draw the separator in the item's left
   gutter instead: absolutely positioned, reserved with margin-left, and
   pointer-events: none. Net layout shift 0.44px.

2. HoverWidget positions the hover at target.center.x - clientWidth / 2
   but placed the caret at Math.round(hoverWidth / 2), biasing it 0.5px
   right whenever the hover's width is odd. Since the hover's own x is
   fractional, the rounding could never align the caret to a device
   pixel; it only broke the centring. Drop it on both axes.

3. hoverWidget.ts treats Constants.PointerSize as the caret's half
   width, but the caret was a content-box square whose 1px borders
   Chromium rounds down to whole device pixels under zoom, leaving a
   5.86px box whose centre is 2.93px from its origin. Size it as a
   border box so the box stays 6px and its centre stays exactly
   PointerSize at any zoom.

Measured against each hover's real anchor element, every pointer tooltip
now centres within 0.011px, independent of width parity and zoom level.

Do not open inline math on an escaped dollar sign in markdown

The lookbehind of math_inline_single and math_inline_double accepted
a backslash before the opening `$`, because `\` matches `\W` and the
only exclusion was a preceding `$`. An escaped `\$` therefore opened a
math span that ran to the next bare `$` and hid the highlighting of
inline code spans in between.

Add `(?<!\\)` to both lookbehinds and cover the cases in the colorize
fixture.

commit_message:
Route git linked-worktree files to the correct window (#290708, #299540)

findWindowOnFile matched windows by simple parent-folder containment of
a file's path. Git linked worktrees store their private per-worktree
files (COMMIT_EDITMSG, rebase-merge/git-rebase-todo, etc.) inside the
*main* worktree's .git/worktrees/<name> directory rather than under the
linked worktree's own folder, so such files always resolved to the main
worktree's window instead of the correct linked-worktree window (e.g.
when core.editor is "code --wait").

Add findWindowOnGitWorktreeFile, checked before the existing
parent-folder matching: it recognizes .git/worktrees/<name> metadata
paths and, by resolving each candidate window's own .git pointer file,
matches against the full worktree directory path rather than just the
trailing <name> segment, so two unrelated repositories that happen to
share a worktree name cannot be confused with one another. Ordinary
repositories (.git as a directory) and non-worktree files are
unaffected and never trigger the new filesystem read.

commit_message:
Fix forked process console forwarding reporting shared references as circular

The JSON.stringify replacer in bootstrap-fork's safeToString pushed every
object into a `seen` array and never removed anything, so a value that is
referenced twice in the console arguments of a forked process (a DAG, not
a cycle) was forwarded to the parent as "[Circular]" after its first
occurrence. For example console.log(shared, { a: shared, b: shared })
arrived as [{"value":1},{"a":"[Circular]","b":"[Circular]"}].

Track only the current ancestor path instead, using the replacer's `this`
(the holder) to drop subtrees that are finished. True cycles are still
reported as "[Circular]". The isObject helper is gone: every object has
to be tracked for the holder check to work, and RegExp/Date were the only
exclusions (a Date is already a string by the time the replacer sees it).

Added an integration test that forks bootstrap-fork with a fixture that
logs a shared reference and a genuine cycle.

not circular. Updated that expectation and added a test for shared

commit_message:
agentHost: publish SDK-native Copilot plugins as plugin customizations

Excluding plugin-provided skills from directory discovery removed them
from session state entirely, since nothing republished them. Project
runtime-installed plugins as top-level PluginCustomization containers
instead, with their agents, skills, rules, hooks and MCP servers as
children, and keep them out of the synthetic session plugin so they are
never registered back with the SDK.

Plugin roots are resolved from the provenance the SDK reports on
discovered files, not from the runtime's installed-plugins cache layout,
which is not part of any SDK contract. A plugin contributing only hooks
or MCP servers therefore still cannot be located.

commit_message:
Preserve collapse state in the SCM Repositories view

The Repositories view re-expanded a repository that has submodules every
time the view became visible, so a collapsed parent repository could not
be kept collapsed.

Two things caused this:

- The tree input was always set with the view state that was read from
  storage once in `renderBody`. That state is only written on
  `onWillSaveState`, so any expand/collapse done in the meantime was
  discarded when the view became visible again. Capture the current view
  state when the view is hidden and use it on the next show instead.
- When the view became visible, all known repositories were re-registered
  through `onDidAddRepository`, and for a repository with a `parentId`
  that unconditionally expanded the parent. Only expand the parent when it
  actually gains its first child repository.

commit_message:
Fix "Upstream already exists" when creating a fork

The GitHub push error handler hardcoded the `upstream` and `origin` remote
names when creating a fork after a permission denied push. When the
repository already had a remote using one of those names - which is the
common case when forking a fork - `git remote rename` failed with
"remote upstream already exists" and the whole fork flow was aborted.

Fall back to a suffixed name (`upstream-1`, `origin-1`, ...) when the
preferred name is already taken. Repositories without such remotes keep
using `upstream`/`origin` exactly as before.

Fixes #160377

margin and, in some consumers, a parent gap:

  preserving its current appearance. Its diff-stat line counts keep
  their own 2px gap, which was never part of this relationship.

This is the first shared-control pilot for the predictable UI
composition proposal, stacked on the authoring guidance in
cherwan/ui-composition-authoring-guidance.

commit_message:
sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization

The V3 new-session onboarding personalizes its 3 prompt options with GitHub
items, falling back to standard options. Telemetry from experiment f716301b
showed 61% of impressions timed out with zero GitHub options, and the existing
events could not measure partial success: `fallbackReason` was only 'none' when
all 3 slots were GitHub, so 2 real issues logged identically to zero.

Telemetry (additive; existing field names and values unchanged):
- promptStrategy gains gitHubOptionCount, candidatesFound, lookupDurationMs,
  per-stage durations and outcomes, and timedOutStage.
- promptOptionInteraction gains optionIndex and optionKindsShown, so per-option
  CTR is computable rather than confounded with availability.
- Both gain a shared impressionId, replacing lossy DevDeviceId joins.
- New 'noComposer' fallback reason splits the infra-bug meaning out of the
  overloaded 'noCandidate'.
- Bounded categories and counts only: no titles, URLs, numbers, repository
  names or prompt text.

Latency, without raising the 10s total budget:
- Publish issue candidates before the linkage lookup, which only filters out
  issues that already have linked pull requests and so must never hide them.
- Keep review-thread enrichment off the critical path; it produced the least
  picked option while being the most expensive stage.
- Rebalance sub-budgets to 4000/1500/3000 so the concurrent chains fit.
- Stream options into the composer: paint the standard options immediately and
  replace slots as lookups land, instead of blocking first paint on the lookup.

INewSessionPromptOptionsController.resolve gains an optional progress callback
that reports whether an update was rendered, so the composer can refuse late
updates while the user is acting on the options and telemetry still describes
what was actually shown.

commit_message:
remote: fix managed resource loading from workbench

Chromium omits referrers for requests originating from the vscode-file
scheme because custom schemes are not registered as allowed referrer
sources. The protocol level referrer check therefore rejected every
legitimate managed remote resource request from the workbench.

webRequest frame tree validation, which rejects requests originating
from vscode-webview frames using browser owned frame identity.

Also return Buffer instances for error responses from the buffer
protocol handler. String response bodies are invalid for
registerBufferProtocol and caused intended HTTP error responses to
surface as net::ERR_FAILED.

commit_message:
Acquire a process lock on the session data directory

The main IPC handle is scoped to the product version, so right after an
update the new process fails to detect the old one via claimInstance and
both processes end up using the same user data directory at the same
time. Chromium does not support sharing session data between multiple
running browser processes and webview service worker registration then
fails with an InvalidStateError.

Add a version independent process lock for the session data:

- createStaticIPCHandle now allows omitting the version so that the same
  handle is produced by all versions for a given user data directory
  (existing callers are unchanged)
- the main process serves that handle (environmentMainService.
  sessionDataLockHandle) for its whole lifetime before any storage in the
  user data directory is opened (claimSessionData runs right after
  claimInstance and before initServices)
- if a live lock holder exists, the process waits for it to exit (polling
  every second, dialog after 10s with Keep Waiting/Exit that re-appears
  every 60s), because concurrent use of the session data directory is
  unsupported and can corrupt Chromium state storage
- stale sockets of dead processes are recovered by probing the handle and
  unlinking it, mirroring claimInstance; the lock is released on shutdown

Signed-off-by: Danila Fominykh <d@m8sh.su>
author: dnch13

commit_message:
Treat ENOENT when probing the session data lock as a released lock

A normal lock release can remove the Unix socket in between the failed
serve() attempt and the connect() probe (and on Windows the named pipe
disappears when its owning process exits). The probe then failed with
ENOENT, which escaped and aborted startup instead of continuing the
polling loop. Treat ENOENT as a released-lock race and retry
acquisition.

The same race applies to the unlink() of a stale socket, which another
process may have removed in the meantime: ignore ENOENT there quietly
instead of logging a warning.

Signed-off-by: Danila Fominykh <d@m8sh.su>

commit_message:
diffEditor: Center the gutter between both editors

The gutter that holds the hunk actions was carved out of the original
editor alone, so the two sides of a side-by-side diff were never the
same width. Both editors now give up half of it.

The edges of the gap are snapped to whole pixels rather than split at
`sashLeft +/- gutterWidth / 2`, so each editor always gets an integer
width and the gap absorbs the leftover pixel. A fractional width would
be floored by `EditorLayoutInfoComputer.computeLayout` and painted at
that size anyway, so it would not keep the editors flush, would wrap one
side a column earlier than the other, and would move the border of the
modified editor off the pixel grid.

`SashLayout.getGutterEdges` is the single definition of that geometry;
the layout and both sashes read it, which keeps the drag handles on the
edges of the gap instead of half a pixel beside them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
author: M393

commit_message:
diffEditor: Keep the minimum editor width on both sides of the gutter

`sashLeft` is clamped so that `MINIMUM_EDITOR_WIDTH` remains beside the
split point, which held while the gutter hung off one side of it. Now
that the gutter straddles the split point, each editor starts half a
gutter further in, leaving both sides 82px instead of 100px at the
limits of a drag.

Clamp in `getGutterEdges` instead, where the gutter width is known, so
the minimum applies to the edges the editors actually get. This also
covers the original editor, which used to drop to 65px at the left limit
because the gutter was taken from that side alone.

commit_message:
fix: merge input state contrib instead of replacing it

chat.customizations.migrationHint: "once" showed the hint on every
request. ChatServiceImpl records that the hint was shown by writing a key
into the input model's `contrib` bag, but ChatInputPart.getCurrentInputState
rebuilds that bag from scratch and lets only widget contributions populate
it. The next input sync - typing, sending, or a model change - therefore
published a contrib object without the flag, and InputModel.setState
replaced the whole bag with it, so "once" degraded into "always".

setState takes a Partial<IChatModelInputState>, so a partial update must
not silently drop nested state it says nothing about. Merge contrib by key
so each writer owns its own keys.

commit_message:
fix: separate PosixShellType.Sh case with POSIX-safe single-quote escaping

POSIX sh does not support ANSI-C $'...' quoting. When a path contains
a single quote, the existing code fell through to the Bash case and
emitted $'...\\'...' which sh rejects.

Fix: give PosixShellType.Sh its own case using close-quote/escaped-quote/
reopen-quote: path.replace(/'/g, "'\\''"). Also tighten collapseTildePath
to check startsWith(home + separator) so /home/user2 is not collapsed when
home is /home/user.

Add regression tests for both cases.

commit_message:
Add non-streaming Responses API handling to mock LLM server

CLI 1.0.84-1 uses the non-streaming Responses transport for resumed
turns: a resumed session restores enableStreaming as false and omits the
`stream` flag from the request, whose wire default is false. The mock LLM
server previously always answered `/responses` with an SSE
text/event-stream, so the runtime rejected the body on resumed turns
("non-streaming Responses body was not valid JSON"), failing the Agent
Host E2E replay suites.

Honor the `stream` flag: when absent or false, emit a single completed
`Response` JSON object via a new sendResponsesNonStreaming() that mirrors
the streaming turn resolution (multi-turn tool-calls, echo-last-message,
echo-last-tool-result, content, and single-turn content). Ported from the
exact-pair reference bump PR (SDK 1.0.13 / CLI 1.0.84-1).

commit_message:
fix: await session state before computing migration hint

The customization migration hint reads migration destinations through
AgentCustomizationItemProvider.provideSourceFolders, which resolves them
from a session-state subscription. IAgentSubscription.value is undefined
until its first snapshot arrives, and the workbench service collapses
that to an empty customization list.

Session-state subscriptions are keyed by chat UI resource. On the first
send of a new chat the untitled resource is materialized into a fresh
real resource, so a new subscription is created at that moment and its
first read yields no customizations. Every migration candidate is then
filtered out and no hint is shown, even though the same computation
reports the correct counts once the snapshot lands.

Add whenCustomizationsReady so one-shot callers can distinguish 'not
loaded yet' from 'no customizations', and await it in provideSourceFolders.
The wait is bounded and cancellable because the chat request path blocks
on the hint before sending the user's message.

commit_message:
fix: share one bounded readiness wait per session subscription

createFileMigration queries provideSourceFolders once per target prompt
type, sequentially, and computeMigrationHint runs categories covering
agent, instructions and skill candidates. With a per-call deadline a
subscription that never hydrates could therefore block the first message
for roughly three deadlines instead of one.

Memoize the wait on the session-state subscription entry so every
source-folder query behind a hint joins the same bounded wait. A new
subscription generation - including the untitled to real rebind that
backs a first send - starts with no memo, so that case still gets a full
wait. Each caller races the shared wait against its own token so one
cancellation cannot settle it for the others.

commit_message:
Add document links for every tsconfig path

`TsconfigLinkProvider` linked three fields: `extends`, `files`, and
`references[].path`. Every other value in a project config that names a
file or a directory was inert, and `extends` only worked in its string
form, so the array form TypeScript 5.0 introduced was silently dropped.

Eighteen contribution rows now cover those three plus `include`,
`exclude`, `compilerOptions.lib`, `types`, `typeRoots`, `rootDir`,
`rootDirs`, `baseUrl`, `outDir`, `declarationDir`, `outFile`,
`tsBuildInfoFile`, `mapRoot`, and `sourceRoot`.

The provider is table-driven rather than a method per field, so a future
field is one row and a future resolution strategy is a row plus a
function. `links.ts` maps JSON paths to link kinds and produces
candidates without touching the file system, which makes it directly
testable. `resolvers.ts` turns a kind and a string into a target URI.
`index.ts` registers the provider and opens what a resolver returns.

Notable behaviors:

- `include` and `exclude` entries are usually globs, so only the literal
  leading segments are underlined and followed: `src/**/*` links `src`.
- Directory targets reveal in the explorer, since an editor cannot open
  a folder.
- `lib` entries resolve against the TypeScript the language service is
  actually using, honoring `typescript.tsdk` and the workspace version
  picker, falling back to the bundled copy.
- A missing target still offers to create the file for the kinds that
  name files, and reports for the kinds that name directories.

`TypeScriptVersionManager` decided which install is active inside its
constructor. That rule moves to an exported function so the `lib`
resolver can ask the same question, rather than reading the manager's
storage key and reimplementing it. The version provider is configured on
first use rather than at activation, because loading the configuration
can shell out synchronously.

Left for later, each one a row plus at most a resolver:
`compilerOptions.paths` values, which resolve against `baseUrl` and need
document context the resolver contract does not carry; `plugins[].name`
and `jsxImportSource`, which are package resolution; `watchOptions`; and
the deprecated `out`.

commit_message:
Fix tsconfig link edge cases found in review

- A glob whose only literal prefix is `.` (`./*.ts`) produced a one-character
  link that revealed the folder the config already lives in. It is no longer
  linked.
- `types` entries and the other path resolvers now classify relative and
  absolute paths the way the compiler does, on every platform: `.`, `..`,
  `.\foo`, `\\server\share` and `C:\foo` are paths, not package names, and
  the check no longer depends on `path.isAbsolute` of the host platform.
- `lib` resolution read `bundledVersion` twice per click. The getter rescans
  disk and shows an error toast before throwing, so a missing bundled install
  produced two identical toasts. It is now read once.
- A directory target outside the workspace was handed to `revealInExplorer`,
  which silently does nothing for it. It is now revealed in the OS file
  manager on desktop, or reported with a message elsewhere.

commit_message:
Configure tsconfig lib links cheaply and describe link kinds in one table

The version provider used by `lib` links was configured lazily on the first
click through the full `loadFromWorkspace()`, which reads every TypeScript
setting and, when `tsserver.nodePath` is "node", synchronously spawns `node`
and may show Node warnings unrelated to the link. It also ran only once, so
with the native preview enabled a later change to `typescript.tsdk` was
ignored until reload.

`loadTsdkFromWorkspace()` now reads just the two tsdk settings, which is all
the provider consumes, and is cheap enough to run at activation and again
whenever those settings change.

Each link kind's resolver, failure wording, and missing-target policy were
spread over a resolver record and two switches. They now live in one
descriptor record, so adding a kind is one entry rather than three places,
and no kind inherits wording from a `default` arm.

commit_message:
Resolve tsconfig lib links through the install's lib map, and open them on web

A `lib` entry was mapped straight to `lib.<name>.d.ts`, but TypeScript
resolves it through its `libMap`, where aliases such as `ES7` or
`ESNext.BigInt` point at the file of the edition that shipped the feature.
Those entries compiled fine yet reported "Failed to resolve TypeScript lib".

The resolver now consults the lib map of each candidate install and nothing
else, so an entry the map does not know is not a lib, however plausible the
file name would look. On desktop the map is read from the `typescript.js`
beside the install's `tsserver.js`, cached per install, and an install inside
the workspace is only loaded once the workspace is trusted, the same rule
tsserver follows. On web the bundle step writes `libMap.json` next to the lib
files it already copies, from the same TypeScript, so the two never drift.

On web the lib files are served over http(s), where the workbench's fetch
provider answers every `stat` with a file and `vscode.open` hands the URL to
the browser, which offered to download it. Existence is now checked with a
real read, and http(s) targets open as text documents.

commit_message:
Fix tsconfig link issues found in review

Link ranges are now mapped through the source text a value was decoded from,
so a narrowed link inside an escaped value points at the characters it names
instead of being dropped, and a string whose closing quote has not been typed
yet is no longer underlined one character short. Glob prefixes accept either
separator, the way the compiler normalizes them.

A path written with Windows separators now resolves the same on every
platform: values pass through `normalizeSlashes` before reaching a URI, since
`Uri.file` and `Uri.joinPath` only treat a backslash as a separator on
Windows. `looksLikeRelativePath` and `looksLikeAbsolutePath` move beside the
other path predicates in `utils/fs`, along with a shared `tryStat`.

A `lib` entry now resolves through the file the install ships whenever one is
named for it, which is all but the aliases, so the common case no longer loads
the install's compiler on the extension host thread. Only a value shaped like
a lib name is looked up that way, so a value carrying a separator cannot point
the link out of the install. The map read that the aliases still need caches
failures too, keys the cache by the modification time of the `typescript.js`
it read, so an install replaced in place is picked up, and drops the module
again once the map is taken from it. An install the service could not read is
skipped, matching the fallback `TypeScriptVersionManager.reset` performs.

On web, a lib file is no longer downloaded once to prove it exists and again
to show it: the lib map already says the file ships with that install. A
folder outside the workspace reports rather than calling `revealFileInOS` in a
remote window, where that command does nothing.

commit_message:
Guard navigator.clipboard in the WebKit clipboard workaround

installWebKitWriteTextWorkaround() called navigator.clipboard.write() without
checking that the async clipboard API exists. Outside a secure context it does
not, and since the handler is bound to click and keydown on every container,
Safari throws on every click and keystroke.

Worse, the handler assigns webKitPendingClipboardWritePromise before the
throwing line, so writeText() takes its early exit and never reaches
fallbackWriteText() - copying silently does nothing although the execCommand
fallback would work.

Reading the clipboard once and returning early when it is absent leaves that
promise untouched, so writeText() falls through to the fallback as intended.
Every other clipboard access in this file is already guarded.

commit_message:
Fix primary side bar width reset when toggled (#334167)

`SplitView.onViewChange` redistributed the size a view gained or gave up in
plain index order, unlike `resizeView` which is layout priority aware. With
Modern UI and the primary side bar on the right, the activity bar changes its
fixed width with side bar visibility and reports that change re-entrantly from
`Part.setVisible`, while `setViewVisible` is still restoring the side bar to
its cached size. Index order made the side bar the first candidate, so it was
squeezed to its minimum width on every toggle. On the left the flexible editor
happened to come first, which is why only the right side showed the bug.

Redistribute by layout priority instead, so the high priority editor absorbs
the change.

commit_message:
Keep all repositories visible when a new one is discovered first

When a repository is not part of the previous session state,
`SCMViewService.onDidAddRepository` selects all repositories, but it keeps
`previousState` in effect. A repository that is discovered afterwards, and that
was visible in the previous session, then takes the "First visible repository"
branch, clears the selection of every repository added so far and ends up being
the only visible repository.

The result depends on the order in which repositories are discovered, and the
bad selection is written back to `scm:view:visibleRepositories`, so it survives
subsequent restarts.

Clear `previousState` once we have decided to select all repositories, so that
the rest of the load is no longer influenced by it.

Fixes #334842

commit_message:
[cherry-pick] Managed settings: reuse cached policy more often (#333704)

managed settings: reuse cached policy on reload instead of refetching

When forceRemoteSettingsRefresh is not effective, a fresh cached
managed-settings response now satisfies startup without a network
round-trip, matching the sibling entitlements/token/MCP fetches which
only refetch once the cache goes stale. Previously a per-process gate
(hasFetchedThisProcess) forced one /managed_settings request on every
reload even with a fresh cache and no policy requirement, which for a
user without an enterprise policy fanned out into one 404 per GitHub
session.

Cache reuse is scoped: a cached response is only reused when it was
captured for the current account, authentication provider, and endpoint
(a legacy cache with no recorded scope is trusted), so a previous GitHub
Enterprise host's policy is not applied after switching scopes.

An outstanding client_update_required compatibility error is never
served from cache: it is revalidated on the next refresh so the
fail-closed block clears once the client or server recovers, instead of
lingering for the full cache lifetime.

The fail-closed path is otherwise unchanged: when the control is
effective, only a fresh successful response for the current account,
provider, and endpoint clears the requirement.

commit_message:
Seed new chat-input sessions from the remembered session-config picks

The Agents window and the chat input seed a new session's config from two
different places. The Agents window replays the user's last picks from profile
storage; the chat input reads only `chat.defaultConfiguration`, which covers the
`autoApprove` and `mode` axes and nothing else.

Any other property therefore falls back to its schema default in the chat input
however many times the user changes it. Claude's `permissionMode` is the visible
case: the Approvals chip reads that property, `chat.defaultConfiguration` does
not write it, so every new chat starts on Default while the Agents window keeps
whatever was last chosen.

Move the storage key and the remembered-key predicate into
`sessionConfigKeys.ts` so both surfaces share one definition rather than a copy,
and seed the chat input's initial config from the same store. Isolation is
spread last so it stays host-owned, and the existing `chat.defaultConfiguration`
handling is left in place, so the two axes it already governs keep their current
precedence in this path.

commit_message:
Fix backspace over a flag emoji leaving a dangling regional indicator

getLeftDeleteOffset()/getOffsetBeforeLastEmojiComponent() already treat an
emoji modifier sequence (e.g. a skin-tone-modified emoji) as a single unit
for backspace, per the fix for #99629. Flag emoji were not covered by that
special-casing: a flag is two Regional Indicator Symbol code points (e.g.
US = U+1F1FA U+1F1F8), and backspacing over one deleted only the trailing
code point, leaving a dangling, meaningless lone Regional Indicator behind
(fixable only with a second backspace) — the exact class of bug #99629 was
meant to prevent, just for a different emoji construct.

Per Unicode UAX #29 rules GB12/GB13, Regional Indicators combine greedily
in pairs from the start of a maximal run of consecutive indicators, so a
run's length parity determines whether its last indicator is paired. Added
isRegionalIndicator()/isRegionalIndicatorPaired() and used them so a
complete flag pair is deleted together, while a genuinely unpaired
trailing indicator (odd run length) is still deleted alone.

Fixes #334807.

Verified by importing the real, unmodified strings.ts directly (via tsx,
no transpilation of the algorithm by hand) and simulating repeated
backspace over several emoji constructs before and after the fix:
- Skin-tone modifier sequence: unaffected, still one unit (regression check).
- ZWJ family emoji: unaffected, still peeled component-by-component to
  match Firefox's behavior per the discussion in #99629 (regression check).
- Single flag: now one backspace instead of two, no dangling indicator.
- Two adjacent flags: now one flag per backspace instead of leaving a
  dangling indicator after each of the first three presses.
- A flag followed by a lone unpaired indicator: the lone indicator is
  still deleted alone, then the completed flag as a unit (no dangling step).

Also ran the existing src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.ts file (54
tests, all passing) via a minimal suite/test shim under tsx, since a full
`npm install` + Electron test run was impractical in this environment —
this exercises the real, unmodified test file end-to-end, just outside
the standard mocha/Electron runner, so a maintainer re-running it via
`./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.js` is the
recommended final check before merge.

commit_message:
Keep every pending steering message instead of only the last

`ChatState` models the two pending-message kinds inconsistently:
`steeringMessage` is a single slot while `queuedMessages` is a list. The
`chat/pendingMessageSet` reducer reflects that, overwriting any existing
steering message with no id check, three lines above a queued branch that
correctly finds by id and appends.

Sending a second steering message therefore evicts the first from state. The
message itself is not lost, because the agent was already handed it, so it
still lands in the transcript when the model consumes it. What is lost is its
pending bubble, which disappears from the sidebar the moment the next steering
message is sent and reappears later when the turn picks it up. Nothing in the
UI required this: the pending-request projection already builds a list carrying
a kind per entry, and it pushed at most one steering entry only because the
state could hold at most one.

Make `steeringMessages` a list and mirror the queued branch in the three
reducer sites, the state aggregation, the pending-request reconciliation and
the projection. The provider hook becomes
`setPendingMessages(chat, steeringMessages, queuedMessages)`, and Claude,
Copilot and Codex each loop rather than handling a single optional message.
author: RyanEwen

commit_message:
Report chat activity for the window before a turn produces content

AHP already has a progress channel and the workbench already renders it well:
`chat/activityChanged` carries a human-readable string, and the client turns it
into a shimmering row with a stable id, so each update replaces the previous one.

Nothing produced it for Claude sessions. The only producer anywhere in the host
is worktree creation, which is why "Creating isolated worktree" is the only
activity a user ever sees. Every other turn reports no liveness, so a session
waiting on CLI or MCP startup is indistinguishable on screen from a hung one.

Report it from `ClaudeAgent` rather than `ClaudeAgentSession`, because the
window worth covering is materialization itself, and the session does not exist
until that has finished. `sendMessage` sets the label before queueing, so the
row is up during startup rather than after it.

The row renders only while the turn has produced no response parts, so there is
no useful per-tool label to add: `ChatToolCallStart` appends a response part,
which is exactly the condition that hides the row. Activity is therefore a
pre-content indicator and nothing more.

Cleared on every exit: turn completion and errors arrive as pipeline signals
through the entry forwarder, cancellation is cleared in `_abortSession` because
`AgentSideEffects` dispatches `ChatTurnCancelled` without going through the
pipeline, and a preflight failure is cleared from the send promise. Labels are
deduplicated per chat, so an unchanged one is not re-sent.

commit_message:
chat: mount MCP App webview in the window it is rendered in

`ChatMcpAppModel` mounted its webview from the constructor, at which point
the container element is still detached: `ChatMcpAppSubPart` builds
`div.mcp-app-part` with `dom.$` and creates the model before that node is
inserted into the tree. `dom.getWindow` therefore resolved to the main
window, so `WebviewElement.mountTo` took the wrong `vscodeWindowId`, hashed
the wrong parent origin, and registered the `message` handler on the main
window. When the chat is in an auxiliary window the MessagePort handshake
never completed and the queued `content` message carrying the app HTML was
never delivered, leaving the card blank.

Defer the mount by a microtask. Both callers append the container
synchronously in the same task (`chatListRenderer` renders a content part
and appends it in one pass; `chatToolInvocationPart` replaces the app node
in the same autorun), so by the time the microtask runs the container is
attached and `getWindow` reports the window the webview really lives in.
`WebviewElement` queues sends while it is initializing, which is what makes
the existing `reinitializeAfterDismount` path work today, so nothing is
lost by mounting one microtask later.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#331140
Refs https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331140

commit_message:
sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization

The V3 new-session onboarding personalizes its 3 prompt options with GitHub
items, falling back to standard options. Telemetry from experiment f716301b
showed 61% of impressions timed out with zero GitHub options, and the existing
events could not measure partial success: `fallbackReason` was only 'none' when
all 3 slots were GitHub, so 2 real issues logged identically to zero.

Telemetry (additive; existing field names and values unchanged):
- promptStrategy gains gitHubOptionCount, candidatesFound, lookupDurationMs,
  per-stage durations and outcomes, and timedOutStage.
- promptOptionInteraction gains optionIndex and optionKindsShown, so per-option
  CTR is computable rather than confounded with availability.
- Both gain a shared impressionId, replacing lossy DevDeviceId joins.
- New 'noComposer' fallback reason splits the infra-bug meaning out of the
  overloaded 'noCandidate'.
- Bounded categories and counts only: no titles, URLs, numbers, repository
  names or prompt text.

Latency, without raising the 10s total budget:
- Publish issue candidates before the linkage lookup, which only filters out
  issues that already have linked pull requests and so must never hide them.
- Keep review-thread enrichment off the critical path; it produced the least
  picked option while being the most expensive stage.
- Rebalance sub-budgets to 4000/1500/3000 so the concurrent chains fit.
- Stream options into the composer: paint the standard options immediately and
  replace slots as lookups land, instead of blocking first paint on the lookup.

INewSessionPromptOptionsController.resolve gains an optional progress callback
that reports whether an update was rendered, so the composer can refuse late
updates while the user is acting on the options and telemetry still describes
what was actually shown.

commit_message:
Fix C/C++ auto-indent after brace-less if/for/while/else (#43244)

JS, TS, and PHP already indent the next line after a brace-less
if/for/while/else via `indentNextLinePattern`, but the cpp language
configuration (shared by c, cpp, and cuda-cpp) never got the same
pattern added, so typing:

    if (condition)
    <Enter>

does not indent the following line in C/C++, unlike other C-family
languages in the editor. The matching outdent-after-single-statement
onEnterRule was already present in this file; only the pattern that
triggers the initial indent was missing.

This adds the same `indentNextLinePattern` already shipped for
JS/TS/PHP so C/C++ gets consistent behavior.

Fixes #43244

commit_message:
terminal: do not buffer pty host events that have no IPC client

`ProxyChannel.fromService` eagerly creates an `Event.buffer` for every event of the
service, and such a buffer only drains once a client calls `listen`. The window consumes
every `IPtyService` event over a direct message port to the pty host
(`TerminalIpcChannels.PtyHostWindow`), never over the localPty channel, so these buffers
never drained: the main process archived every chunk of terminal output for the lifetime
of the session. Reported at 1,150,631 events / 602 MB, ending in a V8 OOM that closes
every window at once, with no warning and no reload prompt.

Mark them unbuffered. The five `IPtyHostController` events stay buffered, those do have a
client on this channel.

Fixes #328885

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
author: DanielGarzaB

commit_message:
terminal: keep the list of unbuffered local pty events exhaustive

The local pty channel opted the `IPtyService` events out of buffering by name, and nothing
checked that list against the service: an event added to `IPtyService` later would have
been buffered again in the main process for a client that never comes, which is exactly
how #328885 came to be.

Move the list next to the interface as `ptyServiceEvents`, derived from an object that
`satisfies Record<..., true>` so that a missing or an extra name does not compile, and add
a test that reflects over a `PtyHostService` instance the way `ProxyChannel.fromService`
does, so an `on*` property the class gains outside the interface has to be classified too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
author: DanielGarzaB

commit_message:
terminal: test the local pty channel itself, not only its list of events

The guardian of the previous commit checks that every event of `PtyHostService` is
classified, but nothing exercised the channel: dropping `unbufferedEvents` from the
registration in app.ts kept every test green while the leak came back.

Move the registration into `createLocalPtyChannel`, next to the service, so that a test
can build the channel production builds and assert that none of the `IPtyService` events
has a listener before a client asks for one, and that a client who does ask gets live
events without a backlog.

commit_message:
Scope MCP tool availability to referenced servers only

When the user references an MCP server in ask mode, the toolReferences
in the request are a snapshot taken when the request was parsed. If the
MCP server is still discovering its tools at that point, the snapshot
contains only the tools registered so far, and tools discovered later
are reported as "disabled by the user" when the model tries to call
them.

Include all currently registered tools of the *referenced* MCP server
(identified via LanguageModelToolMCPSource) rather than all MCP tools,
so availability reflects the live registration state without widening
the scope to MCP servers the user never referenced.

Fixes #334569

commit_message:
Refactor Playwright chat input helper script to use a centralized configuration object for timeouts and retry limits

## Overview
The Playwright CLI chat input helper script currently relies on hardcoded magic numbers for polling intervals, visibility attempts, palette timeouts, and wait limits. This makes it rigid when adapting to different test environment latencies.

## Proposed Solution
Introduce a centralized `CONFIG` object at the top of the script to manage timing parameters cleanly:
- `pollIntervalMs`
- `maxVisibleAttempts`
- `paletteTimeoutMs`
- `maxPaletteWaitAttempts`

## Benefits
- Eliminates hardcoded magic numbers.
- Improves code maintainability and test reliability tuning.

commit_message:
agentHost: key Claude trace anchor lookups by chat resource

The per-turn rotation check in ClaudeAgentSession.send looked up the
session anchor under the send's `resource` argument, which is the
session-wide configuration scope. Materialize, the rematerializer, and
release all key the anchor by the chat's own persistence resource. The
two coincide for a session's default chat but differ for peer and side
chats, so a peer chat's first send found the owning session's anchor,
misread it as a rotation, rebuilt the subprocess, and repeated that on
every later send while the exported parent alternated.

Capture the anchor key at materialize and route both the rotation check
and the rematerializer through one lookup helper so they cannot disagree.
Add a peer-chat regression test with a per-key OTel stub, document the
keying contract, and describe the replay ordering guarantees per mode:
serialized through one forwarder in DB mode, unordered in pass-through.

commit_message:
Update jschardet to v4

Upgrade jschardet from 3.1.4 to 4.0.0-rc.3, the published npm release.
This is an RFC to gauge interest in the upgrade.

Main improvements over 3.1.4:

    Metric                     jschardet 3.1.4   jschardet 4.0.0
    Accuracy (3,138 files)     43.1%             99.4%
    Speed                      126 files/s       780 files/s
    Language detection         —                 93.4%
    Peak memory                831.8 MiB         85.5 MiB
    Supported encodings        ~30               86
    MIME type detection        no                yes
    License                    LGPL-2.1+         0BSD

The trade-offs: the minified bundle grows from ~334 to ~1,141 KiB
(691 KiB gzipped) and cold start from ~30 to ~109 ms.

Detection changes (encoding.ts):
- jschardet >= 4 accepts a Uint8Array directly, in Node and the browser
  alike, so the manual latin1 round-trip (encodeLatin1) is no longer
  needed and is removed.
- Map jschardet's cp932/cp949 outputs onto iconv-lite's shiftjis/euckr.
- Widen the local `guessed` type to `{ encoding: string | null }` to match
  v4's detect() return type (its `encoding` is `string | null`).

Test fixtures:
- Change some.shiftjis.1.txt's trailing text (こんにちは -> 日本語)
  because v4 now detects the old sample as Shift-JIS even without
  candidate encodings, making the test vacuous; the new sample is
  Windows-1252 on its own and Shift-JIS with candidates, restoring the
  contrast.
- Correct some.shiftjis.1.txt's in-memory copy in files.ts: the
  Shift-JIS lead byte 0x82 had been written as the decimal literal 82
  (0x52), so the bytes never matched the on-disk file. v4 declines to
  guess the garbage, which v3 happened to tolerate.

commit_message:
Spare a background subagent's in-flight tool call from the turn-end wipe

`clearPending` drops all cross-message tool attribution on every `result`
envelope. A background subagent outlives the turn that spawned it, so its
inner tool call is still in flight and its result is still coming, but its
entry is wiped along with the genuinely orphaned ones.

When that result arrives the tool name and input are gone, so the call
renders with a generic past-tense label and live diverges from replay.

`drainForegroundSpawns`, called on the same envelope two lines later,
already spares background spawns for exactly this reason.
author: RyanEwen

commit_message:
Fix terminal prompt duplication when resizing the terminal panel

The terminal resize debouncer sent a PTY resize on every layout event even
when the grid dimensions did not change, triggering SIGWINCH storms that
made shells redraw the prompt repeatedly. Additionally, the horizontal
resize debounce was too short (100ms) for shells such as zsh to finish
their prompt redraw, so consecutive resizes were processed with a stale
terminal width and duplicated the prompt line.

Skip resizes whose dimensions are unchanged and debounce horizontal
resizes for 300ms instead of 100ms.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#329946

commit_message:
Fix dictation hangs by adding timeouts to Foundry Local native calls

The on-device (nemo/Foundry Local) dictation backend awaited several
native SDK calls with no timeout and no AbortSignal: the model catalog
lookup, model.load(), session.start(), each session.append() call
(chained serially so one stuck append blocks every later chunk and
stop()), the result stream's next(), and session.stop()/dispose().

If any of these stalls (proxy/firewall silently dropping packets, a
wedged native addon, a driver hiccup during model load), the awaiting
promise never settles. Since start()/pushAudio()/stop()/cancel() all
await these calls directly or transitively, dictation would hang
indefinitely with no error surfaced to the user and no way to recover
short of restarting VS Code.

Guard each of these awaits with a hard timeout that rejects with a
descriptive error, mirroring the existing inactivity-timeout pattern
already used for the native runtime tarball download. A timeout now
surfaces as a normal model/session Error (with a new 'timeout' error
code from classifyModelError) so the existing error-handling UI path
picks it up, and Stop/Cancel can no longer hang forever.

commit_message:
Add ROS2 toolkit, New-Project wizard and node graph view (REQ-3/4/5)

Three requirement slices plus the fixes from a multi-agent review of them.

REQ-3 - RoboAgent ROS2 Toolkit (extensions/roboagent-ros2/):
colcon build/test/clean task provider with a $colcon problem matcher,
ros2 run/debug commands, debug adapters (debugpy for Python, detected
lldb-dap for C++ with a terminal fallback), a Get-started walkthrough, and
the generic CMake/single-file build-run ported from the retired
roboagent-defaults extension. Fork surfaces that an extension cannot own -
the ROS2 status bar and the Package-Explorer context menu - live in
contrib/roboagent and invoke these commands.

REQ-4 - New-Project wizard: a stepped picker (control level, then domain or
MCU target, then environment) that scaffolds a starter, records
.roboagent/project.json, and opens the folder. Both the high-level domains
and the low-level targets are data-driven catalogs, so adding either is a
data edit.

REQ-5 - ROS2 Node Graph: renders the Workspace Knowledge Graph as an
interactive bipartite node/topic graph in an editor pane. Deterministic
layered layout (cycle-safe, barycenter ordering) lives in a pure,
unit-tested module; the pane adds pan/zoom, click-to-highlight, hovers,
live re-render on re-index and an empty state.

Review fixes folded in, notably: findColconRoot no longer walks above the
workspace and returns undefined outside a colcon workspace, so Colcon Clean
can no longer rm -rf in an unrelated project (it now also confirms first);
colcon test dropped an invalid --symlink-install; ros2 run/launch terminals
source the distro and workspace overlay; the status bar learns an
onDidChangeIndexing event so its spinner is reachable; debugpy's PYTHONPATH
points at the package parent; and user-facing strings are localized.

Verified: hygiene, fork and extension type-checks, 30 unit tests, and an
end-to-end pass over a fixture workspace in the running app.

commit_message:
Copy the image when using Copy in a webview context menu

Fixes #292567

The webview `Copy` context menu item runs `document.execCommand('copy')`
inside the webview's iframe, which only copies the text selection. Right
clicking an image does not create a selection, so nothing was copied
unless the user selected the image first.

Track the element the context menu was opened on. When `Copy` runs with
an empty selection and that element is an image, encode it as a png and
write it to the clipboard instead. Images from a genuinely opaque cross
origin response taint the canvas, so fall back to re-requesting them in
cors mode via `createImageBitmap`.

The tracked image is cleared on the next click or keypress so that a
later keyboard copy still acts on the selection.

commit_message:
Add `editor.textDirection` to lay out editor contents right-to-left

VS Code can be localized into right-to-left languages, but the editor has no way
to lay out its contents right-to-left. The direction of a line is inferred per
line, so a file written in Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu renders as a stack of
independently-resolved paragraphs: the caret starts on the wrong side, a line
beginning with an identifier or a symbol flips to left-to-right, and line numbers
and glyph margin stay on the left of text that reads from the right.

Add `editor.textDirection: 'auto' | 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'uiLanguage'`:

- `auto` (default) is exactly today's behaviour: a line takes the direction its
  decorations declare, and every other line is laid out left-to-right.
- `rtl` lays out every line right-to-left and mirrors the editor's own chrome -
  line numbers and glyph margin to the right, minimap to the left, overview ruler
  on the content edge. The vertical scrollbar stays on the physical right of the
  content, because the lines already inset their leading edge by its width.
- `uiLanguage` resolves to `rtl` when the user interface is itself displayed in a
  right-to-left language. It is opt-in rather than the default: most people who
  localize the interface still write Latin identifiers, and flipping their editor
  without being asked is not a behaviour change to make silently.

The setting is language-overridable, which is the scope it usually wants -
direction is a property of what a file contains, not of the window.

The internal coordinate system is unchanged: the editor still measures from a
physical left origin, and the mirrored layout is applied by the view parts and by
CSS guarded on the `text-direction-rtl` class that `EditorClassName` contributes.
`EffectiveTextDirection` resolves the setting once. Lines whose direction is
declared by a decoration are resolved exactly as before, ties included.

`editorLayoutProvider.test.ts` is extended for the mirrored layout. The one-line
change in `monaco.d.ts` beyond the new option is regenerator output: adding an
option shifts how TypeScript prints an unrelated union, and `gulp` fails the build
if the checked-in file does not match.
author: SalehKadah

commit_message:
Fix the right-to-left geometry and per-line direction found in review

Thirteen findings from the review, all of them real. Grouped by what they were:

**One physical origin.** A right-to-left layout puts the minimap at `[0, minimapWidth]`, the
content next to it, and the margin strip flush with the right edge. `HitTestContext` already
measured from `minimapWidth`; `getMouseColumn` (used by `MouseHandler` when dragging outside
the editor) still measured from `contentLeft`, and content widgets added a scrollbar width
that is not there. Both now use the same origin.

**The margin strip is mirrored inside, not only moved.** Its offsets were computed
left-to-right and the strip translated as a whole, which left the glyph margin against the
text and folding at the outer edge. Reading outwards from the text, a right-to-left editor
wants decorations, then line numbers, then the glyph margin: the offsets are reversed in
`EditorLayoutInfoComputer` and the margin hit-test range takes the smaller of the two ends.
`editorLayoutProvider.test.ts` now asserts the mirroring instead of asserting that the two
layouts are identical.

**Rulers measure from where the text starts.** A right-to-left line reserves the vertical
scrollbar with `padding-right` (`ViewLine#renderLine`), so its text begins one scrollbar
width short of `scrollWidth`. Rulers were drawn from `scrollWidth`, i.e. behind the bar.

**Decorations still win, per line.** Indent guides and sticky lines took the direction from
the editor's layout, overriding a line whose decoration declares the other direction - the
precedence this PR is careful about everywhere else. Guides now read
`viewModel.getTextDirection(lineNumber)`, and each sticky line carries its own `dir`
attribute in place of one global CSS `direction`.

**Switching direction leaves nothing behind.** Overlay widgets set `left` in one direction
and `right` in the other without clearing the opposite inset, so the stale one won after a
switch back. `ViewLayout` anchors an unowned viewport to the right while right-to-left; it
now releases that anchor when the layout returns to left-to-right, instead of leaving the
editor parked past the end of its lines.

**A script subtag decides direction.** `uiLanguage` reduced the locale to its primary
subtag, which makes `sd-Deva` right-to-left and `az-Arab` left-to-right - both backwards.
An explicit script subtag is now honoured first.

**The toggle command.** From the Command Palette focus is in quick input, so
`getFocusedCodeEditor()` is null and the command wrote a global value instead of the
language override it promises; it falls back to the active editor and says so when there is
none. It no longer forces `ConfigurationTarget.USER`, which silently did nothing when a
workspace value was in effect, and passes the model resource so folder-scoped values
resolve. The screen-reader announcement no longer claims `auto` means left-to-right.
author: SalehKadah

commit_message:
Make the toggle per file, and finish mirroring what the editor draws

Two things a review of the previous commit made clear.

The toggle wrote to settings, and `updateValue` without a target writes to the scope the
effective value comes from - a workspace folder first. A repository with a checked-in
`.vscode/settings.json` would get an edit in `git status` because somebody flipped the
direction of the file in front of them. The scope was wrong too: an English README and an
Arabic guide are both Markdown, and a per-language setting cannot tell them apart.

`toggleWordWrap` already solved exactly this, so this follows it: transient per-model
state, a `textDirectionOverride` editor option carrying it into `EffectiveTextDirection`,
a three-value cycle that does not discard an explicit `ltr`, and an entry in the View
menu, which is the only surface anybody would have found this on. The command moves to
`workbench/contrib/codeEditor` with its siblings and no longer writes settings at all.

The rest is layout that was mirrored halfway:

- `_hitTestMargin` walked the strip's children in a fixed order while the previous commit
  mirrored their offsets, so in a mirrored layout every gutter click resolved to the glyph
  margin: clicking a line number toggled a breakpoint instead of selecting the line, and
  folding by click did nothing. It now walks them in the order their offsets give.
- The drag-select boundaries were still `contentLeft` and `minimapLeft`, so the last stretch
  of real content counted as outside the editor.
- The minimap moved but painted each line from the left, showing the file's shape reversed
  against the text. Its canvases are flipped.
- Peek and inline chat were placed as if the minimap were on the right.
- The overview ruler was mirrored in the previous commit; that was wrong. It annotates the
  vertical scrollbar, which deliberately does not move, so it stays with it.
- Sticky lines were `verticalScrollbarWidth` narrower than the gutter they sit above, and
  were given a `dir` attribute where they previously had none - a change to the default
  path, which this restores.
- The GPU renderer's fallback, the scroll shadow, block decorations, the current-line seam
  and the collapsed folding chevron each still assumed the left-to-right arrangement.

`isRtlLanguage` also honours a script subtag now, `minimap.side` says in its description
that a mirrored layout does not honour it, and the setting's own descriptions no longer
imply a difference between `auto` and `ltr`: nothing here infers direction from content,
so the two resolve alike, and saying otherwise in the Settings UI would be a lasting lie.
author: SalehKadah

commit_message:
Anchor content widgets to the text, not to the content box, in a mirrored layout

A right-to-left line is inset from the right edge of the content box by the width the
vertical scrollbar reserves - `ViewLine#renderLine` writes that `padding-right`, and it
predates this PR. The visible ranges a content widget's anchor is derived from are
measured inside that inset box, so converting an anchor to a page coordinate has to add
the inset back. It was not being added: the origin was the content box's left edge.

Every content widget therefore sat one scrollbar width away from what it was anchored to.
It is most visible on the suggest widget, which is supposed to touch the caret: measured
in a running editor, its right edge landed at 955 while the caret was at 969.

Measured again with the inset restored: 969 and 969.

Found by the live layout suite, which measures a real window over CDP rather than a
computed layout - no unit test covers the anchor-to-page conversion, and `compile-client`
and the editor suite are both clean either way.

commit_message:
Agent Host: stop the reconnecting banner nagging on a flapping transport

A tunnel relay that drops and restores the transport every few seconds made the
banner appear on a session that worked fine throughout. Two causes.

The outage start time lived in a cached derived. While the host is connected
nothing reads the reconnecting state, so that derived lost its observers while
its cache survived them; the next outage on the same session inherited the
previous outage's start time and showed the banner immediately. It is now an
explicit value maintained by an autorun, which runs whether or not anything is
rendering the reconnecting state.

The delay before the banner appears was also shorter than a routine self-healed
reconnect. Such a reconnect preserves session state and the user would not
otherwise notice it, so the threshold now outlasts one.

commit_message:
Fix RemotePty.resize dropping the last resize of an A-B-A sequence

RemotePty.resize compared the requested size against _lastDimensions
synchronously but only updated _lastDimensions inside the start
barrier's then(), one microtask later. When a terminal was resized
A -> B -> A within one turn, the final A was dropped as a duplicate and
the pty was left at B.

This happens every time a hidden maximized panel is shown:
setPanelHidden(false) lays the terminal out at the restored size and
immediately re-maximizes it in the same task, so remote terminals
(Remote-SSH, Dev Containers) end up with a pty at the restored height
while xterm.js is at the maximized height, and TUIs such as tmux paint
only the top half. The next hide/show flips the phase and repairs it.
LocalPty already updates _lastDimensions synchronously, which is why
the symptom is remote-only.

Update _lastDimensions synchronously, mirroring LocalPty, and add a
regression test.

Refs #325743, #239310

commit_message:
agent host: stop chat queues from wedging on a non-settling SDK RPC

All chat operations for one chat serialize on a single per-chat sequencer. A control-plane RPC in that
queue had no timeout, so an RPC that never settled kept the queue head forever. Every later send,
model change, and abort stayed queued and never ran. The client showed a turn that stayed active with
no response and no error. Abort shared the same queue, so Cancel could not recover the chat.

- Bounds the short SDK control-plane RPCs at 30 seconds through a new `_awaitControlPlaneRpc` helper.
  This covers `session.setModel`, `rpc.agent.select`, `rpc.agent.deselect`, and `rpc.history.truncate`.
  A timeout now rejects the operation and lets the queue continue. Turn delivery through `session.send`
  stays unbounded, because a turn can correctly run for a long time.
- Removes abort from the per-chat queue. Abort must interrupt a blocked queue, so it cannot wait behind
  the task it must cancel.
- Adds an operation name to each `_queueChat` call and logs a warning if a queue task runs for more than
  60 seconds. The warning names the operation that holds the queue.
- Adds regression tests for the timeout, for a queued send that continues after a timeout, and for an
  abort that completes while a queue task is blocked.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334159

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

commit_message:
agent host: address review feedback on the chat queue wedge fix

Three follow-ups from review of the queue-wedge fix:

Taking abort off the chat queue meant an abort arriving while a chat was
still materializing found no target and silently succeeded, so a Cancel
during that window was lost and the queued send still dispatched. Aborts
with no live session now record a pending intent (only while work is
actually queued for that chat), and the send honours and clears it before
dispatching.

Timing out a control-plane RPC abandons the await but cannot cancel the
in-flight request, so the SDK's model/agent/history state may no longer
match what the session believes it applied. A timed-out session is now
marked for resync and the next send discards and resumes it, so a
late-settling request cannot mutate state a later operation depends on.

The stall warning wrapped the whole sendMessage task, including the
intentionally unbounded provider call, so any turn over 60s was reported
as a stalled queue. Tasks now cancel the warning when they reach a
legitimately unbounded phase, leaving it to cover only bounded setup and
control-plane work.

commit_message:
Keep MCP App CSP domain lists to network origins

An MCP App's `csp` block carries four domain lists that widen the policy
its frame runs under. The MCP Apps schema documents each of them as
origins: `connectDomains` as "origins for network requests", and likewise
for `resourceDomains`, `frameDomains` and `baseUriDomains`. The values
were passed through with HTML special characters escaped and nothing else,
so an entry naming a privileged application scheme reached the emitted
policy and granted the frame reach the sandbox exists to withhold.

Keep the entries that are network origins. This enforces what the schema
already says these fields hold rather than adding a rule of its own; the
existing escaping is unchanged and still does its job.

An offending entry is dropped on its own rather than the list being
refused, so one bad value does not cost an app the rest of its policy.

A source with no scheme is a host source and is left alone. A port is not
mistaken for a scheme, which matters because a host is a valid scheme
spelling: `example.com:443` is a host and a port, not a scheme source. A
scheme source is either `scheme:` on its own or followed by `//`.

commit_message:
Bind MCP protected-resource metadata to the server that advertised it

A pending MCP authentication request is matched to an arriving token by
its `resource` value, so `resource` is what decides where a token goes.
`_protectedResourceFromMcpAuthRequest` took that value from the metadata
the MCP server supplied, checked only that the JSON had the right shape,
and used it as given. A server could therefore advertise a resource
belonging to somewhere else and have the token approved for that resource
handed to it instead.

`fetchPrm` in `base/common/oauth.ts` already refuses metadata whose
`resource` does not identify the URL it was fetched for, citing RFC 9728.
This path had no equivalent check. Add one.

The rule is origin plus URL prefix, not equality. Equality would be wrong
here: a server at `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp` legitimately advertises
`https://mcp.slack.com` as its resource, which the existing tests cover.
The prefix is compared by path segment, so `https://example.com/mcp` does
not cover `https://example.com/mcpx`.

Metadata that fails the check is dropped rather than rejected outright,
and the request falls back to the identity derived from the server's own
URL, so the server can still authenticate as itself.

commit_message:
Keep MACHINE target storage keys out of applied profile content

Writing out a profile's global state only emits `StorageTarget.USER`
values, so a key held at `StorageTarget.MACHINE` is never something a
profile produced. Applying profile content did not hold to the same rule:
the initializer took every key it was given, and `writeGlobalState`
excluded application and workspace scope machine keys but not profile
scope ones. Both wrote what they took at `StorageTarget.USER`.

`chat.transferedWorkspaces` is a profile scope, MACHINE target key. It is
this machine's own record that a chat session was moved to a folder, and
`ChatTransferService` grants that folder workspace trust on open. The
read did not look at the target, so a value carried in profile content
satisfied it, and applying that profile made a folder named by the
content trusted.

Two changes, either of which closes it, both worth having:

Applying profile content now uses one shared rule for the keys it will
not take, and that rule includes profile scope MACHINE keys. The
initializer uses the same rule instead of taking everything. Rejecting
one key no longer costs the rest of the content.

`ChatTransferService` requires the list to be at MACHINE target before it
is honoured. This is the half that holds when the key is not already
present on the machine, which the key-based rule above cannot see.

Not addressed here: trust is still granted from an emptiness check made
before the folder is opened, so a folder that gains content in between is
still trusted. That is a separate change to how the transfer flow decides
trust, rather than to which values it will believe.

commit_message:
Withhold the GnuPG sandbox grant from Git commands that can run a supplied program

The agent terminal sandbox grants a Git command `allowAllUnixSockets`
together with read and write access to `~/.gnupg`, so that a signing
operation can reach gpg-agent and the keyring. The rule matched on the
`git` keyword alone.

Git reaches gpg through a child process, and the grant is applied to the
whole sandboxed process tree, so whatever Git spawns inherits it. Several
ordinary parts of Git's command line choose that child: an alias whose
value starts with `!` is a shell command, `core.pager`, `core.editor`,
`credential.helper` and `core.hooksPath` all name programs, `--exec` and
`--upload-pack` take one directly, and `git bisect run` exists to run
one. `git -c alias.audit='!...' audit` reads as an ordinary Git command
to the rule and as an arbitrary shell command to Git, which then holds
the keyring and every Unix socket on the machine.

Refuse the grant for those invocations. Configuration overrides are
checked against an allow list of keys that cannot name a program, rather
than a deny list, because Git keeps adding keys that can and a deny list
would sit one release behind. None of the refused forms is a signing
operation, so nothing a signing flow needs is lost; a command that does
need signing and is refused fails visibly rather than silently running
with the keyring exposed.

Two details are worth noting for review:

`-c` is only read as a configuration override before the subcommand.
After it, `-c` belongs to the subcommand -- `git commit -c <commit>`
reuses a commit message -- and reading that as a configuration key would
refuse the grant to an ordinary signing command. `--exec` and friends are
the other way round: they belong to the subcommand, so the whole argument
list is scanned for them.

The environment can redirect what Git runs just as effectively as the
arguments can, through `GIT_CONFIG_*`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `PATH` and
others, so the parser now reports the assignments that prefix a command
instead of discarding them. This does mean an invocation carrying one of
those assignments no longer receives the grant, `GIT_EDITOR=true git
commit -S` included.

The check runs over the whole invocation next to the existing Docker
check, since the grant covers the process tree and one such command
anywhere in a chain is enough to pass the keyring on.

commit_message:
Authorize the extension id passed to SecretStorage RPC

`MainThreadSecretState` took `extensionId` off the wire and used it
directly as the storage namespace for get, set, delete and keys. Nothing
checked that the extension host on the other end of the connection has
anything to do with that extension.

`ExtensionSecrets` does bind the id to the calling extension's own
identifier, but it does that on the extension host side -- the far side of
the connection -- so it cannot be what the workbench relies on. A remote
extension host runs code from the remote machine, while the store it
reaches here is the user's local secret store, holding the tokens of UI
extensions such as the authentication providers. So a remote host could
name a local extension and read, overwrite or delete its secrets.

Resolve the extension's running location on the workbench side, which is
the trusted answer to where an extension actually runs, and refuse the
call when its kind differs from the connection's kind. An extension this
window does not run is refused too, since secrets belonging to a disabled
or uninstalled extension can still be sitting in the store. Identifiers
are compared through `ExtensionIdentifier.toKey`, so case cannot be used
to slip past the check.

This separates hosts, not extensions within a host: extensions sharing a
host share a process and can already reach each other's state, so a check
at that granularity would not be a boundary.

commit_message:
agentHost: ignore host notice turns when resolving the last turn

The Agents Window sometimes showed an empty changeset for the last turn.
Agent Merge posts status notices ("Agent Merge is enabled for `x`") as
complete, hidden turns via `_writeAgentMergeNotice`. These never reach the
provider and never capture a checkpoint, but both last-turn resolvers took
`turns.at(-1)`, so the notice became "the last turn" and its empty changeset
replaced the real one. Because the notice's request row is hidden, the
transcript still ended on the user's turn, so the UI looked correct.

The same notice also displaced the session changeset's git fast path:
`_latestTurnIdAcrossChats` found no checkpoint for it and fell back to the
edit tracker, which cannot see terminal-tool edits.

commit_message:
Agent Host: accept claude.ai keychain logins in the Claude native account check (fixes #333738)

`isClaudeAccountSetUp` inferred "set up" from `tokenSource` / `apiKeySource`
alone. Those fields name the environment variable a credential came from, so a
`claude login` (claude.ai subscription) credential in the keychain reports
neither: `accountInfo()` answers with `subscriptionType` / `email` /
`organization` and `apiProvider: 'firstParty'` only. Every branch of the check
was false for that login, the native model catalog came back empty, and the
Agents window pushed subscription users to GitHub sign-in or to a plaintext
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`.

Accept the first-party login when the SDK reports `subscriptionType` or
`email` (the fields the SDK's `AccountInfo` type exposes for it), keep the
existing token / API key / third-party branches unchanged, add the observed
keychain shape to the unit test, and log the subscription tier presence next to
the existing source fields.
