commit_message:
agentHost: let managed permissions see shell paths, and stop misstating why a read is gated

Two independent fixes to Copilot managed-permission handling in the agent host.

**Enable the runtime's shell-script safety classifier.**

Managed permission rules such as `Read(...)` and `Edit(...)` match on filesystem
paths. For a shell command the runtime only populates `possiblePaths` and
`hasWriteFileRedirection` when the session option `enableScriptSafety` is set;
otherwise `assess_safety` short-circuits and returns a degenerate assessment
with no paths, no redirection flag, and the whole script as a single non-read-only
command.

The agent host never set the option, so every shell command reached the
permission layer carrying no paths at all. Observed effect: with a managed
`deny: Edit(/.github/workflows/**)` in force, `echo x >> .github/workflows/f.yml`
surfaced as an ordinary shell prompt and modified the file. Even `tail -3 f`
was reported as non-read-only. The Copilot CLI opts in at session creation; the
agent host did not.

The SDK exposes the option on `SessionUpdateOptionsParams` rather than on
`SessionConfig`/`ResumeSessionConfig`, so it is applied from `_finalizeSession`
via `rpc.options.update`. That is the single point shared by the create, resume,
and resume-fallback paths, and it runs before the wrapper is handed to a caller,
so no turn can start without it. Failure is logged at error rather than thrown,
matching the surrounding post-launch option updates.

This restores the path data the permission layer needs. Note that matching
managed path rules against a shell command's `possiblePaths` is a separate
runtime-side concern and is not addressed here.

**Report the actual reason a read needs approval.**

`getPermissionDisplay` returned "Allow reading file outside of workspace?" for
every `read` request, but a read is gated for several reasons: the path is
outside the workspace, a managed or scoped rule matched it, managed rules are
active and an unmatched request defaults to ask, or the model asked to escape
the sandbox. Reads inside the workspace were therefore told they were outside
it. The branch also ignored `requestSandboxBypass`, which was already being
computed for reads, while the neighbouring `shell` and `write` branches vary
their titles.

The title is now chosen from the request: a sandbox-bypass read mirrors the
shell wording, a genuinely outside path keeps the original title, and anything
else uses a neutral "Allow reading file?". Containment uses
`extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase.isEqualOrParent` so platform case-insensitivity is
respected, and a relative path, unknown path, or unknown working directory
falls back to the neutral title rather than asserting a location the request
does not establish.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: address review — multi-root read titles and fail-closed script safety

Two review findings on the previous commit.

**Account for every workspace root before claiming a read is outside it.**

The read confirmation title compared the path only against the primary process
root, so in a multi-root session a read under a peer root
(`ICopilotSessionLaunchBase.additionalDirectories`) still reported "outside of
workspace" — the same misleading diagnosis this change set exists to remove.
`getPermissionDisplay` now takes the session's additional directories and treats
a path as outside only when no root contains it.

**Fail closed when script safety cannot be enabled under managed rules.**

Logging and continuing left the session usable after the runtime failed or
refused to enable the classifier, which silently degrades enterprise
enforcement: managed `Read(...)`/`Edit(...)` rules cannot inspect shell redirect
targets, permitting exactly the bypass this change targets.

Launch now fails and the orphaned session is disconnected when managed
permission rules are in force. Without managed rules there is no policy to
escape, so a transient or compatibility failure is logged as a warning and the
session continues rather than making every user's sessions unlaunchable.
`_finalizeSession` disconnects `raw` before rethrowing, since nothing owns that
session until it is wrapped.

commit_message:
agentHost: keep the out-of-workspace read title reachable

The unauthorized-path gate is the case the original hardcoded title described,
and narrowing the title by path containment alone made it unreachable.

That gate runs ahead of the per-kind gates and fires only for paths outside the
allowed directories. It is not a distinct request kind: it reuses the access
kind, so it arrives as `kind: "read"`, but it carries `paths` (plural) rather
than the per-kind `path`. `getPermissionDisplay` reads `request.path`, which is
therefore undefined for these requests, so the containment check could not
succeed and every out-of-workspace read fell through to the neutral title —
losing the one diagnosis that was correct before this change set.

A request carrying `paths` is treated as out-of-workspace by construction, which
is a stronger signal than comparing against the workspace roots: it is the
runtime's own verdict that the path is outside the allowed directories, and it
covers directories the user approved earlier that are not workspace roots.

The SDK's `PermissionRequestRead` does not model `paths`, hence the structural
check rather than a typed discriminator.

the host's permission layer. `commands_requiring_approval` skips commands the
classifier reports as read-only, so the scenario's `echo` is now resolved by
the runtime without ever raising a permission request. The host's
"Auto-approving sandboxed shell command" branch therefore never runs, and the
SDK-sandbox smoke test failed waiting for that log entry on Linux and macOS.
(Windows skips both sandbox tests, which is why it stayed green.)

Before this PR the classifier short-circuited and reported the whole script as
a single non-read-only command, which forced the prompt the test was keyed to.
The prompt was redundant: the command still runs mxc-wrapped under the pushed
sandbox policy, so not asking is the better behavior, and the assertion is
simply stale rather than the code being wrong.

tool ran the command, and keeps the `Applied SDK sandboxConfig` and negative

for the negative assertion than the old pre-execution entry, since a competing
ShellManager run would have been logged by that point. The host auto-approve
branch still governs non-read-only sandboxed commands and remains asserted by
the custom-terminal-tool test above.

commit_message:
agentHost: fail closed on script safety for every session

`IAgentHostManagedSettingsService` only carries the legacy VS Code settings
bridge — its own documentation says so, and that new enterprise controls belong
directly in the SDK's managed-settings contract. Server and MDM policy is
discovered by the runtime itself under `enableManagedSettings`, so it never
appears in `permissions`.

Gating fail-closed on that signal therefore inverted the intent: a session
governed solely by GitHub or MDM policy looks unmanaged from the host's side, so
an `options.update` failure left exactly the policy-bearing sessions running
without the classifier that managed `Read(...)`/`Edit(...)` rules depend on to
see shell paths.

Querying the runtime's effective managed-settings result instead would cost a
proxy resolution and a separate SDK import on every launch, and would make a
security control depend on a second fallible lookup. The option is cheap,
present in the pinned SDK, and accepted by the runtime, so it is now treated as
required for every session and a failure fails the launch.

The launcher tests cover both a client-bridged session and one where the host
sees no managed rules at all, since that is what an enterprise session governed
only by server or MDM policy looks like from here. The shared resume-fallback
mock gained the `rpc.options.update` surface a real session always has; without
it the fixture failed on a missing `rpc` rather than on the behavior under test.

commit_message:
agentHost: report every terminal turn outcome through onTurnEnd

Closes three gaps where a turn ended without telling contributions. A turn that captured a
start checkpoint and then failed to send never scheduled its changeset recompute, because
`captureTurnStartCheckpoint` runs before `sendMessage` but the catch never reported the end.

- Reports a turn end when a send throws. This is the bug: `CheckpointAndChangesetContribution`
  handles `kind === 'error'` and never heard about these turns, so their changeset recompute
  and unread marking did not run.
- Reports a turn end for a client-dispatched cancellation, which the agent-signal path already
  did. This fires exactly once: the reducer clears the active turn first, so a later
  agent-emitted cancellation takes the no-active-turn path, which reports only completions.
- Adds a `rejected` reason for requests refused before their turn started, and fires it from
  both `startTurn` early returns: a rejected admission and a missing provider. This restores
  the per-rejection observability that hoisting the admission gate removed.
- Makes `MarkUnreadContribution` ignore `rejected`. It filtered negatively, so the new reason
  would have marked a session unread for a request that never ran, and a rejection on an
  archived session would resurface it.
- Leaves `QueueDrainContribution` untouched for `rejected`. A rejected queued turn consumes its
  message and the queue stalls, but draining would cascade an archived chat through every
  queued message. The fix is to return the message to the queue, which is recorded as such.
- Adds tests for all three paths, including that a rejected turn end does not resurface a read
  session. Both new `agentSideEffects` tests were confirmed to fail without the fix.

Rewrites `chatContributions/TODO.md` as a backlog. It had grown into a changelog of finished
extractions and a design-decision record, and two of its claims were already wrong: the
side-chat migration it listed as pending was complete, and `githubReferences` was filed under
outgoing-turn contributions although it only implements `onTurnEnd`. Rationale that had no
other home moved into JSDoc beside the code it explains.

commit_message:
agentHost: observe dispatched actions through a chat contribution hook

Moves session input-needed aggregation, turn-usage persistence, and session flag persistence
out of `AgentSideEffects`, which loses 252 lines. All three observed
`AgentHostStateManager.onDidEmitEnvelope` rather than the client dispatch path, so none of
them could use the existing action hook: most of the actions they react to are dispatched by
the host, not by a client.

- Adds `onDidDispatchAction`, which observes an action from any origin once its outcome is
  known, including server-dispatched actions and rejected ones that never reduced. It is a
  separate hook and not a widening of the client hook, because `queueDrain` depends on that
  hook being client-only and would otherwise see each client action twice.
- Adds `SessionInputNeededContribution` (order 200), which mirrors per-chat blockers into the
  owning session's `inputNeeded` list. This is the bulk of the move at roughly 170 lines.
- Gives `PersistedTurnUsageContribution` the write half of turn-usage persistence. It already
  owned the restore half, so one contribution now owns both directions, as chat drafts and
  chat titles already do.
- Adds `SessionFlagsContribution` (order 700) for read state, archived state, and merged
  config values. It preserves an asymmetry that is easy to lose: read and archived changes
  skip a rejected action, config values do not.
- Makes `AgentHostToolCallTracker` injectable. Input-needed reports blocked and unblocked tool
  calls to it, and it was constructed inside `AgentSideEffects`, so a contribution could not
  reach it.

Renames the two action hooks so each says what it observes:

- `onAction` becomes `onDidApplyClientAction`, and `IObservedAction` becomes
  `IAppliedClientAction`. Rejected client actions never reach it, so an action it sees always
  reduced.
- `onEnvelope` becomes `onDidDispatchAction`, and `IObservedEnvelope` becomes
  `IDispatchedAction`. It also delivers rejected actions, so a name claiming they were applied
  would be wrong.

Registers the built-in contributions in the tool-call and turn-hang telemetry test graphs.
Both build `AgentSideEffects` without them, so they stopped exercising blocked-call telemetry
once that reporting moved into a contribution. The graphs now mirror production wiring; no
assertion changed.

Updates the contributions skill, which described four hooks and named two that no longer
exist. It now documents all seven, records that the admission hook fails closed and is
synchronous while every other hook isolates failures, and carries the design rationale that
`TODO.md` used to hold. `TODO.md` keeps only open work and caveats, with each fact in one
place.

commit_message:
Agents - show a badge on the application icon for sessions needing attention

Adds an opt-in badge on the application icon showing how many non-archived
sessions in the Agents window are unread or waiting for input.

The new `sessions.showApplicationBadge` setting is off by default and carries
`experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`, so it can be rolled out (and rolled back)
through Exp without a window reload.

Platform behaviour differs because the OS support does:

- macOS (dock) and Linux (Unity launcher) render the count themselves via
  `app.setBadgeCount`.
- Windows has no equivalent for an unpackaged Win32 app: `app.setBadgeCount`
  is a no-op there and `BrowserWindow.setOverlayIcon` only takes a bitmap.
  The renderer therefore draws a themed overlay and hands it over as a
  `data:` URL. A nested `VSBuffer` would not survive the `ProxyChannel`,
  which only revives buffers passed as top-level arguments.

`DockBadgeManager` now owns the application-wide badge for both the transient
`FocusMode.Notify` attention dot and the per-window counts, so the two cannot
overwrite each other. Counts are keyed by window and released on window
dispose, so a closed or crashed window cannot strand a phantom badge.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Agents - fix application badge property init order and IPC payload

- `iconDataURL` was set to `undefined` on platforms that do not need an

commit_message:
debug: work around frozen renderer when launching from Run and Debug

Launching the workbench with the "VS Code" or "Renderer and Main processes"
compound can leave the window painted but unresponsive: nothing is clickable,
the keyboard does nothing, and the extension host never finishes starting.

The renderer is stuck in the debugger's waiting-for-debugger state.
`Inspector.workerScriptLoaded` can arrive for a web worker whose CDP session
js-debug has not registered yet; js-debug throws, the throw escapes
`EventEmitter.fire` and leaves its delivery queue populated, and that
permanently stops the CDP message pump. `Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger` is
therefore never sent.

Add a hidden configuration to the affected compounds that detects a renderer
whose event loop never turns and resumes it. It waits 8s first so js-debug can
attach normally, and is inert when the renderer is healthy.

Reported upstream as microsoft/vscode-js-debug#2401 with a fix proposed in
microsoft/vscode-js-debug#2402; this should be reverted once that ships.

commit_message:
Reserve the sign-in window during the user gesture

Browsers only allow `window.open` while a click's user activation is still
live. Chat sign-in shows a dialog, activates an extension and fetches an
authorization URL first, so by the time it opens anything the gesture has
expired and Safari refuses the window.

In a browser tab this surfaces as a "browser blocked opening a new tab"
prompt whose Retry works, because Retry runs inside a fresh click. In an
installed web app (PWA) on iOS there is no tab to fall back to and the
prompt is covered by the "Signing in..." modal, so sign-in dead-ends with
no way forward.

Claim the window synchronously on the click instead, and let
`windowOpenWithSuccess` navigate that reserved window once the URL is
known. Gated to Safari, so other browsers are unaffected. The reservation
is released when setup ends without using it, so a cancelled or failed
sign-in does not leave a blank window over the app.

commit_message:
chat: show one OS notification when a session has no more work

Agent host sessions can be open in the editor window and the agents window at the
same time. This caused two problems with the OS notifications. A "finished" toast
came when a response ended, even if more requests were in the queue. A session that
was open in two windows made one toast from each window.

- Adds an idle observable in the chat window notifier. It combines the request
  state, the input state, and the count of queued requests. The notifier shows the
  toast only when the session has no more work. A 500ms delay prevents a toast in
  the short gap between two queued turns.
- Makes the chat window notifier the only source of toasts in a window. It now
  shows the toast for needed input and for the idle state. The toast in the chat
  accessibility service is removed. That service keeps the accessibility signal and
  the ARIA announcement.
- Limits the sessions window notifier to sessions that have no chat model in this
  window. Sessions with a model are the responsibility of the chat window notifier,
  which knows about the queue.
- Adds a dedupe key to the toast options. The main process does not show a second
  toast while a toast with the same key is on the screen. This prevents duplicate
  toasts from two windows for one session.
- Delays the toast 250ms in a window that does not show the session. The window
  that shows the session makes its toast first, so a click opens the window that
  the user worked in.
- Delays the completed toast 1500ms in the sessions window notifier. A session with
  no chat model here gives no queue information, so the delay prevents a toast in
  the gap between two queued turns. See
  https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/issues/426 for the permanent fix.

commit_message:
agentHost: keep a model reference for chats that are created

A side chat that was started with `/btw` during an active turn opened an empty widget that
never answered. `createSideChat` acquired a chat model, applied the carried-over model and
agent, then released the reference immediately. The reference count fell to zero, which
disposed the provided session and released its agent host chat subscription. The open and
send steps that followed raced that asynchronous teardown. Both steps resolved the session
content at the same time and each built an `AgentHostChatSession`. The second session
replaced the first in `_activeSessions`, but the chat model kept the first. Turn progress
went to a session that no widget observed.

- Deduplicates concurrent session resolution in `ChatSessionsService`. Callers share one
  in-flight promise. The shared work is cancelled only after every caller cancels, so one
  caller that gives up cannot abort the work of the others.
- Disposes a session that the service does not adopt. This covers the session that loses the
  cache race and a session that a provider returns after cancellation. The agent host
  provider does not honour cancellation, so it can still return a fully wired session.
- Replaces the immediate release in `createSideChat`, `forkChat`, and `_createAdditionalChat`
  with a model reference that expires after 10 seconds. The reference keeps the model alive
  across the open and send steps and cannot become permanent.
- Removes the redundant `getOrCreateChatSession` call from those three paths. The standard
  `acquireOrLoadSession` path resolves the session and owns it with a reference count.
- Logs an error when a new agent host session replaces an active session for one resource.
  This invariant was assumed in many places but was enforced in none.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332862

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: protect the active session from a late cancelled resolution

Hydration does not stop when the token is cancelled, so a resolution that every caller
abandoned still builds a session. A retry can register its own session first. The abandoned
session then replaced it in `_activeSessions`, and the disposal that follows released the
subscriptions that the live session still used. The live chat became unresponsive again.

- Returns an abandoned session without registration when an active session exists for the
  same resource. The session is disposed by the caller and must not rewire shared state.
- Makes the disposal cleanup conditional. A session removes the state for its resource only
  while it still owns the entry in `_activeSessions`.
- Adds a regression test. The test fails without both guards, because the disposal releases
  the session and chat subscriptions of the live session.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

commit_message:
sessions: pull request operations in the changes title bar

The changes button bar only offered "Create PR" variants, and they
disappeared once a pull request existed. It now keeps offering the next
step for that pull request, and gives Agent Merge a home next to it.

Agent host:

- New `AgentHostPullRequestStatusService` watches the `core` and
  `mergeability` fragments of the session's pull request. It subscribes
  only while a client is subscribed to the session's changeset, so the
  GitHub API cost is bounded to the session the user is looking at.
- `AgentHostPullRequestOperationContribution` now advertises
  `pr-mark-ready`, `pr-merge` and `pr-enable-auto-merge` /
  `pr-disable-auto-merge` instead of bailing out once a pull request
  exists. Auto-merge is driven off GitHub's own capability flags rather
  than re-deriving its rules. Nothing is advertised while the state is
  unresolved, so the bar stays hidden rather than flashing the wrong
  action, or once the pull request is merged or closed.
- `AgentHostPullRequestLifecycleOperationHandler` executes them. Merging
  goes through `prepareMerge`, so a pull request that stopped being
  mergeable between render and click is rejected rather than
  force-merged, and enqueues when the repository requires a merge queue.
- Adds the `markReadyForReview` and `disableAutoMerge` GitHub mutations.

Agents window:

- New `AgentsChangesOperationsDropdown` menu whose entries are merged
  into the primary button's dropdown. A submenu contributed to its
  `primary` group names a group of related actions rather than being one,
  so clicking the button opens just those as a context menu.
- Agent Merge contributes its session toggle, repair-action toggles,
  merge-choice submenu and "Agent Merge Defaults" there, gated on the
  existing precondition plus the session having an open pull request.

`chat.agentMerge.mergePullRequest` becomes a three-way enum. `ifUnchanged`
merges only while Agent Merge has not changed the pull request: when a
repair turn lands a commit the session's value rewrites itself to `never`
and says so in the transcript, so the chosen value always reflects what
will happen. Re-selecting it starts a fresh baseline. Existing boolean
values migrate.

commit_message:
agentMerge: base the unchanged check on the local commit

The `ifUnchanged` merge option compared the pull request's published head
before and after a repair turn. GitHub reports a push only after a
replication delay, and a turn ends by evaluating immediately, so the
comparison routinely read a stale head: the session was not demoted, the
gate still saw `ifUnchanged`, and it could merge changes the option exists
to hold back. It also failed open, treating "cannot tell" as "unchanged".

Compare the session worktree's commit instead, captured when the repair
turn starts and re-read when it ends. The commit exists locally the moment
the agent makes it, so there is no window to race, and it answers the
actual question -- did Agent Merge change anything -- without also firing
when somebody else pushes to the pull request.

The decision now happens once in `_completeTurn` rather than on every
evaluation, with the sync path keeping it only as a backstop for a host
restart that lost the in-flight turn. An unreadable worktree records a
sentinel baseline that no commit can match, so it fails closed: a missed
automatic merge is cheaper than merging agent-written changes unreviewed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Address review feedback on the pull request operations title bar

- Rebuild pull request watches when the GitHub credential is invalidated
  for an account or endpoint change. `PullRequestResourceService` disposes
  the resource for those reasons, so the watch was left holding a
  subscription whose snapshot could never update, advertising stale
  operations until an unrelated event happened to resync it.
- Gate the Agent Merge entries on a distinct open-pull-request signal
  rather than on an operation being advertised. An open but blocked pull
  request in a repository without auto-merge offers no operation, which is
  exactly when the repair actions are useful, yet the entries were hidden.
- Clear the repair baseline when "merge only while unchanged" is selected
  afresh. The client writes only its own Agent Merge state, so a baseline
  left by an earlier repair turn would immediately demote the choice back
  to never and the option could never be turned back on.
- Move the Agents Window menu IDs to `sessions/browser/menus.ts` so the
  shared platform layer no longer owns Sessions concepts.
- Cover the watcher's subscription lifecycle, mid-flight invalidation and
  credential handling, and the merge handler's preparation gate,
  merge-queue selection, configured-method rejection and stale
  preparation.

commit_message:
Show a spinner on the changes title bar button while work is in flight

The title bar buttons deliberately show no icon, so a running operation had
no visual feedback: the loading-icon prefix the operation actions carried was
stripped along with every other icon by the button config provider.

`WorkbenchButtonBar` gains an opt-in `showSpinner` button config, rendering
the pixel spinner already used for in-progress sessions in the sessions
list, session header and automations view. It leads the label, inherits the
button foreground through `currentColor`, and the primitive pauses itself
offscreen and honours reduced motion. For a dropdown button it attaches to
the primary half rather than the chevron.

The changes button bar turns it on while an advertised operation is running
-- create PR, commit, and the rest -- and while Agent Merge owns the primary
button and is enabled, since it watches the pull request continuously rather
than completing. `sessionAgentMergeEnabled` moved to the shared sessions
context keys so the widget can read it without importing Agent Merge.

commit_message:
Add "Continue with Microsoft" sign in for GitHub

Brokers a GitHub session from an Entra token the built-in `microsoft`
provider already holds, so someone signed in to Microsoft can reach
Copilot without a second browser round trip.

The flow is deliberately two exchanges. The first buys a `read:user`
discovery token, just enough to `GET /user` and show which GitHub account
the Entra identity maps to. Nothing is published until the user confirms
that identity. The second exchange then mints the scopes the caller
actually asked for. The discovery token is never persisted and never
published as a session.

Entra-brokered sessions live in memory for the life of the window and are
never written to the Keychain. What survives a reload is the user's
consent, recorded in global state as a GitHub label, a Microsoft label,
and the GitHub user id. A fresh window mints the session again from that
row, silently, re-verifying through discovery that the row still points
at the same account.

Rows are keyed by GitHub account label, because that is what VS Code
itself keys an account by: `getAccounts` collapses sessions by label and
the account preference is stored by label. The id is kept for one job
only, checking that the token GitHub just returned belongs to the account
the row names.

Signing out of the Microsoft account drops the sessions, since nothing
can renew them, but leaves the rows alone. The Microsoft account list is
a per-window cache that reads empty for a moment while it repopulates,
and the rows are global state shared by every window, so acting on a
blink of that list would sign the user out everywhere with no way back.
Dropping only the sessions self-heals: the next read mints them again
from the row that is still there.

Verify the granted token against the account the user confirmed, not just
the discovery token, and give that mismatch its own failure kind so a
restore only forgets a link when GitHub positively names somebody else.

Make a failed unlink write stick for the window that did it, so a sign out

was in flight, settle every expired session rather than only those with

commit_message:
Show the exact requested URL in the prompt install confirmation

The dialog rendered `url.toString()` while the request is made with the raw
`urlString`. `URI.toString()` reserializes, so a URL such as
`https://user%40example.com@evil.test/file` is displayed as
`https://user@example.com%40evil.test/file`, which reads as if the host were
`example.com` when the request actually goes to `evil.test`.

Pass the string that is actually requested into the confirmation and escape it
for the attribute context, so the label, the tooltip and the accessible name all
describe the URL that will be fetched.

commit_message:
Fix broken "Sent from another chat" request-origin link

Two independent bugs prevented a delegated request's request-origin
pill from opening its source chat:

- In the Agents window, OpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution fell back to
  a bare openSession() when a link carried no chat id. Per
  buildOpenSessionLinkUri's invariant, an absent chat id means the
  session's default chat, but openSession() only activates the
  session without switching the active chat, so clicking the pill was
  a no-op whenever a different chat of the same session was already
  showing. It now resolves the target chat explicitly (the peer chat
  when a chat id is present, otherwise the session's main/default
  chat) and opens it via openChat() in both cases.

- In the regular editor window, AgentHostOpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution
  never registered an opener with IChatRequestOriginService (only with
  IOpenerService for markdown-authored links), so clicking the pill
  found no opener and fell back to treating the opaque
  agent-host-session:// link as a session resource directly, which
  never resolves. It now also registers a request-origin opener that
  reuses the existing link-opening logic.

Added focused regression tests for both fixes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: don't tell the agent to reply-and-stop after create_session (#330138)

The `create_session` / `send_message` server tools instructed the model to
"Reply with one short sentence confirming the … was created" — both in the tool
result and in the tool description. The model read this as a turn terminator, so
a request like "spawn a session for X and then do Y" stopped after X.

- Make the tool results neutral statements of fact (`New session created
  (link).`), carrying the open link with no reply-and-stop imperative.
- Make the tool descriptions purely functional: drop the UI-presentation policy
  ("the UI renders…", "don't print the URL") and the "reply with a single short
  sentence" instruction.
- Add a focused regression test locking both the neutral results and the
  functional descriptions.
- Regenerate the Copilot prompt snapshots for the updated descriptions.

Removing the explicit stop signal is a real improvement, but because the agent
host runs a model-driven loop the model can still choose to end a turn after any
tool call; a fully reliable fix would be structural (see issue discussion).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
sessions: Reconcile offscreen chat approval heights; keep "once" in aria label

Address PR review feedback:

- Offscreen virtualization height staleness: the per-row approval autorun is
  tied to the (disposed) row template, so an approval that appears, clears, or
  changes line count while a chat row is virtualized offscreen left the
  ListView's cached height stale, clipping the Allow control on re-entry. Add a
  list-owned autorun (SessionsList.reconcileChatApprovalHeights) that watches
  each chat's live approval and reconciles its cached height independently of
  the row template — so offscreen changes correct the height immediately. It is
  re-established after every update() since chat items are rebuilt each render.
- Accessibility: restore the one-time permission scope dropped from the Allow
  button's accessible name — "Allow: {0}" -> "Allow once: {0}".

Adds a regression test that changes an approval while its row is virtualized
offscreen and asserts the row reserves the reconciled height (and shows the
Allow control) once scrolled into view.

commit_message:
Honor a server-supplied Retry-After instead of capping it

Capping every rate-limit wait at 8s also shortened a server-supplied
`Retry-After`, which re-issued the request inside the window the server
had just asked us to stay out of. With `Retry-After: 60` that meant three
retries at 8s, 16s and 24s, each earning another 429, feeding the rate
limit that caused the problem and dropping the session anyway.

Split the cap in two: RATE_LIMIT_MAX_BACKOFF_MS now bounds only the
backoff this client computes for itself, and a separate wait budget
bounds the pass. A delay that does not fit the budget ends the retries
rather than being trimmed to fit, so the read reports its 429 and leaves
the scan partial for a later pass.

Also moves the test off the deprecated timeTravelScheduler re-export.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Let a host declare which changeset the Changes view defaults to

The Changes view hardcoded `branch` as its default — the commits `HEAD`
introduces relative to its merge-base with the base branch. A cloud sandbox
agent edits the working tree without committing, so that view is empty and
the panel read "No Changed Files" for work the chat had just reported.

Add an optional `defaultChangesetKind` to the adapter options and have the
cloud sandbox contribution declare `session`, the changeset holding the
agent's own edits. Hosts that declare nothing keep the `branch` default.

commit_message:
agentHost: gate turns through an onIncomingRequest chat contribution hook

Adds an admission hook to the chat contribution model and moves the read-only guard and
local command interception onto it. Turn admission was duplicated: `handleAction` and
`QueueDrainContribution` each ran the same preamble, and the read-only guard sat further
down in the send path. Admission now has one route and one copy.

- Adds `onIncomingRequest`, which decides whether a turn may proceed to its provider. A
  contribution returns `accept`, `handled`, or `reject`, and the first non-accept
  disposition wins.
- Makes the hook fail closed. Every other hook skips a contribution that throws; a throwing
  admission contribution rejects the request instead. The gate stops a client from running
  work in a session that can have no worktree on disk, so a failure must not open it.
- Makes the hook synchronous. A gate must decide before the send path awaits, so the state
  it reads cannot change before the decision takes effect. An asynchronous version deferred
  the read-only guard by one microtask and broke three existing tests.
- Adds `TurnAdmissionContribution` (order 100), which rejects turns on read-only chats and
  archived sessions.
- Adds `LocalCommandContribution` (order 50), which handles `/rename` and `!command`. The
  order is load-bearing: local commands were always intercepted before the read-only guard,
  so they stay available in read-only and archived chats.
- Adds the `startTurn` function, which runs the shared preamble: the gate, title seeding,
  provider lookup, the `noAgent` error, and turn telemetry. Both admission paths invoke it
  with `IInstantiationService.invokeFunction`. It is a function and not a service because it
  holds no state, so a service registration would only add one line to every hand-built test
  service graph.
- Moves `AgentHostTurnFailureStage` to `common` so the disposition can name a failure stage.
  The node telemetry reporter re-exports it, so no importer changes.
- Removes the admission block from `_sendTurnMessage`, which is now only the send tail.
- Accepts that a rejected turn no longer reports `userMessageSent` or `turnCompleted`. The
  gate runs before `turnStarted`, so there is no turn to complete. `chatContributions/TODO.md`
  records this.
- Rewrites `chatContributions/TODO.md`. It listed `githubReferences` as an outgoing-turn
  contribution although it only implements `onTurnEnd`, and described an admission flow that
  no longer exists. Adds a table of all six hooks and their contributions in order.

commit_message:
feat: brand Code - OSS 1.131.0 as FusionIDE

Seeds the FusionIDE fork from the upstream 1.131.0 stable tag and applies the
product identity as a reproducible overlay rather than a hand-edited file.

build/fusionide/apply-product-overlay.mjs merges FusionIDE's identity into
product.json and deletes what a fork must not ship. Upstream 1.131 carries more
than the branding rename: an in-tree GitHub Copilot integration
(defaultChatAgent's entitlement and token endpoints, plus the
trustedExtensionAuthAccess grant that lets Copilot Chat take a GitHub session
silently), a Microsoft voice WebSocket, and a telemetry app name. A
hand-maintained product.json reacquires whatever the next upstream merge adds,
so the overlay is a script with a --check mode that fails the build if anything
forbidden reappears.

builtInExtensions is dropped rather than kept: build/lib/builtInExtensions.ts
downloads those extensions from whatever gallery product.json configures, so
with an Open VSX gallery the build would ask Open VSX for Microsoft-published
extensions. Re-add individually only after confirming the registry serves each.

The gallery is Open VSX, and the overlay refuses any product.json whose gallery
host is not open-vsx.org or that mentions marketplace.visualstudio.com,
vscode-unpkg.net, or vscode-cdn.net.

FUSIONIDE.md records the branch and rebase model, the marker convention for
source edits, why each planned patch cannot be an extension, and the binding
policy on gallery, telemetry, trademark, and attribution.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
patch(terminal): strip FusionClaw control variables from every PTY

FusionClaw starts this server with an allowlisted environment, so no provider
credential is in the process tree to begin with. What remains is the one handle
it must pass through: the path to a 0600 file holding the loopback bridge URL
and its token. The extension host needs that; a shell does not, and a shell that
could read the file could drive the desktop bridge as though it were the IDE.

This is a patch rather than an extension because EnvironmentVariableCollection
can only append, replace, or prepend named variables -- it cannot remove one,
and it cannot see a variable a user re-injected through terminal.integrated.env.
TerminalProcess is the single choke point every PTY passes through.
author: vsimoesbh

commit_message:
patch(menus): add the FusionClaw menubar entries and Tools submenu

Extensions cannot reach the menubar: contributes.menus exposes context menus,
editor titles, and view titles, but has no File or Help slot and no way to
declare a top-level submenu. The commands are registered by the
fusionclaw.fusionide-bridge extension; core only says where they appear, so a
menu change never rebuilds the workbench.

Command ids are string literals on purpose -- core must not import from an
extension, and a missing command renders a disabled entry rather than breaking
the menu.
author: vsimoesbh

commit_message:
patch(webview): allow the microphone for FusionClaw's own webviews

FusionVoice records inside the chat webview, and an iframe cannot obtain a
device its permissions policy never granted -- no extension API widens that
policy, which is why this is a patch.

Both frames are patched: the outer element in webviewElement.ts and the inner
service-worker frame in pre/index.html, since granting on only one leaves the
capture without a microphone.

It is an allowlist keyed on the owning extension, not a blanket grant, so a
third-party extension installed from the gallery cannot silently reach the
microphone. The desktop still owns the OS-level permission prompt.
author: vsimoesbh

commit_message:
agentHost: move chat draft and title restore into chat contributions

Moves chat draft handling out of AgentSideEffects and AgentService into the chat contribution
model. Draft persistence and draft restore were in two different orchestration classes, and the
custom chat title had its write half in a contribution and its read half in AgentService. Each
behavior now has one owner.

- Adds an `onHydrateChat` hook. It restores host-owned chat state before a chat enters the
  session catalog. This is separate from `onHydrateTurns` because the two hooks run at
  different times, not because they carry different data: turn hydration runs lazily, after
  the provider returns a turn list, but a peer chat must show its title and draft at catalog
  registration, before its turns load.
- Adds a `hydrateChat` dispatcher. It copies the `hydrateTurns` semantics: a threading
  accumulator, per-hook ordering, and failure isolation that keeps the previous value. A
  failed contribution must not discard an already-restored title or draft.
- Adds `IRestoredChat` as an object, like `ISendContribution`, so a subsequent host-owned
  restorable field does not need a sixth hook. `IHydrationContext` is unchanged.
- Adds `ChatDraftContribution` (order 600). It owns draft persistence in both directions.
- Adds `onHydrateChat` to `SessionTitleContribution` (order 400), which already persisted the
  custom chat title in `onAction`.
- Removes `_persistChatDraft` and its envelope branch from AgentSideEffects, and `_getChatDraft`
  and `_readPersistedChatTitle` from AgentService. The three restore call sites each become one
  `hydrateChat` call.
- Changes the draft persistence trigger from `onDidEmitEnvelope` to `onAction`, which narrows it
  from client and server dispatch to client dispatch only. `ChatDraftChangedAction` is a
  `ClientChatAction` that nothing server-dispatches. This also stops a rejected draft from being
  written, because `onAction` runs after the reject guards in `_dispatchActionNow`.
- Keeps the `meta.model` overlay in AgentService. It seeds the draft model from provider-supplied
  session metadata, so it is provider-shaped and must not enter `IHydrationContext`.
- Adds dispatcher tests for ordering, async contributions, failure isolation, absent hooks, and
  the built-in sequence. The AgentSideEffects and AgentService suites are unchanged, which shows
  the extraction kept the previous behavior.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

commit_message:
Do not resolve content references as filesystem entries

A protocol `ContentRef` is read with `resourceRead` and carries its own
`sizeHint` and `contentType`. `resourceResolve` is "the combination of POSIX
`stat` and `realpath`" and answers only `file` / `directory` / `symlink` — none
of which a content ref is.

The agent-host filesystem provider stat'd them anyway, short-circuiting on a
hardcoded `session-db` / `git-blob` allowlist. Those are two of the shapes
VS Code's own host emits, so local sessions always hit the shortcut. A host is
free to pick its own shape: copilotd publishes
`ahp-session:/<id>/changeset/turncontent/<sha>`, which fell through to the
host's filesystem resolver and was rejected as a malformed file path. That
failed the stat the diff editor issues before reading, so the read — which the
host would have served — never ran and the diff came up empty.

Mark the URI instead of guessing from its scheme. Callers read these out of a
`ContentRef` field and know what they hold, so wrap them with
`toAgentHostContentUri`, which records it in the metadata the transport URI
already carries. `stat` and `realpath` short-circuit on that marker, and the
allowlist stays only for refs minted before it existed.

Apply external-session filter to wrapped-session paths

`shouldShowSession()` only guards the disk listing path. `getSession()` can
load an existing external session into `_sessionWrappers` without changing its
origin, and both `getSessionItemImpl()` (which prefers the wrapper) and the

listing paths. Sessions created or forked by this window are tracked in memory
since the origin metadata write is fire-and-forget, so a freshly created local
session cannot race its way out of the list.

commit_message:
agentHost: run Codex workspace hooks

Codex refuses to execute a hook until its exact command hash is recorded
as trusted in `config.toml`. That ledger is only written by the codex
TUI's startup hook review, a surface agent host users never reach, so
`.codex/hooks.json` hooks were listed in the Customizations view but
never dispatched.

Pass `bypass_hook_trust` on every codex thread (`thread/start`,
`thread/fork`, `thread/resume`) via a shared config fragment. This is
the documented use of the flag for automation that vets hook sources
up front: the agent host already requires VS Code Workspace Trust for
every session working directory before a session may start, matching
how the Claude and Copilot harnesses run workspace hooks. Enterprise
`allow_managed_hooks_only` is enforced independently by codex and still
applies.

Also protect `.codex/hooks.json`, `.codex/config.toml` and
`.codex/agents/**` with the always-checked edit patterns, so the agent
cannot silently write a hook manifest that now actually executes —
`.github/hooks/**` and `.claude/settings*.json` were already covered.

Fixes #331285

commit_message:
sessions: track manually typed characters in session summary telemetry

Adds `typedCharacters` and `typedFileCount` to `agents/sessionSummary`, reporting how much the user hand-edited a session's workspace rather than letting the agent do the work.

A new SessionsTypedCharactersTracker observes the text models of the window it runs in and counts only edits that pass the editor's `isUserEdit` predicate, so agent edits, accepted suggestions, paste and undo/redo are excluded. Because it sees only this window's models, typing done for the same folder in a regular window is naturally not counted. Typing fires one change per keystroke, so counts are buffered per resource and flushed in batches.

Attribution considers only the active session. Since flushing is batched, the active session is cached and the buffer flushed before adopting a new one, so characters stay with the session they were typed into when the user switches. Resources are matched against `folder.workingDirectory` rather than `folder.root` because a worktree session's root is the shared checkout it never edits. File identity is persisted as a hash and capped per session so stored state discloses no paths and stays bounded.

Also refreshes the workspace topology fields on every interaction. They were captured once at first observation, so a session whose workspace resolved or gained folders later reported stale counts.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: benibenj

commit_message:
sessions: address review feedback on typed-character telemetry

Two correctness fixes from review.

Typing is no longer dropped when a session workspace is still hydrating. The active session is now captured per keystroke instead of being read when the buffered batch is reported, and the reporting callback hands back entries it could not attribute so they are retried rather than discarded by a timer, save, or session-change flush. Retries are bounded, and quick chats -- workspace-less by product intent -- are discarded immediately instead of retried. Capturing the session at type time also removes the flush-before-switch workaround.

File identity now uses a truncated SHA-1 instead of `hash()`. That is a 32-bit polynomial string hash whose collisions are structural rather than random, so ordinary sibling paths collide outright: `file:///repo/Aa.ts` and `file:///repo/BB.ts` hash equal and were counted as one file. Identities persisted in the superseded numeric format are dropped on load because they cannot be compared against the new digests.

git: don't reveal deleted resources in OS file explorer

scm/resourceState/context menu for every Source Control resource,
including ones with Status.DELETED / INDEX_DELETED / BOTH_DELETED.

deleted resources, and surface a warning instead of failing silently.

streams: settle pending writes when a writeable stream is destroyed

commit_message:
ternary search tree: keep unrelated keys on deleteSuperstr

deleteSuperstr cleared all three child links of the prefix node, but
only the mid chain holds superstrings; left and right hold unrelated
keys that merely sort around that character position, so deleting a
prefix silently dropped unrelated entries. The context key service
calls this on every settings change, wiping unrelated cached config
values and leaving them out of the change event. Only mid is cleared
now. With left and right surviving, the value-less prefix node can
enter the BST removal path whose successor copy orphaned the
successor's equal-child chain; that chain now moves up together with
the copied segment. The removal guard also no longer treats stored
falsy values as absent, so an exact key holding 0, false or an empty
string survives deleting its superstrings.

commit_message:
Split session artifacts into artifacts and references

An artifact is something the session produced that is not an ordinary
workspace edit: a pull request or issue it opened, a plan file written
outside the workspace, another side effect of its work. A reference is
something it did not produce but the user should look at because of the
task: the pull request or commit that introduced a bug, a relevant page.

The agent now says which it recorded through a mandatory `isArtifact`
flag, so the tools are renamed to `add_artifact_or_reference`,
`remove_artifact_or_reference` and `list_artifacts_and_references`, and
the per-type `createdByThisSession` field is gone — being produced by the
session is the definition of an artifact. Entries persisted before this
change read back as artifacts. Tool calls render "Added artifact" or
"Added reference" from the flag; removal takes its wording from what it
actually removed.

References get their own pill, always summarized as a count, placed
directly after the artifacts pill so the two read as a pair. Only
artifacts are promoted into the pull request and issue pills, which poll
GitHub, but a reference keeps its link identity so anything those pills
already show is offered exactly once.

Along the way:

- The artifacts pill no longer collapses into a lone entry unless it is a
  file, whose name and themed icon say what it is; every other single
  artifact stays behind "1 Artifact" so the row keeps a stable shape.
  `alwaysSummarize` becomes a `ChatPillSingleEntry` policy interpreted in
  one place.
- Parsing GitHub issue and pull request references out of user messages is
  removed. It fed the same pills from a second source, which would show a
  recorded reference twice, and it guessed at intent the agent can now
  state outright.
- A `uri` the client cannot open is rejected when it is recorded, instead
  of being reported as added and then appearing in no pill at all.
- Reading persisted artifacts reports what it could not parse, so a
  corrupt row no longer empties a session's artifacts without a trace.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Address review feedback on artifacts and references

- `isArtifact` accepts only a boolean, with an absent field as the sole
  legacy default. A malformed value such as `"false"` or `null` no longer
  reads back as an artifact; the entry is rejected and counted among the
  dropped rows the caller warns about.
- A recorded `uri` is validated by the client's own strict `URI.parse`
  rather than a hand-rolled pattern, so the two can no longer disagree.
  The previous check accepted values like `foo/bar:baz`, which the client
  then failed to open, leaving the entry in no pill at all.
- Renamed server tools keep answering to the names they were advertised

  legacy name before dispatching, and the display path falls back to it
  once no advertised tool matches — so restored history and prompts
  written against `add_artifact` still route and still render. Groups only
  ever see their current names.
- The Sessions and agent host provider specifications now state that
  `ISession.artifacts` carries both categories and that consumers must use
  `isArtifact` to tell them apart.

commit_message:
Resolve changeset URI templates published relative to the session

A session's changeset catalogue advertises each entry's subscribable URI as a
`uriTemplate`. AHP describes that template as itself subscribable, and VS
Code's own agent host publishes it that way, so the client parsed it verbatim.

A Copilot host publishes the catalogue relative to the session channel
instead — `changeset/branch` rather than `<session>/changeset/branch`. Parsed
verbatim that becomes `file:///changeset/branch`, which addresses the client's
own filesystem, so the host answered NotFound for every static changeset and
the changes view stayed empty with no error surfaced.

Templates are now resolved against the session channel before use, and ones
that already carry a scheme are returned unchanged so hosts publishing
absolute templates are unaffected. The resolved URI is byte-identical to what
`buildBranchChangesetUri` and friends already produce.

Only the changes view was affected: the chat response summary derives the
turn changeset URI from the session itself rather than from the catalogue, so
it reported the same edits correctly throughout.

commit_message:
Do not cache a session-state subscription that failed to subscribe

Pinning a visible session is deliberately idempotent so that "re-running per
tick also recovers a subscription that could not be created earlier". That
recovery never ran: a subscribe that failed was stored in
`_sessionStateSubscriptions` like any other, so every later tick saw a live
subscription and returned early.

A failed subscribe is easy to miss because it settles via `onDidError` and
never fires `onDidChange` — the only event this consumer listened to — so the
session simply stopped receiving state, silently and permanently. Its
changesets never reached the adapter, which left the Changes view empty for
the rest of the session.

This is reachable whenever a session is addressed before the host has created
it: a cloud sandbox subscribes with the id Mission Control minted, roughly
700ms before `createSession`, and the host answers NotFound. The same applies
to the momentarily-disconnected remote the existing comment describes.

The subscription is now dropped when it errors, in both directions: bail
without caching if it already carries an error, and delete the entry if one
arrives later. The next tick then re-subscribes, by which point the session
exists.

commit_message:
chat: explain why Agent Merge turned itself off

Agent Merge could stop monitoring a session without saying anything. The
controller only wrote an `info` log line, so from the UI the feature simply
switched itself off with no explanation.

This is easy to hit on a session using `folder` isolation: the controller pins
the branch that was checked out when it was enabled, and any later `git
checkout` in that shared clone — from the user or another session — trips the
branch-changed guard and disables monitoring.

Report both transitions in the session transcript instead:

- "Agent Merge is on and watching `<branch>`." when it captures a branch.

  because the checked-out branch changed from `<a>` to `<b>`."

The notice is dispatched as server state only, so it reaches clients without
ever entering the agent's context, and is recorded through `AgentHostLocalTurns`
so it survives a reload like other host-injected turns.

All ten disable reasons now pair a stable English log detail with a localized
notice, so existing log output is unchanged.

center` floated the icon to the middle of a wrapped message. It now sits on the

commit_message:
Add shell init snippet generators for the SDK shell tool

The SDK built-in shell tool spawns a fresh no-rc shell per command, so the
user's Python environment and shell hooks are absent. Add the generators that
produce the init script text later sourced via ShellOptions.initScripts.

Three runtime behaviors shape the generated text: only the final exit status is
observed (so every script ends in a statement that always succeeds), bash
init-script stderr is discarded (so diagnostics go to stdout), and PowerShell
scripts are dot-sourced under $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop' (so the body is
wrapped in try/catch/finally).

The profile snippet sources ~/.bashrc and then replays marker-delimited managed
blocks that did not take effect. Stock rc files early-return in non-interactive
shells and tools such as conda append their init block below that guard, so
sourcing alone never reaches it. Replaying recovers shell functions such as
conda activate, which are never exported and so cannot arrive through the
inherited environment.

Publish Python activation and profile scripts for agent shell commands

Adds the workbench half: a synchronizer that resolves what a session's shell
tool needs and publishes it as script text on the session's config, which the
agent host then materializes and registers with the SDK.

Python activation is read from the environment-variable collection the Python
Environments extension publishes, scoped to the workspace folder that owns the
session. Only that extension may supply the value, since it becomes an
executable script. On POSIX the zsh variable is accepted as a fallback for
bash: the extension emits identical text for both, and the tool shell is always
bash. Fish and cmd are never used because their syntax would not parse.

Worktree-isolated sessions resolve through their originating project, since a
worktree path is not a workspace folder and activation commands carry absolute
paths.

Config is dispatched only when the value actually changes, and an empty list is
never published to a session that never had one. Session config is shared
across windows, so an unconditional write would let two windows overwrite each
other indefinitely.

commit_message:
agent host: anchor side chat forks at the last completed turn

A side chat can branch from a turn that is still running. The host asked the provider to
fork at that active turn, but an active turn is not yet in any provider history. Each
provider then used a different fallback: Copilot inherited all turns, Claude created a
fresh chat, and Codex made an error. Side chats were thus not available for Codex.

The host now anchors the fork at the last completed non-local turn, and the side chat
contribution adds only the turns that the fork cannot carry. Thus the side chat shows the
source conversation one time.

- Adds `resolveLastNonLocalTurnId` to the shared conversation context module. The host and
  the side chat contribution use the same helper, because the two values must agree.
- Anchors an active-turn side chat fork at the last completed non-local turn. The origin
  keeps the identifier of the turn that the user branched from.
- Removes the fork when no completed non-local turn is available, which makes a fresh chat.
  Turn execution uses per-chat queues, thus creation does not wait for the source turn.
- Limits the added context for an active turn to the trailing local turns, the active turn
  message, and the partial response.
- Enables side chats for Codex. No other Codex change is necessary.
- Divides the advertised side chat capability from the end-to-end replay coverage with
  `supportsSideChatsE2E`, which obeys the `supportsChatForkE2E` pattern. The Codex scenario

commit_message:
Back off GitHub requests instead of hammering a failing service

GitHubCredentialService kept no memory of failure: any failed identity
resolution cleared the current generation, so the next getCredential()
immediately reissued GET /user. A 401 amplified that, because
handleRequestError invalidates the generation and both
PullRequestResourceService and GitHubQueryService answer the resulting
onDidInvalidate by rescheduling every fragment and entity at now, each of
which asks for a credential again. When /user succeeded but real requests
kept being refused, that was an unbounded zero-delay loop for every user
with a subscribed pull request.

Add githubBackoff.ts with the shared escalating-delay math and a
GitHubBackoffGate that holds back attempts against a subject that keeps
failing. Callers wait rather than being rejected, so recovery stays
automatic and everyone queued behind one delay shares the attempt that
follows it. A working /user deliberately does not clear the record, since
it only proves identity resolution recovered; recovery is signalled by a
new token, a new host, or the record decaying while nothing fails.

Also unify the three other escalating retries onto the same helper, give
the capability probe a negative cache so an unusable result is not
re-probed on every fragment fetch, and stop trusting rate limit hints that
have already elapsed or that report the primary quota window for a
secondary limit.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: benibenj

commit_message:
Park primary 403 rate limits and unpin capabilities on re-auth

Address review feedback.

GitHub reports primary rate limit exhaustion as a 403 carrying spent quota
headers rather than as a 429, so that form skipped the refusal floor and
fell through to getDelay's remaining/resetAt fallback. When the reset was
missing or had already elapsed, the caller retried at once. Treat every
rate-limited refusal alike, keeping an authorization 403 unparked so a
credential problem still surfaces immediately.

The degraded capability record was keyed only by host and enterprise
version, yet a probe can be refused for the credential rather than the
host, for instance under SAML enforcement. Re-authenticating therefore
stayed pinned to the incomplete REST fallbacks for up to the fifteen
minute maximum. Scope the record to the credential generation so a new
credential probes at once, while successful host entries stay host-scoped.

commit_message:
Clip the notebook editor to the rounded editor card

Notebook editors are not children of the editor part. The widget is parented
to a host on the workbench that `OverlayLayoutElement` anchors over the part
and clips with `clip-path: content-box`. That host carries no radius, so the
clip is a sharp rectangle and `notebook.editorBackground` paints square
corners on top of the card. Text editors sit inside the part and are clipped
by it, which is why only notebooks show this.

Rounding the host makes its content box a rounded rect so the existing clip
follows the card. The widget tags the host with a marker class and keeps the
outer edge classes in sync from the part, the same way `OverlayWebview` drives
its rules in `floatingPanels.css`, so compact mode is covered as well.

Because the host spans the whole part rather than one group, this stays
correct when the editor is split. A group only loses a corner where it
actually meets a corner of the card, and a group in the middle keeps all four
square.

commit_message:
Load ESM extensions synchronously instead of queueing them

Replaces the load queue with Node's synchronous require(esm) path, which
Node already uses for this. Nothing else can run during a synchronous load,
so the timer covers the extension's own work by construction rather than by

Module graphs were already evaluated one at a time, so the queue was

setImmediate, which isn't an ESM lifecycle boundary and only held by
implementation detail.

ESM modules using top-level await can't load synchronously, so they still go
through import(). Node reports those with ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE before

commit_message:
Remove external session files from the agent host adaptor

The session adaptor derived an `externalFiles` observable that reduced file
edits across every chat and every turn of a session. It was the only reader of
`IChatFileEdits.allEdits`, and reading it forced a chat-state subscription for
every peer chat plus a parse of every completed turn.

Remove the feature and its three consumers, then simplify the parsing it was
holding up:

- Chat pills: `buildSessionArtifactSections` no longer takes external files.
- Agent feedback: a file is eligible unless it is an output-channel resource;
  the changes, external-changes and workspace-containment checks are gone.
- Changes view: the "Other Files" section, its widget, view model, CSS and
  fixture are removed, and the split view drops from three panes to two.
- `ISession.externalChanges`, `ISessionFile` and `SessionFileOperation` are
  removed from the session model.

With `allEdits` gone, per-chat parsing becomes lazy: a chat's state
subscription is only opened when its last-turn changes or customizations are
requested, so peer chats nobody reads cost nothing. Only the last turn is
parsed for file edits — earlier completed turns are never walked.

commit_message:
chat: don't prompt for workspace trust on internal agent-session folders (#332280)

* chat: don't prompt for workspace trust on internal agent-session folders

The send-time workspace-trust gate treated two internal folders as user
workspaces and prompted "Do you trust the authors of the files in this folder?":

- Workspace-less quick chats run in an internal scratch dir
  (~/.copilot/chats/<id>) that is persisted as the session's working directory.
  The gate now honors the `workspaceless` marker and skips the folder-trust
  check for such sessions.
- Worktree sessions run in a sibling <repo>.worktrees/<name> dir that whole-repo
  trust does not cover. Trust is now inherited from the already-trusted base
  repository at both the open gate (canOpenSession) and the send gate, guarded
  structurally to the repo's `.worktrees` sibling so an arbitrary working
  directory can never inherit trust just because its reported base repo is
  trusted.

Extracts getWorktreesRoot into platform/agentHost/common so the node agent host
and the browser trust gates share one implementation.

Fixes #332249

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: restrict worktree trust inheritance to strict descendants

Address PR review: the worktree structural guard used `isEqualOrParent`, which
is inclusive of equality, so a session whose working directory is exactly the
shared `<repo>.worktrees` container would inherit trust for the container. Since
workspace trust applies to all descendants, that would silently trust every
current and future worktree under it.

Introduce a shared `isWorktreeUnderRepository` helper in
platform/agentHost/common/worktreePaths.ts that requires a normalized strict
descendant of `<repo>.worktrees` (never the container itself), and use it at both
trust-inheritance sites (canOpenSession's helper and the send-gate handler).
Normalizing first ensures equivalent spellings (e.g. a trailing `.`) can't slip
the container past the check. Adds regression tests at both sites.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: add canOpenSession worktree-trust regression tests

Address PR review: the open-time trust-inheritance path in
SessionsService.canOpenSession had no focused regression test — existing tests
exercise the mount backstop and the send gate, so removing or reordering the
ensureSessionWorktreesTrusted call (inherit-before-prompt) would go uncaught.

Add two tests driving the real canOpenSession: a trusted base repo grants the
worktree before the folder-trust check (no prompt), and an untrusted base still
prompts for the worktree.

commit_message:
Fix Copilot client cold-start and Kerberos proxy handling (#332375)

* agent host: self-heal Copilot client cold-start config-changed abort (#332256)

* agent host: self-heal Copilot client cold-start config-changed abort

When a startup-config value changes while the Copilot SDK client is
starting, `_ensureClient` aborts the now-stale start and throws
`CopilotClientStartupConfigChangedError`. Because the next start uses the
current config, that abort is transient — but it was surfaced to session
restore, producing sticky failures such as "could not describe … yet" /
"Couldn't open session".

`_ensureClient` now transparently re-acquires the client once with the
current config. The acquire-and-retry sequence is shared across all
concurrent callers via `_ensureClientHealing`, so the retry budget is
global (bounded by `MAX_STARTUP_CONFIG_RETRIES`) rather than per caller,
and per-attempt coalescing in `_ensureClientOnce` is unchanged. No caller
observes the transient abort.

Related to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8895

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agent host: address review on the _ensureClient self-heal

Two findings from the automated review:

- Clear `_ensureClientHealing` from inside the async sequence's `finally`
  rather than a trailing `.finally()` on a separate chain. The external
  chain ran one microtask after awaiting callers resumed, so a caller that
  resumed on success and immediately re-entered `_ensureClient` (e.g. after
  `_stopClient()`) could be handed the fulfilled handle for an already-
  stopped client, bypassing the `_clientStopping`/`_client` guards. Clearing

* agent host: normalize empty Kerberos proxy SPN to avoid spurious restart

the applied-baseline (`_applyProxyEnv`) and effective-value (`_refreshProxy`)

genuinely-set SPN still restarts. Also name the actual trigger in the restart log
instead of the misleading `(none) -> (none)`.

commit_message:
Agent Host: apply multi-root capability change to open drafts without a reload (#332403)

* Agent Host: apply multi-root capability change to open drafts without a reload

The hidden `chat.agentHost.<provider>.multiRootEnabled` setting only took
effect after `Developer: Reload Window`. The renderer already mirrors the
setting to the agent host and the host re-advertises the
`multipleWorkingDirectories` capability (root state updates in the renderer),
but a not-yet-started provisional session computed its working-directory set
once at creation and was never re-scoped when the capability flipped, so an
already-open draft kept its single-root scope until the window was reloaded.

Subscribe to `rootState.onDidChange` in
`AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService` and re-run the working-directory
reconciliation for each open untitled draft, so a runtime capability change
re-scopes the draft (and its active-client customization scope) immediately.
Gated to untitled drafts because a started session's working directories are
the agent's fixed process root once the session has started. The shared
reconcile body is extracted into `_reconcileWorkspaceRootSet`.

Fixes #332335

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Agent Host: re-bind multi-root root-state listener on host start

The runtime multi-root re-scoping bound its `rootState.onDidChange` listener
once at construction. On desktop, `rootState` is a noop whose event never fires
until `startAgentHost()` creates the protocol client, and the host can restart
behind a fresh root state. A provisional service constructed before the host
started (for example when AI features are enabled mid-session) would therefore
listen on a dead event and silently miss the capability flip, degrading back to
the "reload required" behavior.

Re-bind the listener on every `onAgentHostStart` and reconcile once per (re)bind,
mirroring the existing pattern in `agentHostSdkSetupNotification`. Adds tests for
the host-start re-bind and the multi-root disable (ON->OFF) direction.

commit_message:

The launch skill drove Code OSS exclusively through raw `@playwright/cli`,
which means every agent hand-writes selectors for surfaces that

populated asynchronously.

`PlaywrightDriver` only uses that object for `windows()` / `close()` and

objects attach to the instance `launch.sh` has already started.

doc. `SKILL.md` now points at both from a short "Drive the UI" section and ends
up shorter than it was before this change.

`attach.ts` is a module rather than a documented snippet because three of its
steps are invisible from the type definitions and each fails in a way that does
not point at its own cause: the compiled output is CommonJS, `Quality` is a
`const enum` with no runtime value, and `window.driver` only exists when the
window was started with `--enable-smoke-test-driver`. Each is checked up front
and reported together with the fix.

Address review: poll for window.driver, and reject Code.exit() clearly

Two problems found in review.

`launch.sh` reports the endpoint ready as soon as `/json/version` responds,
which can be before the workbench has run `setupDriver()`. Sampling
`window.driver` once therefore reported a correctly launched instance as

with a rejection that explains what to do instead.

surface (a task aimed at the workbench silently misleads in the Agents window),

commit_message:
Keep locally provisioned sessions out of the list until they are real

A provider that creates a session remotely has to seed it into its cache
before connecting, so a later discovery pass reconciles against it instead of
creating a second entry. But the caller is still showing an optimistic
placeholder row for that same session until the first turn is dispatched, so
publishing the seed straight away listed the session twice for as long as the
environment took to wake (~8s observed).

Retiring the placeholder earlier is not an option: swapping when the session
merely exists hands the UI a session it cannot open yet and the view falls
back to the new-session screen. So the seed is now withheld from
`getSessions` instead, and revealed as the placeholder is retired. The reveal
is silent because the list re-reads on any change, letting a single event
swap both rows rather than listing both for a frame. Withheld sessions stay
reachable by resource, so opening one still works.

Separately, such a session could be evicted before it existed on the host.
Connecting triggers a reconciliation that prunes anything cached but not
listed, and the session id is minted before the host materializes the
session, so that first listing can legitimately omit it. Evicting there
dropped the row the user was looking at and bounced the view to the
new-session screen, re-adding the session seconds later.

Sessions seeded as provisional now resist that eviction until the host lists
them. The base provider already made this exemption for a sibling case, so
that is generalized into an overridable hook rather than adding a parallel
mechanism. The protection is bounded: without a deadline, a session the host
will never list becomes a permanent row that only a reload clears, trading a
visible flash for an invisible one.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: osortega

commit_message:
Do not strand a provisional session that never finishes connecting

Two ways the provisional guard could leave a session worse off than no guard
at all.

A failure after the seed — a rejected connect, or teardown while the sandbox
wakes — returned before the caller received a provider, so nothing could
publish the seed. Discovery does not rescue it either: a later pass finds the
entry already in the cache and only backfills its project. The session
existed remotely and was invisible until reload. It is now published on the
way out, while the provider is still the registered one.

The grace period also started at seed time, before connecting. Waking a
sandbox can take minutes, so a slow wake burned the whole period before the
host had said anything, and the first listing that omitted the session met an
already-expired deadline — evicting it immediately and recreating the
disappearance the guard exists to prevent. The clock now starts when a
connected host first omits the session, which is what the grace is actually
measuring.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Let agent host sessions tolerate hosts that differ from the client

Three ways a session against a host that is older than, or shaped
differently from, the client would fail outright.

Customizations changed from an `enabled` boolean to list-shaped `enablement`
in protocol 0.8.0. A host below that version expects the superseded shape and
rejects the whole request with `invalid params: missing field 'enabled'`,
which fails `createSession` and leaves no session at all. Client-published
customizations are now dropped for such a host, degrading to a session
without them. The gate is applied on both paths that publish an active
client, since reconciliation republishes it after creation.

A host can also address only certain working directory schemes. A remote
workspace may be the repository itself (`https://github.com/owner/repo`)
while the agent runs against a checkout on its own disk, and sending the
remote URI fails `createSession` with `unsupported scheme 'https'; expected
'file'`. Working directories the host cannot address are now dropped, falling
back to letting it choose its own. The host's reported `defaultDirectory`
names the scheme it can address, so this adapts per host rather than
hardcoding one.

Finally, a session the host has never heard of rendered "Couldn't open
session". A provider can legitimately address a session id before the host
knows it, with `createSession` bringing it into being, so the banner is now
suppressed for `NotFound` specifically. Genuine open failures still render,
which a test covers directly.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Judge working directories by the scheme the host receives

Remote folders travel as `vscode-agent-host:` wrappers on the client and are
unwrapped by `createSession` before being sent, so comparing the wrapper
scheme against the host's `defaultDirectory` dropped SSH and tunnel working
directories the host addresses perfectly well. Compare the unwrapped scheme
instead, which is what the host actually receives.

Also covers the reconciliation republish path, which had no test even though
an ungated republish is enough for an older host to reject the update.

Both tests were checked against the bugs they describe by reverting each fix
and confirming the matching test fails.
