commit_message:
tunnels: address review feedback on CLI-hosted tunnels

Four fixes from PR review:

- Agent host sharing hard-rejected every non-GitHub request, but
  `remote.tunnels.access.enableMicrosoftAuth` still exposes Microsoft
  accounts and the renderer prefers them when enabled. Carry `authProvider`
  through to `tunnel user login` instead of hard-coding GitHub.

- The pending service uninstall lived in one queued generation, so a
  concurrent sharing update could preempt the reconcile that owed it and
  leave the tunnel service installed. Persist it on the coordinator until an
  uninstall succeeds.

- `getTunnelName()` is also called while access is inactive, to compare the
  name this machine would use against a previously used one. Returning the
  running tunnel's name yielded undefined and permanently skipped the
  remote-extension recommendation. Expose the coordinator's intended name.

- Machine-status events were written straight to the emitting process's
  stdout, so when the editor attached to an existing tunnel the singleton
  server's token errors never reached it and token expiry was never
  surfaced. Events are now always generated, relayed to attached clients
  over a new singleton notification, and printed only where a process-global
  stdout toggle is set.

Also converts a runtime protocol-version assertion added by this branch into
a const assertion, which `clippy --all-targets` rejects as an assertion on
a constant.

commit_message:
agentHost: fix lost session customizations on materialization race

`AgentService.createSession` captured the provisional `SessionState` object
before awaiting the provider's initial customization snapshot. When the
provider materialized the session during that await,
`AgentHostStateManager.markSessionPersisted` replaced `entry.state`, so the
post-await write landed on an orphaned object and the customizations never
reached the authoritative state.

Apply the resolved snapshot through the existing
`AgentHostStateManager.setSessionCustomizations` API instead, which resolves
the session entry at call time. This is the same path the restore flow
already uses.

This is the cause of the flaky
"Timed out waiting for parsed plugin ...; last state: undefined" failure in
the Codex customizations provider integration test: Codex prewarms (and thus
materializes) in the background while `createSession` is awaiting the
snapshot, so the synced plugin was dropped and never surfaced in session
state.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Fix /clear in the Agents window (#330446)

The `/clear` slash command was silently doing nothing in the Agents
window: the current session was not marked as done and no new session
was opened.

`/clear` is registered once, in the shared workbench contribution, and
its handler is written against the classic workbench abstractions:

    agentSessionsService.getSession(sessionResource)?.setArchived(true);
    commandService.executeCommand(ACTION_ID_NEW_CHAT);

Neither call reaches the Agents window, which is a separate workbench
layer under `src/vs/sessions/` with its own session model:

- Archiving there goes through `ISessionsProvider` via
  `ISessionsManagementService.archiveSession()`. For agent-host sessions
  the provider owns its own cache and dispatches to the backend, so
  `IAgentSessionsService.setArchived()` never touches that state.
- `ACTION_ID_NEW_CHAT` resolves through `clearChatSessionPreservingType`,
  which branches on `isIChatViewViewContext(widget.viewContext)`. The
  Agents window builds its `ChatWidget` with an undefined view context,
  so it falls through to `widget.clear()` -> `viewOptions.clear?.()`.
  Only the chat view pane, chat editor and quick chat supply that
  callback, so the call is a no-op. The Agents window's real entry point
  is `ISessionsService.openNewSession()`.

Skip the core registration when running in the Agents window and add a
sessions-window `/clear` that uses the sessions services, following the
existing `/btw` contribution. The new command is silent so archiving does
not leave a stray `/clear` turn behind, and its description continues to
follow `chat.experimental.sessionArchiveActionWording`.

Co-authored-by: Mohammed Samir <51956976+SamirSaji@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
markdown: refactor: use setTaskCheckboxChecked for task toggles

The webview hand-rolled the task checkbox source edit: it looked up the list
item offset, computed the '[ ]' range and applied a StringEdit itself. That
logic now lives in EditorModel.setTaskCheckboxChecked, so delegate to it.

This also fixes toggling in read-only mode. The old handler bailed out on
model.readonlyMode and then routed through applyEdit, which is itself
read-only gated, so clicking a rendered checkbox in read-only mode did
nothing. Read-only in this editor means markers hidden and no text editing
while selection and copy still work - a rendering and interaction mode
rather than a document permission - so setTaskCheckboxChecked deliberately
bypasses that gate while applyEdit, applyEditForSelection and
materializePendingParagraph stay gated.

Requires a @vscode/markdown-editor release containing
setTaskCheckboxChecked (microsoft/vscode-packages#253).

commit_message:
agentHost: scope client customizations to session working directories

The synthetic vscode-synced-customization plugin was keyed only by session type, so one bundle identity was shared by every session of a provider and resolved against whatever workspace folder happened to be ambient. In the Agents window the ambient folder is swapped on every active-session change, so switching sessions re-resolved and re-published customizations to every live session and leaked one repository's files into sessions running in another.

Customization state is now keyed by the session's working-directory set. Scopes are refcounted and shared by sessions with identical roots, so each repository gets a stable bundle authority and nonce and the agent host's plugin cache stops re-materializing on every switch. Prompt enumeration takes an explicit root instead of reading the ambient workspace.

Publishing is consolidated into a single debounced per-session reconciler, replacing four separate dispatch sites that each compared against not-yet-updated session state and produced redundant actions. Publishing is gated on the scope having resolved so a freshly acquired scope cannot transiently wipe the host's customizations, an identical payload is never re-sent, and undefined-valued keys are omitted from published payloads so a value round-tripped through the wire compares equal to the one that produced it.

commit_message:
Move the Auto routing explanation into the response footer hover

A turn served by Auto shows "Auto" in the response footer, but nothing
there explained which model actually ran or how confident the router was.
That information existed as an `autoModeResolution` response part, but it
was only surfaced as a collapsible "Routed to <model>" widget wedged into
the response body, above the answer the user actually asked for.

Hovering the footer now leads with the routing decision -- "Routed to
<model>", the Auto description, and the reasoning label with confidence --
ahead of the existing token-usage breakdown, so the model name the user is
pointing at can explain itself. The inline collapsible part is dropped:
the explanation now lives on the label it describes rather than
interrupting the response. Turns Auto did not route are unaffected.

The "Learn More" link is left out of the hover since a transient hover
cannot reliably be moused into to follow it.

Report Auto in the response footer instead of the model it picked

A turn routed by Auto named the resolved model in its footer, so the

The footer's hover now explains the routing, so the pick is no longer

commit_message:
Gate the Auto routing explanation behind an experiment setting

Turns the footer-hover explanation into one arm of an A/B rather than the only
presentation. `chat.experimental.autoModeExplainability` selects between `inline`,
which names the picked model in the footer and repeats the decision as a collapsible
part in the response, and `footer`, which reports `Auto` and explains the pick only
on the footer's hover. The setting is experiment-locked at startup so the arm cannot
flip under already-rendered responses. This restores the inline content part the
previous commits removed, so the control arm is available again.

Also makes the router's classification optional end to end. Auto v2's `/auto`
response carries no label or confidence, and the converter previously coerced an
absent label to `fallback`, which renders as "Unable to resolve" - libelling every
Auto v2 turn. Only an unrecognized label degrades to `fallback` now; an absent one
stays absent and the detail line is dropped rather than the whole explanation.

Finally, the routing decision is now reported on every turn Auto serves, not just
the ones the router runs for: it is skipped after the first turn, gated off outside
panel chat, and bypassed when it falls back, but the UI still has to be able to say
which model is serving. AgentIntent resolves the endpoint before consuming the
decision so the report belongs to this turn rather than the previous one.

commit_message:
Declare VS Code's identity to the Copilot CLI for telemetry

The agent host spawns the Copilot CLI, and the CLI then describes itself in
the telemetry it emits: the client name falls back to `copilot-cli` and the
version fields report the CLI's own build. Sessions VS Code drove look the
same as someone running the CLI in a terminal, so the client identifiers on
an event can disagree about which surface produced it.

`createCopilotCliEnvironment` now takes an optional client identity and
passes it to the CLI as `COPILOT_CLIENT_INFO`, so the editor name, editor
version, surface name, and surface version all describe VS Code.

An inherited value is cleared rather than forwarded, since it would describe
whichever process launched VS Code rather than us.

commit_message:
fix(chat): stop observing prompt timeline host height

PromptTimelineWidgetContrib used a ResizeObserver on the full chat-session
host only to update the rail when its width changed. ResizeObserver also
activates when that host's height changes.

During a stacked input-height update, the deeper ChatInputPart observer
publishes height synchronously and ChatViewPane resizes the chat-session host.
Because PromptTimeline observes that shallower ancestor, Chromium cannot
deliver its notification in the same observation phase and reports a loop
with undelivered notifications.

Exact 1.132 restored-profile experiments isolated the observed target:
- baseline: warning in 3/3 runs;
- pet observer removed: warning in 3/3;
- ChatWidget list relayout removed: warning in 3/3;
- ChatViewPane relayout removed: zero in 3/3;
- PromptTimeline host observer removed with all relayout restored: zero in 3/3;
- explicit widget layout-width signal: zero in 3/3.

Replace the width-only host observer with ChatWidget.onDidLayout. Initialize
the rail from the current client width, then update it from explicit widget
layout widths. Sticky-only configurations no longer install a useless host
observer. Input height publication and stacked ViewPane relayout remain
synchronous and unchanged.

Validation:
- npm run typecheck-client
- npm run transpile-client
- 4 Playwright chat ResizeObserver tests
- 5708 chat unit tests
- exact 1.132 restored-profile differential

commit_message:
Bound signed-out models notification wait instead of replacing readiness

The signed-out Agent Host guidance gated on a fixed 5s delay, so a user who
already had a BYOK model configured could be shown "Choose how you want to use
Copilot" before the catalog settled and the notification self-corrected.

Restore the deterministic readiness gate and keep the timeout as a ceiling: the
notification shows as soon as local model readiness settles, or once the grace
period elapses. Readiness can stall indefinitely when a vendor named in the
user's BYOK config never resolves — no provider registers for it, or the
provider's model lookup hangs — so the wait stays capped.

Drop the shutdown tracking, which the registered MutableDisposable already
covers, and add coverage for the timer transitions the pure state function
cannot exercise.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: vritant24

commit_message:
Give each grace period wait its own budget

A timer armed while waiting outlived the transition to visible when readiness
settled first. Firing later marked the grace period elapsed for good, so a
vendor configured after that never returned to waiting; firing after a new wait
began handed that wait only the remainder of the old budget.

Clear the pending timer once the notification is visible so the next wait arms
its own. An already elapsed flag is preserved: clearing it there would flip the
state straight back to waiting and hide the notification it had just shown.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

`github.copilot.github.org` were silently absent on `invoke_agent` spans for
workspaces whose remote points at a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server
instance on a custom domain, while `github.copilot.git.branch` and
`github.copilot.git.commit_sha` were present on the same span. GitLab,
Bitbucket Server, and plain git servers were affected the same way.

`buildWorkspaceMetadata` derived the remote URL exclusively from
`getOrderedRepoInfosFromContext`, which only yields remotes that resolve to a
repo id via the `['github.com', 'ghe.com']` allowlist or the Azure DevOps
hosts. Branch and commit are read straight off `RepoContext` with no host
check, hence the asymmetry.

Add a `pickRemoteUrl` helper that prefers a remote resolving to a repo id, so
repositories that already reported a URL keep reporting the same one, and only
falls back to the highest-priority remote of any host when nothing resolves.
The fallback requires `parseRemoteUrl` to succeed, which admits only ssh, https
and http, keeping local remotes (`file://`, absolute and relative paths) out of
telemetry.

Rewrite `extractGitHubOrg` to delegate to `getGithubRepoIdFromFetchUrl` instead
of a `github.com`-only regex. This keeps the org attribute scoped to recognized
GitHub hosts while recovering it for `*.ghe.com` and ssh host aliases, which
the regex previously dropped. It remains absent for custom-domain GitHub
Enterprise Server, which cannot be distinguished from an arbitrary git host
without reading `github-enterprise.uri`.

Also fix an unrelated latent crash surfaced by the new tests: strategy 1 of
`getOrderedRemoteUrlsFromContext` asserted `remoteFetchUrls[0]!`, but a
push-only remote carries no fetch URL, so `undefined` escaped the declared
`Iterable<string>` and threw inside `parseRemoteUrl`.

The repo id allowlist, `getOrderedRepoInfosFromContext`, and every consumer
that depends on repo identity for GitHub API calls are left untouched.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#330239

commit_message:
fix: address review feedback on OTel remote reporting

Scope the host-agnostic remote to OTel emission. `WorkspaceOTelMetadata` now
carries both `remoteUrl` (any host, for OTel attributes) and
`recognizedRemoteUrl` (restricted to remotes resolving to a repo id). The two
consumers that forward a remote to GitHub telemetry rather than to the user's
own OTel exporter — `inline.trackEditSurvival` in userActions and
`fastApply/editOutcome` in MultiFileEditInternalTelemetryService — now read
`recognizedRemoteUrl`, so those channels collect exactly what they collected
before and the OTel fix carries no privacy expansion.

Reject loopback hosts in the fallback. `parseRemoteUrl` admits ssh, https, and
http, so scp-style syntax could smuggle a local filesystem path through an
accepted scheme (`git@localhost:/Users/alice/dev/repo.git`). Loopback hosts
(localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1, 0.0.0.0) are now skipped. Absolute
paths on routable hosts are still reported, since those describe the server's
layout rather than the user's.

Document that ssh host aliases normalizing to github.com or *.ghe.com also
produce `github.copilot.github.org`, in both the attribute reference and the
monitoring docs.

commit_message:
Add cache-aware history manager for customendpoint providers

Fixes #298554, #316187, #321551

On self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints (DeepSeek / DS4 / vLLM /
llama.cpp with disk KV), the server caches the key/value tensors of the
prompt prefix. A request sharing a long common prefix with the previous
request can reuse that cached work instead of recomputing it. In
practice the prefix was not stable across requests, so the cache almost
never hit.

Before (DS4 server log):
- 0 cache hits vs 532 misses; every request was a token-mismatch miss.
- Common prefix stuck at ~35k tokens while the live checkpoint grew to
  ~72k-82k tokens, forcing a full prefill of ~40k-50k tokens per turn.
- Disk KV cache (512 GB budget) perpetually full, churning 1,600+
  evictions.

Root causes in the request path:
1. Unstable tool ordering / schema additions mid-session mutated the
   prompt near the beginning, breaking token-position alignment.
2. History compaction and context updates shifted message boundaries on
   every turn, so the token prefix changed retroactively.
3. No per-conversation state, so nothing guaranteed the prefix stayed
   byte-for-byte identical across requests.

What this fixes (cacheAwareHistoryManager.ts, wired into
languageModelAccess.ts on the request path):
1. Freezes a common shared prefix - keeps system prompt + tool ordering
   stable and only ever appends new turns.
2. Small initial prefill - first request sends only system + latest user
   message (buildPrefill), so the KV cache starts from a minimal stable
   prefix.
3. Overlapping prefix across requests - per-conversation state keyed by
   a stable deriveConversationId records what was last sent; subsequent
   requests grow from it.
4. Discrete, predictable truncation - drops oldest non-system turns in
   blocks (truncateToBudget) instead of shifting message boundaries.
5. Isolates dynamic changes so mid-session tool/context shifts do not
   invalidate the cached prefix.

After (DS4 server log):
- Common prefix now tracks the live cache closely (99-99.6% overlap).
- Incremental prefills now occur (e.g. ctx=61446..61488:42 in 0.9s,
  ctx=69094..72432:3338 in 10s) instead of full prefills every turn.
- Whole log: 421 incremental vs 332 full prefills, 750 prompt done.

Remaining known limitations (server-side, not addressed here):
- reason=token-mismatch still reported on every live miss (580 total).
- Disk KV at 512 GB capacity causes constant eviction churn; every
  eviction shows hits=0.
- Full prefills still dominate wall-clock (108-159s each) on turns where
  the sent prefix does not exactly match the live cache.
author: stevescot

commit_message:
Address review feedback on cache-aware history manager

- Avoid orphan tool results by falling back to full history when the latest
  user message carries a tool result (prefill) and by dropping tool-call /
  tool-result exchanges atomically during truncation.
- Consult lastSentMessages to compute extendsLastSent and prefer a prefix
  that overlaps with the previous request so the KV cache still hits.
- Count all content parts (tool-call args, tool results, thinking, data,
  prompt-tsx) when estimating tokens instead of text-only.
- Budget against the computed tokenLimit rather than the full prompt capacity.
- Canonicalize tool definitions by name so ordering is stable across requests.
- Bound the per-conversation state map with LRU eviction.
- Honor the truncationPolicy (aggressive vs conservative) when trimming.
- Inject the running summary as a system message when summarizeDroppedTurns
  is enabled so it actually reaches the model.

commit_message:
mcp: fix: show one row per agent MCP server, not one per customization

A session can carry two customizations for a single MCP server. The agent host
publishes the declaration as a child of whatever declared it -- a plugin, or
the .mcp.json VS Code syncs into the agent -- and separately mints a top-level
customization for any server the SDK reports before that child can be resolved
by name. Once minted it stays for the session, so both remain in state.

Every consumer of getMcpServers saw both. In the servers list that meant the
same server rendered twice with contradictory status, because the child holds
the declaration and never leaves "stopped" while the top-level entry is the one
the host keeps current. It was worse than a repeat: the list's matcher refuses
to match when two candidates answer to one key, so the server's local row could
not adopt its session twin either, and both copies fell through as extra rows.

getPresentableMcpServerCustomizations drops a child that a top-level
customization already speaks for. The top-level copy wins because that is the
one the host treats as live: it carries the running state and channel, and its
id is what the host resolves for lifecycle and enablement. Position in the tree
is the signal rather than the shape of the minted id, which is the host's own
business and not something the workbench should be parsing.

Nothing else is collapsed. Two plugins that each declare a server of the same
name stay two servers. Only the presentation path dedupes; id lookups still
walk every customization, so an id from either copy continues to resolve.

Replaying 887 customization snapshots from a real session: 34 rendered a
duplicated server before this change and none do after, with no server lost.

commit_message:
mcp: refactor: match installed servers to running ones in one place

MCP servers are described by two independent models -- IWorkbenchMcpServer for
what is installed and configured, IMcpServer for what is actually running --
with no shared key between them. Correlating the two is how a row learns its
status and tool count, and it was being done ad hoc at each call site.

Collected here, with the rule stated once: a candidate is accepted only when
exactly one server answers to a key. Attributing one server's tools or failure
to another is worse than showing nothing, so ambiguity resolves to nothing.

The matcher indexes by every key a server answers to, so a list of rows can be
correlated in one pass rather than rescanning the runtime set per row.

commit_message:
mcp: feat: rework the MCP servers list around what a row needs to say

The list did not say what it already knew, and could not be acted on without
leaving it. Status was a colour-only icon in the far-right actions slot, and
only for some states: getMcpStatusPresentation returned no icon for Stopped and
the render path early-returned on a missing icon, so the most common state drew
zero pixels. Tool counts were cached and never shown. Turning a server on or
off was six context-menu items behind a `...`.

Three rules decide the result.

Say it only when it is not already said. Status is a word beside the name, and
appears only when it adds something: Failed, Sign-in needed, Starting, and
scope-qualified Disabled (Workspace) / (Session). Running and Idle are
lifecycle rather than news -- MCP servers start lazily, so "not running" is the
normal resting state and says nothing about health -- and a bare Disabled is
already stated by the switch beside it. The accessible name deliberately breaks
this rule and keeps a plain "Disabled", because a screen reader reads the row
label without the switch next to it.

One control, one meaning. The switch means enabled or disabled, durably. It
writes the profile layer, which also clears any workspace entry, and settles
the running session so a server just turned on cannot stay visibly off. Scoped
choices stay in the context menu, where they are spelled out rather than
implied by which row you happen to be on.

Sections answer one question: where is this defined? User, Workspace,
Extensions & Plugins, Built-in, ordered from the user's own choices outwards,
empty ones skipped. Because the header names the origin, rows stop repeating
it. Servers contributed by the agent join Built-in -- one that is there because
you are using Copilot came with the product as much as one shipping in VS Code
-- and name their product on the row, since that section now holds two. That
name is the leading origin rather than the "nothing else to show" fallback,
because a failing server fills the line with its error and would otherwise be
the one row that never says where it came from.

Line two carries origin, transport, and either the failure reason or the
description; the error replaces the description because when something is
broken that is the only thing on the line worth reading. Failures expose a
labelled Show Output, auth-required rows a Sign In. Tool counts read from cache
state, so they survive an idle server and read one step quieter when they are
last-known rather than live.

Fixes carried in this rework, each with a cause that is not guessable from the
symptom:

- Show Output was unclickable on exactly the rows that need it. The status
  autorun rebuilt the row's trailing slot about twice a second while rendering
  byte-identical content, and a DOM node replaced between mousedown and mouseup
  never receives a click. Rows now skip the rebuild unless something visible
  changed; the signature covers the static context too, or an edit to a
  server's description is dropped whenever its runtime state is unchanged.
- Every extension-provided server was labelled "Built-in": the origin check
  tested collectionId.startsWith('ext.'), but extension collection ids are
  <extensionKey>/<collId>.
- Choosing Disable produced "Disabled (Session)", because separate copies of
  the disabled-state rule disagreed. Durable outranks session now, from one
  shared resolver.
- getScopeOriginLabel dropped RemoteUser, leaving line two blank for those rows.
- Typing in the search box inflated the sidebar badge, and could produce
  duplicate rows once a local server was filtered out from under its runtime
  twin. Both now dedupe against the unfiltered list.
- The switch had no tabindex content attribute, so List.onTab could not find
  it, and rebuilding the trailing slot from inside the toggle handler destroyed
  focus -- a keyboard user could not toggle the same row twice.
- Two delayed hovers were registered on the same row container; the hover
  service keys them by element, so tearing one down removed the other's.
- Row accessible names were computed once at splice time and went stale, since
  status changes without a splice. They are observable now.

commit_message:
mcp: fix: repair the enablement path, and stop the pane re-deriving the join

Four frontier-model reviews of this branch (architecture, engineering,
correctness, UI/UX) found defects I had shipped. Each was reproduced in the
code before being fixed here.

The switch could be a dead control. An agent-host session row snapshots its
durable enablement when the list is built, `updateActiveSessionStatus` is a
plain call rather than an autorun, and `setMcpServerEnablement` wrote storage
without notifying anyone. So when the agent host already held the value being
written, nothing re-rendered and the switch stayed where it was -- every click.
The write now fires the customizations change the list already listens to.

The switch also destroyed a choice it never showed. It always wrote the profile
layer, and both profile writes delete the workspace entry, so toggling a
workspace-enabled row off and on again silently converted it to a global one.
The scope was only ever displayed while the row was off, so the user could not
see what they were losing. Writes now preserve the deciding layer, which is
also the layer that wins on read-back. `toggleContributionEnablement` -- added
by this branch, never called, and documenting exactly the rule the switch was
breaking -- is replaced by `withContributionEnabled`, which is used.

The detail pane re-derived the session join instead of sharing it. The matcher
is consuming and order-dependent; the pane built a fresh one with no claims, so
with two rows answering to one name it could adopt the server the list had
already given to another row -- the precise disagreement its comment claimed to
prevent. The row's claim now travels with the selection. The pane also never
subscribed to agent-host customization changes, leaving the one surface built
to explain status showing a stale one.

Rows claimed session servers against the *filtered* list, so hiding a row with
the search box released its claim for another row to pick up. This is the bug
already fixed for the sidebar badge and left in place for the rows; both now
claim over the same unfiltered sets in the same order, so they cannot disagree.

`renderTools` tore down and rebuilt the tool list on every tick of an autorun
that runs about twice a second while a server retries -- the same teardown bug
this branch fixed in the list, reintroduced in the pane two commits later, and
worse here because it cancels a selection the user is making over the text the
pane exists to let them read.

Status resolution had three copies: two branches calling the same method and an
inline third computing the same answer by hand. They agreed only by
coincidence, in the file whose own history says three copies had already
drifted with two of them wrong.

Also: the render signature omitted the label that names the buttons, the switch
and the row's accessible name; and a narrow pane spent its width on the
qualifier rather than the name ("Web S... - Disabled (Workspace)"), so the name
now keeps a floor and the status ellipsises after it.

Tests cover the corrected scope behaviour, including the off-then-on round trip
that used to be lossy.

commit_message:
agentHost: watch every git repo root for multi-root changeset freshness

The changeset file-watcher previously attached only to a session's primary
git repository root, so external edits (terminal, Editor Window, another
tool or app) to a SECONDARY repository did not refresh the all-folder
changes summary until the next turn boundary or re-subscribe.

Watch every unique git repository root of a session (resolved via
resolveSessionRepositories over getEffectiveWorkingDirectories), reusing the
existing shared, ref-counted, turn-suspended watcher machinery. On a change
to any watched root, refresh git state via the session's PRIMARY working
directory so branch/PR state is never mis-attributed to a secondary repo,
while the downstream all-folder summary recompute (already fanned out over
all repos) reflects the change. A non-git primary no longer suppresses
watching of the session's secondary git repos.

Per-session to repository-root state is generalized from 1:1 to 1:N;
active-turn tracking stays primary-only and releases all idle root
attachments during a turn. Adds multi-root coverage to
agentHostChangesetCoordinator.test.ts.

commit_message:
agentHost: make worktree removal idempotent for archived session deletion

Deleting an archived agent session failed with "git worktree exited with
code 128: fatal: '<path>' is not a working tree". Archiving a session already
removes and de-registers its worktree, so deleting the archived session tried
to remove it again; `git worktree remove` then fails because git no longer
tracks that path.

Make `removeWorktree` idempotent: when a removal fails, treat it as success if
git no longer registers the worktree (the removal goal is already met),
otherwise rethrow. Registration is checked against git's own worktree list
rather than the (truncatable, localizable) error text, reusing the same
`_isWorktreeRegistered`/`_canonicalizeWorktreePath` helpers as `main`.

Adds real-git integration tests for both the already-removed case and the
residual case where the directory remains but git no longer tracks it.

Refs #329982

commit_message:
Name the stuck tool on turnHung

`turnHung` reported only a count of in-flight tool calls, so a wedged
tool could be seen but not identified. That gap mattered most for
agent-host-provided tools: those never enter the session input queue, so
`agentHost.toolCallStalled` — which only fires for blocked tool calls —
cannot see them at all, and the count was the only signal available.

The turn tracker now retains each in-flight tool call's id and source
kind, and emits `toolId` / `toolSourceKind` on `agentHost.turnHung`:

  - `waitingOnUser`: the tool call gated by the blocking request. A
    result-confirmation prompt resolves to undefined, since the tool has
    already completed and the turn is waiting on the user reviewing a
    result rather than on a tool; an elicitation has no tool at all.
  - `runningTool`: the longest-running in-flight call. With several tools
    running in parallel there is no way to tell which is wedged, so this
    is a heuristic — `inFlightToolCallCount` travels alongside it, and
    filtering to a count of one gives unambiguous attribution.

Contributor refinement from `ChatToolCallReady` is mirrored from the tool
call tracker (reusing its now-exported `canRefineContributor`) so
`toolSourceKind` agrees between the two events for the same tool call.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: roblourens

commit_message:
Qualify toolId ambiguity and cover the unnamed-tool paths

Two fixes from PR review.

The `inFlightToolCallCount` description claimed a value above one always
means `toolId` is a best guess. That is only true for `runningTool`; when
`hangReason` is `waitingOnUser` the tool comes from the blocking request
and is exact no matter how many other calls are in flight. As written it
would have led analysts to discard valid blocker attribution. Both that
field and `toolId` now state which reason each rule applies to.

The two intentional `undefined` paths were undocumented by tests: a
pending-result confirmation (the tool completed and left the in-flight
set, so the turn waits on the user reviewing a result rather than on a
tool) and a chat-input elicitation (no tool at all). Both are covered
now.

Mutation-testing the blocker lookup showed a third gap: no test
distinguished "the tool the blocker gates" from "any in-flight tool",
because every existing case had at most one in-flight call. Added a case
with a long-running tool alongside a separate gated one, and verified it
fails when the lookup is replaced by first-in-flight.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_message:
Stop synced customization bundle churn in the Agents window

The synthetic "VS Code Synced Data" plugin
(`vscode-synced-customization:/<sessionType>`) is a single window-global
artifact shared by every session of a session type, identified by a
content-hash nonce. It was being built partly from workspace-scoped
inputs: `PromptsStorage.local` files and workspace-discovered MCP servers.

In the Agents window the workspace is not stable — the
`WorkspaceFolderManagementContribution` rewrites workspace folder 0 to
follow the active session. So focusing a session in a different worktree
rewrote the shared bundle, changing its nonce, which made
`ActiveClient.requiresRestart` destroy and resume every live session. That
destroy/resume-same-id sequence trips a race in the Copilot runtime that
silently orphans the session, so the UI spins forever.

Measured from a live 85-minute agenthost/AHP log with one Agents window:
one client emitted 20 distinct bundle identities and 44 re-syncs, with
flips as little as 1.8s apart and nonces repeatedly returning to
previously seen values. `.mcp.json`'s `${workspaceFolder}` cwd alone took
17 distinct worktree paths. Replaying the same recorded scans with this
change yields 1 distinct bundle identity and 0 re-syncs.

It was also a correctness bug, not just churn: sessions received their own
worktree's `.github/instructions` via the agent host's native per-session
discovery *plus* a second, stale copy of another worktree's via the
bundle.

Excluding workspace-scoped content from the window-global bundle is
lossless for everything the agent host discovers itself from each
session's own working directory (instructions, skills, agents, hooks). The
exception is workspace `.github/prompts`, which has no native equivalent
and no longer reaches Agents-window sessions; a slash command from an
unrelated worktree is worse than none, and delivering them correctly
requires bundling per session rather than per window. Regular workbench
windows are unaffected, since there the workspace is stable and genuinely
describes the session.

Also fixes a latent collision in `AgentPluginManager`: nonces are signed
32-bit hashes, and sanitizing stripped the sign, so `-N` and `N` mapped to
one directory while being tracked as distinct LRU entries — evicting one
deleted the other's materialized content.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: roblourens

commit_message:
Make includeWorkspaceStorage explicit at each registration site

The previous commit defaulted `includeWorkspaceStorage` to
`!isSessionsWindow` inside `registerForAgent`. That silently applied to the
*remote* agent host registration too, which also runs in the Agents window
and passes only `{ includeUserStorage: true }`.

Remote is the one registration where the client bundle is load-bearing
rather than redundant: the host runs on another machine and cannot natively
discover any of this client's files, which is exactly why it opts into user
storage in the first place. Inheriting `false` there was wrong in intent
even where it may be inert in practice.

The correct value depends on facts the service cannot see — whether the
window's workspace is stable, and whether the host can discover the files
itself — so the default is removed and both callers now state it:

- local agent host (runs in both window types): `!isSessionsWindow`
- remote agent host: `true`

No behaviour change for the local Agents-window case this PR targets.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_message:
Make the nonce directory mapping injective and migrate the cache

Addresses PR review feedback on the previous nonce fix.

The `{sanitized}-{hash32}` scheme was not injective. A nonce is an opaque
client token, so a client may legitimately send a value that is already
path-safe and identical to another nonce's generated key — for example
`28114114-<hash>`, the key produced for `-28114114` — which mapped both to
one directory while the LRU tracked them as distinct revisions. The 32-bit
hash could also collide outright. Either recreates the aliasing bug where
evicting one revision deletes another's materialized content.

Every nonce is now encoded reversibly as URL-safe base64 (whose alphabet is
already path-safe) under a reserved `n-` prefix, with a SHA-1 fallback under
a disjoint `h-` prefix for nonces too long to encode within the name limit.
Injectivity now holds by construction rather than by assumption: no raw
values are preserved and no two schemes share a namespace.

Changing the mapping also orphaned the previous layout: entries written by
an older build pointed at directories this build never looks up, so the old
trees were never removed and their LRU entries could never be cleaned up
(eviction targeted the new path instead). The cache file is now versioned;
on upgrade the superseded directories are removed best-effort and the LRU
starts empty, so plugins simply re-sync.

Also corrects documentation that claimed "nothing important is lost" while
the same paragraph documented the removal of workspace prompt slash
commands. Both the option docs and AI_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md now state that most
workspace types remain available through native discovery and treat prompts
as an explicit, user-visible exception.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_message:
Let piece tree's nodeAt and nodeAt2 return null

Both methods can fall through their search loops and did `return null!`,
so every caller was typed as receiving a `NodePosition` while actually
being handed `null`. `findMatchesLineByLine` already compensated with
explicit `=== null` checks, which the types made look like dead code.

Make the return type `NodePosition | null` and handle it at each call
site:

- `getCharCode` and `getLineCharCode` return `0`, matching what
  `_getCharCode` already returns when there is no adjacent node.
- `getValueInRange` and `getNearestChunk` return the empty string.
- `equal` reports the buffers as different, since a missing node means
  the other buffer ended early.
- `findMatchesLineByLine` returns the matches collected so far.
- `insert` and `delete` use `assertReturnsDefined`. Skipping a mutation
  would leave the buffer out of sync with the model, so these should
  keep failing, just with a meaningful error.

Every one of these sites previously dereferenced `null` and threw a
`TypeError`, so behaviour is unchanged whenever a node is found.

commit_message:
Fix terminal prompt duplication when resizing the terminal panel

The terminal resize debouncer sent a PTY resize on every layout event even
when the grid dimensions did not change, triggering SIGWINCH storms that
made shells redraw the prompt repeatedly. Additionally, the horizontal
resize debounce was too short (100ms) for shells such as zsh to finish
their prompt redraw, so consecutive resizes were processed with a stale
terminal width and duplicated the prompt line.

Skip resizes whose dimensions are unchanged and debounce horizontal
resizes for 300ms instead of 100ms.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#329946

commit_message:
Use modifier from mouse event in editor drag and drop

Read the trigger modifier directly off the drop mouse event in
`_onEditorMouseDrop` instead of tracking it across keydown/keyup, as
suggested in the discussion linked from the issue.

Dropping the tracked state also looks like it resolves a latched-flag
problem. `onEditorKeyUp` guarded its reset with `hasTriggerModifier(e)`,
but on the keyup of Alt/Ctrl itself that modifier already reads as
released, so `_modifierPressed` was never cleared there. It stayed true
from the first modifier press until the editor lost focus, which should
mean a later plain drag and drop copies the selection instead of moving
it.

The keydown/keyup handlers are kept for updating the mouse cursor, since
`_onEditorMouseDrag` only fires while the mouse is moving and would
leave the cursor stale if the modifier is pressed while holding still.

Fixes #58515
author: Manibharadwaj

commit_message:
Send the pointer up event out with the editor mouse drop

`emitMouseDrop` was passing `_lastMouseEvent`, which is only assigned on
pointer down and pointer move, so its modifier state was whatever it was
at the last pointer movement. `GlobalPointerMoveMonitor` did receive the
pointer up event but dropped it instead of handing it to the stop
callback, so a modifier pressed or released after the final movement was
not visible to drop listeners.

Forward the pointer up event through `stopMonitoring` (the parameter and
the `IOnStopCallback` signature already allowed for it, and
`GlobalEditorPointerMoveMonitor` already relays it) and send it out as
the drop event. The drop position keeps coming from the last pointer
move event, since the pointer up event is captured and its target does
not necessarily correspond to a position in the editor.

commit_message:
sessions: make the Agents window sign-in gate setting-driven

The window-level gate that forces GitHub sign-in before any of the sessions
UI is shown used to combine the `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable`
opt-in with per-type readiness: it stayed closed until some registered session
type reported `SessionTypeAuthRequirement.None`.

That second input resolves asynchronously — the local agent host only
advertises its agents at `AfterRestored`, well after the setup widget has
decided — so the gate raced the very modal it was meant to suppress, and every
consumer needed lifetime-scoped re-checks to retire a dialog it had already
raised. It also duplicated a judgement the per-type gate already makes
(`getSessionTypeAvailability()` → `SignInRequired`), with a standing TODO about
the two predicates drifting.

Drop the readiness input. The window gate now reads the opt-in alone, and
per-type on-demand sign-in carries the actual work once the window is open —
which is the right altitude for a fact that changes as credentials come and go.

- `observeUsableWithoutGitHub()` → `observeAllowSignedOutWhenUsable()`, no
  longer taking `ISessionsManagementService`; both `SessionsSetUpWidget` and
  `TitleBarAccountWidget` lose that dependency.
- Extract `shouldForceGitHubSignIn()` so the window gate is one named,
  unit-testable predicate.
- Rename `IAccountTitleBarStateContext.usableWithoutGitHub` →
  `allowSignedOutWhenUsable`; it carries the opt-in now, not a usability fact.
  `IDiscoveredConfigNudgeContext.usableWithoutGitHub` is unchanged — that one
  really is provider-derived.

No behavior change while the opt-in is off (the default), which remains
today's mandatory-sign-in behavior.

commit_message:
agentHost: perf: stop repairing worktree roots while listing

`listSessions` ran a data migration that re-derived every session's
repository root through `git worktree list --porcelain`, to repair roots
persisted by builds older than #328375. On a large catalogue that spawned
hundreds of Git processes and made the first listing take ~52s, and the
Agents window renders nothing until it returns.

A listing API should not be a migration path: this one had unbounded
fan-out, no completion guarantee, and a write side effect on the critical
render path.

Nothing in the host needs it. `WorktreeIsolation._readWorktreeMetadata`
already canonicalizes the persisted root and writes it back, and every
host-side consumer reads through it: archived resume, worktree removal,
archive cleanup, unarchive recreation and `resolveWorktreeProject`. Within
the host, the listing's project label was the only consumer that did not.

#328375's stated rationale — that an archived session may never reach that
reader — is true as far as it goes, but its only consequence is a wrong
sidebar group label on a session the user never opens. That does not
justify spawning a Git process per session on every listing.

So use the persisted root as-is. Opening a session still heals it:
`_withWorktreeProject` resolves the worktree project, which canonicalizes
and re-persists the root, and `listSessions` overlays the live summary, so
every later listing reports the healed value from two independent sources.
The heal is deferred rather than immediate — restore deliberately emits no
`sessionAdded`, and the renderer ignores `project` on `sessionSummaryChanged`,
so the corrected root reaches the UI on the next `listSessions` refresh,
which is turn- or reload-driven rather than periodic.

This is a compatibility tradeoff, not a free removal. Until a legacy
session is first opened, its sidebar group is named after the linked
checkout, and renderer surfaces that read `folders[0].root` — "New Session"
on a workspace section, and the customization writes on a just-opened
session — can target that checkout. Those surfaces derive a Git root from a
display field and so never read through the repairing reader; that is a
pre-existing defect this change makes easier to hit, tracked separately.
The target was a checkout of the same repository when it was persisted, and
session creation re-canonicalizes the root, so a new session is still filed
under the primary checkout. The merge-into-parent command cannot reach it
at all: its only menu is gated on `ContextKeyExpr.false()` and it registers
no `f1` entry. Also accepted: a root persisted without its branch (only
reachable via a partial metadata write) used to be repaired by the listing
and now never self-heals; the reader's JSDoc records that.

Measured on an 804-session catalogue: 49 sessions carry a worktree root
across 4 distinct roots, and all 4 were already primary checkouts — the
migration re-verified correct data on every listing.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: never treat a git directory as a repository root

`git worktree list --porcelain` does not always answer with a working
tree. Inside a submodule it reports the superproject's git directory,
and for a worktree of a bare repository it reports the bare directory:

    inside /super/vendored (a submodule):
      git rev-parse --show-toplevel  -> /super/vendored
      git worktree list --porcelain  -> /super/.git/modules/vendored

WorktreeIsolation persisted that value as copilot.worktree.repositoryRoot,
and getWorktreesRoot() derives the worktrees directory from it, so a
worktree-isolated session created from a submodule checkout was
materialized at /super/.git/modules/vendored.worktrees/<name> — inside the
repository's own git directory. The same value also grouped the session
under that path and fed removeWorktree and archived-session resume.

Add isGitDirectoryPath() and refuse such an answer in
_resolvePrimaryWorktreeRoot, so creation and resume-repair inherit the
guard from one place; it now also reports whether git genuinely resolved a
root, so a fallback is never persisted over a stored value. Decline the
same shape in adoptExistingWorktreeMetadata and in the list-time repair.

The predicate is a conservative refusal by name: a --separate-git-dir
target can be named anything and is deliberately not recognised.

commit_message:
agentHost: perf: stop re-deriving worktree roots on every listing

Reloading the Agents window could leave session details unavailable for tens of
seconds while the first `listSessions` handled hundreds of `git worktree list
--porcelain` launches.

Listing repairs repository roots written before the worktree-identity fix, and
that repair asks Git which worktree is primary. Git is the right authority for
that question, so keep asking it — but almost never. Three things stopped the
answer from being reused.

The resolver already learns a repository's entire membership from one listing,
and then threw it away: a 100-entry bound evicted exactly the siblings it had
just recorded, so practically every session launched Git again. The entries are
the membership Git reported, so any bound only decides how many worktrees it
takes to reproduce the storm — a capacity that silently chooses between one
subprocess and hundreds. The cache is unbounded instead, holding two short
strings per checkout that exists on disk; fifty thousand of them cost 7 MB.

Those entries also have to match the next lookup. Git reports resolved paths
while a session persists the path it was created with, so `/tmp/x` and
`/private/tmp/x` were separate keys for one worktree and every lookup missed.
Keys are canonicalized, which doubles as an existence check: a checkout that is
gone cannot be canonicalized, and Git could only have been launched to fail on
it.

Finally, a repaired root is stamped, so the migration costs one resolution per
session ever rather than one per listing, and a resumed session no longer
re-derives it either. The stamp carries the resolution's version and the exact
root it certifies, so rewriting the root through any other path invalidates it
and a future correctness fix can re-migrate. Only a root Git actually answered
for is certified: a fallback is the raw checkout root, which is the value this
migration exists to replace. Roots Git could not describe stay unstamped and are
retried, bounded by a short-lived negative entry rather than a permanent one,
because the host outlives any window.

Persisting the repair is no longer awaited, and one listing's total repair time
is capped; leftovers stay unstamped and are picked up by a later listing.

Against a real 301-worktree repository, 300 concurrent sessions go from 201 Git
launches and 13.9s to one launch and 74ms. A catalogue's cost is its shape
rather than its size, so that single repository is the easy case: 530 sessions
spanning 20 repositories, 30 checkouts Git can no longer describe and 200 deleted
ones cost 50 launches and 465ms on a cold host — one per repository and one per
undescribable checkout — and none at all thereafter, which the stamp then carries
across restarts.

Fixes #329880

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: ulugbekna

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: keep listing repairs durable, bounded and unfrozen

Review of the implemented change found three defects, each invisible from the
design and each undoing part of what it claimed.

The repair never reached disk. Listing wrote the repaired root and its stamp
without awaiting them, then released the session database on return; releasing
the last reference closes it, and a write that has only been started is rejected
once closed. Against a real database both writes fail, so the stamp never landed
and neither did the repair — worse than before this change for exactly the
archived sessions listing exists to serve. The writes are awaited now, which the
budget accounts for. The test that was meant to cover this could not: the double
it writes through keeps a map in memory and its reference releases into a no-op,
so a lost write still looked persisted. It now models a released database, and
rejects a write that arrives after one.

The budget bounded nothing. Sessions are repaired concurrently, so all of them
read the clock at once, before any Git had run, and all passed. The check now
sits where the cost is, immediately before a launch, and the clock starts at the
first launch rather than at the start of the listing — otherwise enumerating
sessions and reading their metadata spent the time meant for Git, and the
largest catalogues, which need repair most, would have got none. A near-empty
budget now stops a 530-session catalogue after one launch instead of running all
fifty.

Nothing the resolver learns outlives the pass that learned it. Git reports "this
is not a worktree" and "Git could not run just now" identically, so remembering a
failure froze a wrong project for every window until the Agent Host process
restarted — a minute of it by the clock, and reloading the window did not help
because the host outlives windows. Successes were kept forever, which is no safer
now that a listing certifies what it resolves: a worktree path reused by another
repository, or a primary that moved, would be answered from memory and stamped.
Both now live in the pass, so a listing still spends one launch per repository
and the next listing is free to disagree.

Fifty launches and 432ms for that catalogue are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: ulugbekna

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: report a checkout absent only when it really is

Canonicalizing a checkout doubles as the check that lets listing skip Git
entirely for one that is gone. It caught every error to decide that, so an
unreadable parent, a symlink loop or a volume briefly away all read as absence —
and Git, the actual authority, was never asked about a checkout that was really
there.

The filesystem does distinguish these: absence is ENOENT or ENOTDIR, and
everything else means the question went unanswered rather than answered "no".
Only the former now reports absence; anything else falls back to the path as
given so Git still gets asked and can fail on its own terms. A thrown error is
not an answer either, so the resolver's own guard falls back the same way instead
of inferring absence from it.

Nothing here could freeze a wrong root — an unresolved checkout is never stamped
— but it could have skipped a repair for as long as the condition lasted.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: ulugbekna

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: never persist a root the stamp will not certify

Verification of the stamp invariant turned up a case that satisfied it and still
made things worse. Git answers a submodule with its git directory rather than a
working tree, and the stamp refuses to certify that. But the root itself was
written anyway, so listing replaced a session's repository root with the git
directory and left it unstamped -- a value every later listing had to derive
again, for exactly the sessions that can never converge. Refusing to certify a
root now also means refusing to store it, on both the listing and resume paths,
which leaves the stored value untouched and the session grouped where it was.

The refusal also claimed more coverage than it had. Bare repositories answer with
the bare directory, whose name ends in `.git` without ever being a `.git`
segment, so those were certified. They are declined now too. A
`--separate-git-dir` target can be named anything, so it cannot be recognised by
path at all; the comment no longer implies otherwise.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: ulugbekna

commit_message:
agentHost: test: pin that a stamp certifies only a stored root

The stamp is issued alongside the root it vouches for, so it can land when that
root's write does not. Nothing durable goes wrong, because the stamp embeds the
exact root and a mismatch reads as uncertified -- but that is the whole reason
the value is in the stamp, and it was only argued, never pinned.

Now a failing root write is exercised directly: the stored root is left alone,
the stamp that survived certifies nothing, and the next listing repairs the
session instead of trusting it. Replacing the stamp with a bare version marker
fails this test, which is the point.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: ulugbekna

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: never adopt a git directory as a repository root

Declining to certify a git directory covered listing and resume, but not the
place the value originates. Creation resolves the primary worktree the same way
and persists whatever Git answers, so a worktree-isolated session started from a
submodule checkout stored `<super>/.git/modules/<name>` as its repository root
before any listing ran -- and the worktrees directory is derived from that value,
so the session's worktree was created inside the repository's own metadata.

The refusal now lives at the resolution site, so creation, resume and adoption
all get it: when Git answers with a git directory, the caller keeps the checkout
root it already had, which is what `rev-parse --show-toplevel` reports for a
submodule anyway. Adoption declines outright, having nothing to bridge to.

Deleting the list-time repair would not have fixed this, because creation writes
it too.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: perf: resolve primary worktree roots without spawning git

Reloading the Agents window could leave session details unavailable for tens
of seconds while the first `listSessions` handled hundreds of `git worktree
list --porcelain` launches.

Listing repairs repository roots written before the worktree-identity fix, and
that repair asked Git which worktree is primary. Neither cache in front of it
could absorb the work: the AgentService cache is keyed by session, so every
session in a listing missed it, and the resolver cache is keyed by checkout
path, where each session again brings its own. Only the sibling paths recorded
from a successful listing could be shared, and a 100-entry bound evicted those
before the next session reached them. Practically every session therefore
spawned Git, serialized behind the resolver's sequencer.

Git's on-disk layout already answers the question: a primary worktree owns a
`.git` directory, and a linked worktree's `.git` file leads through `commondir`
back to the primary worktree's git directory. Read that instead, and keep Git
as the fallback for layouts it cannot describe, such as bare repositories and
submodules. Resolving 28 real worktrees drops from 484ms and 28 processes to
10ms and none, with identical results.

Both caches are also sized to hold a full session catalogue so a repeat listing
re-reads nothing.

Fixes #329880

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: only answer worktree layouts git would recognize

Review of the previous commit surfaced a wrong-value class the on-disk
resolution introduced. Git accepts a `.git` directory only when it actually
holds a repository and keeps searching upwards otherwise; the walk here
accepted the name alone. A checkout whose worktree link had been replaced by an
empty `.git` directory therefore reported *itself* as the repository root, and
because that answer is truthy it also consumed the caller's fallback to the
persisted root. Listing then wrote it back, regrouping the session under its own
worktree folder — the very defect this metadata exists to prevent, and not
self-healing.

Two neighbours behaved the same way: a bare repository, which owns no worktree,
was climbed out of and answered with whatever checkout happened to contain it,
and a `core.worktree` redirect was answered with the repository directory rather
than the detached working tree.

Validate a `.git` directory the way git does, treat a bare repository as a
boundary, and defer to git when `core.worktree` is in play. Differential testing
against `git worktree list --porcelain` across 17 layouts — submodules, bare and
nested-bare repositories, separate-git-dir, damaged and stray `.git`, moved
primaries, symlinks — now shows no divergence.

Also stamp a repaired root, so the migration costs one resolution per session
ever instead of one per listing. That retires the in-memory cache the previous
commit had merely enlarged, and leaves an unresolvable root unstamped so a later
listing can still repair it.

Canonicalize the linked-worktree answer as well: git records a resolved path
there, but a restored link need not, and Windows only settles on-disk casing
through a real path lookup. One spelling per repository is what keeps sessions
grouped together.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: ulugbekna

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: never certify a repository root git did not confirm

Review of the stamp found that it certified roots nobody had confirmed.
Materialization resolves the primary worktree with the selected checkout as its
own fallback, and that fallback is exactly the linked-checkout path the listing
repair exists to correct. The resolver collapsed "resolved" and "fell back" into
one return value, so a transient git failure during session creation persisted
the wrong root and stamped it as canonical. Listing trusts the stamp, so the
repair would skip that session for good: a passing failure frozen into a
permanent one, reinstating the bug #328375 fixed.

Report whether the repository actually answered, and stamp only then. An
unconfirmed root stays unstamped and is repaired by a later listing, which is
the behaviour that existed before the stamp.

Certify on the resume path too, so a session repaired while being read does not
make listing derive the same answer again.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: ulugbekna

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: do not read a refused path as an absent one

A checkout the filesystem declines to describe was treated as one that is not
there. Every probe swallowed its error, so an unreadable `.git` looked absent,
the search climbed past it, and the enclosing repository was returned as the
session's root. Git refuses outright in that situation. Listing certifies what
it is given, so a momentary permission or mount failure would have been frozen
into a permanent mis-grouping.

`realpath` and `stat` already distinguish the two: `ENOENT` and `ENOTDIR` mean
absent, while `EACCES`, `EIO`, `ELOOP` and an unmounted volume mean the question
went unanswered. Report absence only for the former and let anything else defer
to git, which is the one component entitled to decide.

Verified against a `chmod 000` checkout inside a repository: previously the
enclosing repository was returned where git returns nothing, and now both agree.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: ulugbekna

commit_message:
agentHost: test: prove the repaired root survives database release

The in-memory session database accepts writes forever and its reference
disposes to nothing, so a listing repair that outlived its database reference
would still look successful under test. The real database rejects writes once
its last reference is dropped, and listing drops that reference the moment the
repair returns, so nothing here was actually pinned down.

Model the release: defer the write the way the real sequencer does, then refuse
it once released. Deferring is the part that matters. A synchronous check still
passed with the writes made fire-and-forget, because the write began before the
reference was dropped and only its completion would have failed.

Confirmed the test fails when the awaits are removed and passes with them.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: fix: never let the stamp outlive the root it vouches for

The stamp was written alongside the repository root rather than after it. The
writes are independent, so a failed root write with a successful stamp left the
previous value certified as canonical, and listing skips a stamped session, so
the repair could never correct it.

Write the stamp last and only once the root it vouches for is stored. Nothing
else about the metadata write changes.

The new test fails when the two are issued together, which is how the gap was
found.

commit_message:
Add generic agent turn hang telemetry to the Agent Host

A hung agent turn was previously only detectable as the *absence* of
`agentHost.turnCompleted` after `agentHost.userMessageSent`, which does
not surface on dashboards. Add a positive signal.

`AgentHostTurnTracker` now arms a `disposableTimeout` watchdog per
in-flight turn, debounced by any turn-scoped activity. On expiry it
classifies the quiet state and reports `agentHost.turnHung`:

  unexpected: `noProgress` (nothing was ever observed for the turn - the
              signature of a lost turn), `stalledAfterProgress`
  expected:   `waitingOnUser` (an input request is outstanding),
              `runningTool` (a tool call is in flight, which also covers
              subagents)

Each reason is reported at most once per turn and the watchdog re-arms
for at most six quiet windows, so a permanently dead turn cannot produce
unbounded events or timers. A paired `agentHost.hungTurnCompleted` fires
when a previously hung turn later completes, so permanent hangs can be
separated from merely slow ones.

`AgentSideEffects` feeds the watchdog: turn-scoped protocol actions as
activity, tool call start/complete as in-flight state, and session input
requests as blockers. Turn tracking is also cleared on channel teardown
and on truncation, closing a pre-existing leak where entries for turns
that never completed lived forever.

The existing `agentHost.toolCallStalled` telemetry is kept as-is: it is a
more specialized signal (it carries tool identity and only covers tool
blockers), and keeping it avoids breaking existing queries.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: roblourens

commit_message:
Correct hang classification for client tools and denied confirmations

Two fixes from PR review, both cases where the watchdog would misstate
what a turn was waiting for.

Client tool execution is not a wait on the user. The protocol defines
`SessionInputRequestKind.ToolClientExecution` as delegated running work
rather than a prompt — the call has already cleared its confirmation
gate and is simply executing elsewhere — and the session reducer's
`awaitsUser` predicate excludes it for exactly this reason. Recording it
as a user blocker classified every long-running client tool as
`waitingOnUser` with `blockedOn: toolClientExecution`. Outstanding
requests are still tracked for bookkeeping, but only user-blocking kinds
drive `waitingOnUser` and `blockedOn`; client execution is represented by
the in-flight tool set and so reports `runningTool`. That predicate is
mirrored rather than imported because the reducer file is generated.

A denied tool confirmation is terminal. The reducer moves the call to
`cancelled` and ignores any later completion for it, so the tool call id
stayed in the turn's in-flight set forever and a subsequent hang was
reported as an expected `runningTool` instead of `stalledAfterProgress`.
Denials now clear the entry on both the client (`handleAction`) and
agent (`_dispatchActionForSession`) paths, since the action arrives on
both.

Both new tests were verified to fail against the pre-fix code.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_message:
agent host: resolve session pull requests by remote branch and head commit

Pull request detection keyed the GitHub lookup on the *local* branch name,
so a session working on a pull request head under a differently named local
branch was never associated with its pull request. A branch created with
`git switch -c <local> FETCH_HEAD` and pushed with an explicit refspec has
no upstream and no remote branch of that name, so
`pulls?head=<owner>:<local>` correctly returned nothing on every lookup.

Resolve the head branch from the upstream tracking ref when there is one,
mirroring what the create-PR handler already does, and fall back to looking
the pull request up by the commit at HEAD when the branch name matches
nothing. The commit identifies the pull request regardless of how the branch
is named locally, so it also covers branches that track nothing at all.

`commits/{sha}/pulls` lists every pull request that *contains* the commit,
so only pull requests whose head is exactly that commit are considered, and
a commit shared by several of them reports none rather than guessing.

Also cache pull request listings alongside their ETag: caching the validator
without the payload made a revalidated (304) route look empty, which could
drop a known pull request after switching branches away and back.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: benibenj

commit_message:
Fix `<`/`>` incorrectly colored/paired as brackets inside `<<=`, `>>=`, `>>>=`

Bracket-pair colorization scans text directly for `<`/`>` characters
wherever they're configured as colorized brackets (TypeScript, TSX,
C++, C#, Java, Rust, etc.), independent of the syntax grammar. That
scan had no guard against `<`/`>` being part of a longer operator
token, so it matched the first `<`/`>` inside `<<=`, `>>=` and `>>>=`
regardless of context, causing false "unmatched bracket" coloring and
false pairing across unrelated statements.

Excludes `<`/`>` from bracket matching only when they unambiguously
form `<<=`, `>>=`, or `>>>=`, using lookahead only (no lookbehind).
This is required because the engine has two text-scanning strategies
- one re-slices per match, the other (FastTokenizer, used for a
file's very first paint before background tokenization completes)
scans continuously - and a lookbehind-based guard passed under the
first but broke nested generic matching (Array<Array<string>>) under
the second.

Fixes #329789

commit_message:
agentHost: describe entry persistence with a static config table

Remote agent host entries were persisted by branching on
`RemoteAgentHostEntryType` in a dozen places, and "this type is not
persisted" was expressed by `entryToRawEntry` returning `undefined` and
being dropped by `.filter(isDefined)`. Registering a tunnel therefore
still called `updateValue('chat.remoteAgentHosts', ...)` with a
byte-identical array. On Windows that write can fail with EPERM when the
atomic `settings.json.vsctmp` rename hits a file lock, and because the
write was awaited inline in the connect path, a healthy tunnel was
reported as a failed connection and torn down.

Collect the per-type differences into a static
`IRemoteAgentHostEntryTypeConfig` table, modelled on
`IPluginFormatConfig`: each connection type declares its durable `store`,
whether it is self-connecting, whether its address is normalized, and how
it converts to and from its persisted form. The table is an exhaustive
mapped type, so adding a connection type is now a compile error rather
than an entry that silently vanishes on save.

This absorbs `entryToRawEntry`, `rawEntryToEntry` (including its
flat-shape SSH sniffing) and the `getEntryAddress` switch, and collapses
the duplicated upsert/merge and configuration-scope helpers.

Two fixes follow from the model:

- Entries whose store is `runtime` (WSL, tunnel, cloud sandbox) are never
  written, so connecting or disconnecting them performs no I/O at all.
  Settings and storage writes are additionally skipped when the value is
  unchanged.
- `_reconcileConnections` no longer disconnects runtime-registered
  connections. `desired` is built only from persisted entries, so any
  write to either store - including an unrelated SSH connect - used to
  tear down live tunnel, WSL and cloud sandbox connections.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: connor4312

commit_message:
agentHost: address review feedback on the entry type config table

Persist both durable projections from the merged entry set again. Entries
are keyed globally by normalized address, so a replacement can move an
address between stores; writing only the destination store left the source
row behind for `_getConfiguredEntries` to overlay back on top, so replacing
an SSH entry with a WebSocket entry silently kept the stale SSH row and the
new connection never started. Each store keeps its own unchanged-value
guard, so this does not reintroduce redundant writes. The legacy SSH
migration now writes the whole merged set once instead of one store at a
time.

Seed `_names` and `_tokens` from the runtime registrations before
overlaying configured entries. Reconciliation clears both maps and
repopulated them only from persisted entries, so once runtime connections
stopped being disconnected they survived with their address reported as
their name, which downstream provider reconciliation treats as a rename.

Model the config table as a discriminated union so a durable store
requires both converters and `runtime` forbids them. The invariant was
previously only documented, leaving the non-null assertions in the
persistence paths unguarded against a future config that declares a store
without converters.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Stop auto-update policy from being overridden per extension

Turns out that once org policy locks extensions.autoUpdate, there
were still three ways around it: the per-extension "Auto Update"
checkbox writes to a storage list that the actual update check
happily honors regardless of policy, "Disable Auto Update for
Extensions" just pins every installed extension directly (metadata
write, doesn't even go through config), and the publisher-level
toggle lets someone opt back in when policy forces it off. So an org
turning this on to guarantee security patches land could have it
quietly undone extension-by-extension.

Added a small helper (isAutoUpdateConfigLockedByPolicy) plus a
context key for it, and used both to make the update-check ignore
those override lists while locked, make the bulk enable/disable
command a no-op, and grey out the checkboxes so the UI stops
pretending you can change something you can't.

Fixes #325909
author: RajeshKumar11

commit_message:
Fix extensions.allowed schema flagging valid version arrays as invalid

The `extensions.allowed` JSON schema had two patternProperties regexes
anchored only at the end ($), not the start. This let a key like
`ms-vscode.cpptools` match both the extension-id pattern and the
publisher-only pattern (by matching just the `cpptools` suffix against
the latter). Since JSON Schema requires a value to satisfy every
matching pattern, an array value like ["1.31.4"] - valid under the
extension-id pattern - failed against the publisher-only pattern
(which only allows boolean/string), producing a false "Incorrect
type" warning in settings.json.

Anchor both patterns with ^ so they're mutually exclusive, and reuse
the now-identical EXTENSION_IDENTIFIER_PATTERN constant instead of
duplicating it inline.

Fixes #327194
author: RajeshKumar11

commit_message:
feat(byok): add gemini apiType to Custom Endpoint provider

Adds a fourth Custom Endpoint apiType, 'gemini', for endpoints that
speak the Gemini generateContent REST format (the official Google
Generative Language API, or a compatible gateway/proxy).

The Gemini SDK builds its own request URL from a base URL and API
version rather than a fixed path suffix, so URL handling for this
type runs in the opposite direction from the other three: it
normalizes a user-supplied URL back down to a base instead of
appending a path. resolveGeminiBaseUrl() implements that, stripping
a trailing version segment and any models/...:generateContent tail
while leaving gateway path prefixes untouched.

Rather than threading a new ModelSupportedEndpoint through the
shared ChatEndpoint pipeline (as Messages did), this delegates to
the native Gemini provider's existing request handling. The native
provider's GoogleGenAI client now accepts an optional baseUrl,
defaulting to the official API when unset so its own behavior is
unchanged. Custom Endpoint lazily creates one delegate instance and
routes gemini-typed requests to it, reusing the already-tested
streaming, tool-call, and thought-signature handling instead of
duplicating it.

Verified with the existing customEndpointProvider and
geminiNativeProvider vitest suites and a full tsc typecheck.
author: jyje
