commit_message:
fix(byok): construct Gemini delegate in constructor, not lazily

Resolving GeminiNativeBYOKLMProvider through _instantiationService in
a request-time method hides the dependency and reruns its
constructor's migration side effect on the first Gemini request,
against this repo's rule that service dependencies must be declared
in constructors, not accessed via the service locator elsewhere.

Now constructed once in the constructor, matching how every other
constructor-injected dependency here is handled.
author: jyje

commit_message:
fix(byok): forward requestHeaders and modelOptions to Gemini delegate

_toGeminiModel only carried apiKey/baseUrl/apiVersion, so a gateway
needing a custom auth header, or a model configured with temperature/
top_p overrides, would have those settings silently dropped whenever
apiType is gemini.

GeminiModelConfiguration gains headers/modelOptions. headers merges
into the SDK's httpOptions.headers. temperature/top_p is new plumbing
for the native Gemini provider generally (it wasn't wired to
GenerateContentConfig at all before, native vendor: gemini included),
using the same fields @google/genai's GenerateContentConfig already
exposes.
author: jyje

commit_message:
fix(byok): respect configured streaming mode for Gemini requests

_makeRequest unconditionally called generateContentStream, so
streaming: false was ignored and even an explicitly configured
:generateContent URL was turned into a :streamGenerateContent
request. Gateways that only implement the unary route would fail.

Threads a streaming flag (default true, preserving prior behavior)
through to _makeRequest, which now calls the SDK's non-streaming
generateContent and treats its single response as a one-chunk stream
so the existing chunk-processing logic (thought signatures, tool
calls, usage accumulation) stays shared between both paths.
author: jyje

test(byok): cover Gemini delegation and httpOptions/streaming wiring

geminiNativeProvider.spec.ts: extend MockGoogleGenAI to capture

variant). Add tests asserting baseUrl/apiVersion/headers/modelOptions
reach the SDK client, and that streaming: false uses generateContent
instead of generateContentStream.

customEndpointProvider.spec.ts: add a mocked-SDK test asserting an
apiType: 'gemini' model actually routes through the Gemini delegate

author: jyje

commit_message:
fix(byok): interpolate ${apiKey} in requestHeaders for the Gemini delegate

The other three apiTypes let a header value contain the literal token
${apiKey}, substituted with the configured key at request time, so a
gateway needing a custom auth header can reuse the same secret-stored
key instead of a second one. The Gemini path forwarded requestHeaders
as-is without this substitution.

Auth-header suppression, the other half of the original review
comment, needs no extra code: @google/genai's own addAuthHeaders
already skips adding x-goog-api-key when the header is already
present in httpOptions.headers.
author: jyje

commit_message:
fix(byok): honor per-request supportsReasoningEffort in Gemini delegate

GeminiNativeBYOKLMProvider resolved supported reasoning effort levels
from this._knownModels, populated only at construction time. The
Custom Endpoint delegate is always constructed with knownModels
undefined, so a configured supportsReasoningEffort was silently
dropped: the Thinking Effort picker still rendered (that comes from
shared getAllModels plumbing), but any selection was ignored at
request time.

model.configuration.supportsReasoningEffort now takes priority over
the knownModels lookup, with the knownModels path kept as a fallback
so native vendor: gemini behavior is unchanged.
author: jyje

commit_message:
test(byok): use gemini-3.6-flash consistently in gemini apiType tests

The tests added for the Custom Endpoint gemini apiType work used a mix
of gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-2.5-flash, and gemini-3-pro as mock model
ids, with no functional reason for the variation. Unifies them to
gemini-3.6-flash, matching the model used for live verification.
Pre-existing tests for the native provider are untouched.
author: jyje

commit_message:
fix(byok): sanitize custom headers before forwarding to the Gemini delegate

requestHeaders forwarded to the Gemini path skipped every check
OpenAIEndpoint applies to the other three apiTypes: the reserved
header blocklist (Host, Cookie, Forwarded, Content-Length, and more),
RFC 7230 name validation, a 20-header cap, and control-character/
header-injection checks on values.

Extracts that sanitizer out of OpenAIEndpoint into
byok/common/customHeaderSanitizer.ts so both paths share one
implementation instead of Gemini reimplementing or, worse, skipping
it. OpenAIEndpoint's behavior is unchanged, including its
_isReservedHeader override hook for the Messages API auth headers.

Sanitization runs before ${apiKey} interpolation, matching the order
CustomEndpointOAIEndpoint already uses for the other three types.

fix(byok): reuse the singleton Gemini provider in Custom Endpoint

CustomEndpointBYOKModelProvider constructed its own
GeminiNativeBYOKLMProvider instance at startup, alongside the singleton

commit_message:
fix(byok): honor per-request modelOptions in Gemini delegate

temperature and top_p were only ever read from model.configuration
(the static per-model config), never from options.modelOptions (the
vscode API's per-request override field). This contradicted the
Custom Endpoint contract that explicit per-request values override
configured defaults.

Resolve each value from options.modelOptions first, falling back to
the configured default. An explicit null on either side means "no
override here" rather than "send null to the SDK".
author: jyje

commit_message:
fix(byok): report actual streaming mode in Gemini OTel span

The OTel span's REQUEST_STREAM attribute was hardcoded to true even
when streaming was configured false, misreporting non-streaming
Gemini requests in telemetry. Use the streaming value already resolved
earlier in the same request.

commit_message:
docs(byok): clarify Gemini URL suffix has no effect on streaming

The url field's markdownDescription implied an explicit
:generateContent path is called as written. In practice
resolveGeminiBaseUrl strips that suffix entirely, and the streaming
vs non-streaming route is chosen solely by the streaming property
(defaults to true), independent of what the configured URL says.

commit_message:
fix(byok): allow auth header override for Gemini gateways

The Gemini delegation path sanitized requestHeaders with the default
reserved list, which still blocks Authorization and api-key. Unlike
CustomEndpointOAIEndpoint, it had no way to let a gateway behind the
configured URL replace the inferred credential, and even a differently
named override header couldn't stop @google/genai from also sending
its own x-goog-api-key derived from the configured apiKey.

Extract CustomEndpointOAIEndpoint's auth-override allowance and
suppression-signal set into shared helpers in customHeaderSanitizer.ts,
reuse them for the Gemini delegate, and pre-empt x-goog-api-key with an
empty placeholder when the user supplies their own auth header (the
SDK's NodeAuth only adds it when the header isn't already present).
author: jyje

commit_message:
docs(byok): mention Gemini in CustomOAI deprecation messages

The customoai provider's two deprecation messages listed only Chat
Completions, Responses, and Messages as what customendpoint supports,
understating its capabilities for anyone migrating off the deprecated
provider now that customendpoint also supports apiType: gemini.
author: jyje

commit_message:
fix(byok): allow an absent apiKey for Gemini Custom Endpoints

Custom Endpoint doesn't require an apiKey: it already passes '' to
CustomEndpointOAIEndpoint when one isn't configured, supporting
unauthenticated endpoints and ones authenticated solely via a
requestHeaders entry. The Gemini delegation reached the native
provider's unconditional apiKey check instead, so every request on
such an endpoint failed even though the model was listed and
selectable.

Add apiKeyOptional to GeminiModelConfiguration, set only by the Custom
Endpoint delegation. The native provider (official Google API) keeps
requiring a key. Also pass '' rather than undefined to the SDK
constructor when the key is absent, since undefined makes it fall back
to ambient Application Default Credentials lookup instead of using no
credential at all.
author: jyje

commit_message:
agentHost: widen native Claude setup detection

`detectExistingClaudeSetup` recognized only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, so several ordinary BYO-Anthropic setups read
as "no local Claude" and were forced to sign in to GitHub. Add three more
sources to the `~/.claude/settings.json` validator, which is the single
source of truth for the key set:

- `env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` - first-class in Anthropic's own resolution
  order, right after `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` - counts on its own, since it points Claude at
  a gateway that supplies the credential.
- top-level `apiKeyHelper` - a command the CLI runs to mint a key, so a
  setup can be complete with no credential stored anywhere.

`apiKeyHelper` sits outside the `env` block, so `readClaudeSettingsEnv`
becomes `readClaudeSettings` and returns the whole validated object. The
env predicate and its derived type are renamed (`hasClaudeCredential` ->
`hasNativeClaudeEnv`, `ClaudeCredentialEnv` -> `ClaudeNativeEnv`) because
a base URL is an endpoint override, not a credential.

Presence-only and empty-string-doesn't-count both still hold: nothing
here reads a credential beyond asking whether it is a non-empty string.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
author: TylerLeonhardt

commit_message:
Read each native-setup source independently

Whole-object validation meant one malformed value voided the rest of the
file: `{ apiKeyHelper: "...", env: { ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: 42 } }` reported
no setup at all, even though the helper alone is a complete setup. Split
the validator per source and carry `unknown` values, so `isNonEmptyString`
is the only thing that decides usability and a mistyped entry reads as
absent rather than failing its siblings.

Also trims the JSDoc on the detection helpers to the 1-2 sentence rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
author: TylerLeonhardt

commit_message:
Use the shared string and JSON helpers

Both local helpers were hand-rolled versions of things base already has.
`isNonEmptyString` becomes `isString` + `isFalsyOrWhitespace`, which also
makes an all-whitespace value read as absent rather than as a credential.
`JSON.parse` becomes the tolerant `json.ts` parser, matching how VS Code
reads every other hand-edited config (see agentPluginParser) — comments and
a trailing comma in settings.json no longer hide a real setup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
author: TylerLeonhardt

commit_message:
Check the JSONC parser's errors instead of catching

`parse` never throws — it reports on the `errors` out-param and salvages a
partial result. So the try/catch inherited from `JSON.parse` caught nothing,
and a truncated settings.json yielded a whole recovered credential: the
probe returns {env:{ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:"sk-ant-api-x"}} with 2 errors from
input that stops mid-object. That read as a native setup the CLI itself
could not have loaded.

Reject on a non-empty `errors` array, keep the try/catch on readFileSync
where something actually throws, and allow empty content so an empty file
is "no settings" rather than corrupt.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
author: TylerLeonhardt

commit_message:
agentHost: require GitHub for Claude unless a BYO-Anthropic setup exists

Since #329331 ClaudeAgent advertised the GitHub Copilot protected resource as
`required: false` unconditionally, on the reasoning that per-session routing
means no host-global mode can make Copilot strictly required. But `required` is
not a question about routing -- it is read only by
protectedResourcesRequireGitHubCopilotSignIn, which backs the Agents window gate
and the per-session-type gate. Answering it "optional" for a user with no
Anthropic credential claimed Claude was usable without GitHub when every model
the merged catalog can offer for them is Copilot-routed.

Restore the pre-#329331 condition: the resource is optional only when a local
BYOK setup is discovered. New private _hasUsableNativeSetup() is the single
"can Claude run without GitHub right now?" fact -- the allowSignedOutWhenUsable
opt-in AND detectExistingClaudeSetup (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY /
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in the process env or the `env` block of
~/.claude/settings.json). _defaultTransportMode() now feeds hasExistingSetup
from the same helper, so the advertised requirement and the fallback transport
cannot disagree.

Two deliberate choices. The resource is still *kept* in the list rather than
dropped, so the silent probe survives: authenticateProtectedResources matches on
`resource` and ignores `required`, so an already-signed-in user still has a token
forwarded and authenticate() still acquires the proxy handle Copilot-routed
models need. And sign-in state is deliberately not an input -- whether GitHub is
*required* is a property of what the user can run without it, not of whether
they happen to be connected at this instant.

Making this derived rather than constant introduces a staleness risk, so it was
verified live: AgentSideEffects already republishes agent infos on
RootConfigChanged, and _publishAgentInfos' `equals` guard limits the dispatch to
real changes.

Verified end-to-end against a signed-out Agents window (--use-mock-keychain),
reading the published protectedResources off the AHP JSONL log:

  - no credential, opt-in on  => required=true,  "Sign in to use Agents" gate
  - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, opt-in on  => required=false, window opens signed out
    with Claude selected and the discovered-config nudge
  - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, opt-in off => required=true,  gate (kill switch holds)

The third run also exercised the republish path: the host started with a stale
`true` in its agent-host-config.json, published required=false, then flipped to
required=true 93ms after the client pushed the setting.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: TylerLeonhardt

commit_message:
agentHost: keep the native Claude catalog published through first sign-in

`_onAuthToken` blanked the model catalog unconditionally before kicking off
the refresh for the new token. On a *first* sign-in there is no superseded
account to drop, and the catalog being cleared is the account-independent
native bootstrap list — so blanking only publishes an empty catalog for the
duration of the refresh.

The Agents window reads an agent with no models as
`SessionTypeAuthRequirement.Unusable`, so that empty window closes the
`chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable` gate mid-startup and forces the
sign-in dialog on a user who is already signing in: the GitHub session
resolves before the Copilot default account does, so the welcome flow still
believes it is signed out.

Blank only on a *replacement* (`oldHandle` present), where a different
account genuinely can have different model entitlements.

commit_message:
agentHost: run the agent host on the remote server

The agent-host harness never appeared in the session-type picker when
connected to a remote (Codespaces, Remote-SSH, Dev Containers, WSL).
Two independent gaps caused this.

1. The REH server only spawned an agent host when launched with
   `--agent-host-port` / `--agent-host-path`, and only bridged renderers
   when `--agent-host-bridge-*` was set. The Rust CLI's `code tunnel`
   sidecar is the only caller that passes those flags, so every other
   remote registered `UnavailableAgentHostChannel`: the renderer's
   connect rejected, root state never arrived, and no agent chat session
   types were registered.

   The server now self-provisions an agent host when no flags are given,
   listening on a per-server random socket path guarded by a random
   connection token. It starts lazily on the first renderer connect, so
   servers where chat is never used pay nothing and remote auto-shutdown
   idle timers are unaffected. Startup only reports success once the
   agent host confirms its listener is bound, so the first connect can't
   race the socket into existence.

2. The agent host chat contributions were registered only from the
   desktop workbench, even though the web workbench already wired up
   `EditorRemoteAgentHostServiceClient` and enables the agent host
   whenever a remote authority is present. They now live in the browser
   layer and are shared by web and desktop, which is what makes the
   Codespaces browser client work.

Gating is unchanged: the agent host is offered only when a real
server-backed remote exists, so serverless web stays dark.

Also stop forwarding the client-resolved default shell to a remote agent
host. Sending a client's shell path to a server of a different platform
is wrong; the agent host resolves its own shell when the key is absent.

Fixes #326125

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: address review feedback on remote server startup

- Keep the caller's `ensureStarted()` pending across automatic retries.
  Rejecting while a retry was still in flight made a transient first-spawn
  failure fatal for the window, since the protocol client treats a failure
  during connect as terminal and never sees the later successful start.

- Register the crash handler only after startup fully succeeds. An exit
  during startup already rejects the pending readiness request, so the
  retry loop now owns that case exclusively; previously both paths could
  fire and start two replacement processes while burning the budget twice.

- Cache only the in-flight endpoint resolution in `AgentHostChannel`.
  Resolution is `ensureStarted()` on the lazy server path, so retaining a
  resolved endpoint meant a later reconnect dialed a dead socket instead
  of restarting the host.

- Remove a stale socket before spawning. Unix sockets outlive the process
  that bound them, so a crashed agent host left its path behind and every
  restart failed to bind with EADDRINUSE, exhausting the retry budget
  without recovering.

Also document that the agent host starts once a chat-enabled remote window
loads rather than on first session use: the contribution injects
IAgentHostService, which connects from its constructor. That matches the
pre-existing desktop behaviour; the server-side laziness is about servers
with no connected renderer.

Tests waited a single microtask for startup, which the readiness await made
insufficient; they now wait for the real signal.

commit_message:
Add floating chat-input window with multi-session routing

Introduces a frameless, always-on-top auxiliary window that hosts the real
chat input (dictation, voice mode, and the input glow) via a compact,
input-only ChatWidget. Submissions are scored against the current session
list by a new ISessionRouter and dispatched with three outcomes:

- low confidence -> start a brand-new session
- several comparable high matches -> ask the user which session
- a single clear match -> dispatch straight to it

ISessionRouter keeps prompt/parse/heuristic logic pure so the scoring
backend (renderer language model now; CAPI utility or a local model later)
can be swapped without changing the contract; it degrades to a token-overlap
heuristic when no model is available. Toggle via the command
"Toggle Floating Chat Input Window".

commit_message:
Chat input window: advisory badge with auto-send instead of silent routing

Routing is no longer silent. After scoring the utterance against existing
sessions, the window resolves a single pending target (top match above the
confidence threshold, biased toward the last-used session; otherwise a new
session) and shows an inline badge naming that target with a short countdown.
When the countdown elapses the request auto-sends. The user can redirect it
("Change"), abort it ("Cancel"), or just keep typing — any edit cancels the
auto-send — so a request is never dispatched without a visible, correctable
step.

- Add ROUTE_AUTOSEND_DELAY_MS countdown + pending-send badge in the aux window.
- Remember the last routed session (workspace storage) and pre-select it.
- Generalize the target picker to list all scored candidates with a preselected
  entry, reused by the badge's "Change" action.

Make omni-chat input window draggable via command-center pattern

Adopt the same approach the command center uses in the title bar: a
dedicated, full-size .chat-input-window-drag-region layer sits behind the
input and is marked -webkit-app-region: drag in CSS, while the interactive
controls (editor, toolbars, attachments) render on top and are marked
no-drag. This gives a large, reliable drag surface (the input-box chrome)
instead of relying on a thin transparent ring or fragile app-region
inheritance.

commit_message:
Refresh cloned plugin marketplaces on a TTL

Private marketplace repos are discovered by cloning, because
raw.githubusercontent.com returns 4xx for them. `ensureRepository`
short-circuited whenever the clone directory already existed, so
discovery stayed frozen at the originally-cloned commit and newly
added plugins never appeared. The raw-fetch path had an 8h TTL; the
clone path had none, and the only refresher (`pullRepository`) is
reached from `updateAllPlugins`, which iterates *installed* plugins —
so a marketplace with nothing installed from it could not be
refreshed at all.

Give the clone path the same TTL via `refreshIfOlderThanMs`: a stale
clone is silently pulled inside the existing clone sequencer, so
concurrent fetchers collapse to a single pull. Local-file
marketplaces and SHA-pinned refs are never pulled. Failures are
non-fatal and still timestamped, so an unreachable remote cannot
cause a pull storm; cancellations are not timestamped, so navigating
away does not suppress the next attempt.

`pullRepository` now records the timestamp too — an explicit pull
leaves the clone just as fresh, and without this `updateAllPlugins`
pulled every marketplace twice in a row.

Also adds `Chat: Refresh Plugin Marketplaces` to bypass both caches
on demand, and hoists service lookups in the plugin commands into the
synchronous window: `invokeFunction` invalidates the accessor once the
handler returns, so the existing post-`await` `accessor.get` calls in
`updatePlugins` were throwing instead of showing their notifications.

Fixes #328523

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: connor4312

commit_message:
Address PR feedback on marketplace refresh

- Don't commit a cancelled fetch's results. `fetchMarketplacePlugins`
  wrote its results to `lastFetchedPlugins` unconditionally, so
  cancelling the refresh replaced the list with the empty/partial
  result and blanked the marketplace UI.

- Thread the caller's token into the cold-clone path. Only stale
  pulls honoured it, so cancelling the refresh did not stop a
  first-time clone. Cancelled clones no longer raise a failure
  notification, since the user asked for the abort.

- Report partial failures. The fetch helpers swallow per-marketplace
  errors and return `[]`, so the command reported success even when a
  marketplace failed to clone. Add `onMarketplaceError` so callers can
  distinguish a partial result, and warn with the affected names.

- Invalidate the raw-fetch cache entry when falling back to cloning.
  A marketplace that went from public to private kept serving its
  stale raw entry on the next non-forced fetch until the original TTL
  expired.

commit_message:
agentHost: remove the claudeUseCopilotProxy setting

Since #329331 the Claude model picker shows Copilot-proxy and native-Anthropic
models together, each carrying a provider-qualified id, and a session routes on
the provider of the model it was started with (resolveClaudeSessionTransport).
That makes the host-global override redundant — and, worse, incoherent.

Model enumeration (_refreshModels) gates the proxy half on holding a GitHub
token and the native half on detectExistingClaudeSetup; neither consulted the
setting. getProtectedResources() advertises the Copilot resource required:false
unconditionally. So `claudeUseCopilotProxy: false` never stopped Copilot-routed
Claude from being offered or used by a signed-in user, which is exactly what its
title ("Route Claude Through Copilot") promised. Its only remaining effect was
on the model-less fallback, where an explicit `true` broke the one state the
signed-out feature exists to serve: opt-in on, signed out, local Anthropic
credential present — forced to proxy and dead-ended on AHP_AUTH_REQUIRED.

resolveClaudeTransportMode drops its explicitProxy input and reduces to three:
opt-in off => proxy; signed in => proxy; else local setup => native; else proxy.

Clean deletion, not a deprecation: the key was never forwarded from a VS Code
setting (AgentHostRootConfigForwarder never managed it) and was only ever
hand-written into agent-host-config.json. A profile carrying a stale value
starts with no error and drops the key on the first config write.

Also corrects mergeClaudeModelCatalogs' claim that proxy-first ordering makes
Copilot the session default. It does not: the picker re-buckets by the _meta
vendor token, so the Anthropic group sorts first and the pre-selected model
routes native. Verified end-to-end.

commit_message:
agentHost: feat: let subsessions inherit the parent permission level

A session an agent creates via the `create_session` server tool always
started at the default permission level, with no way to carry over the
permission level the parent was running at.

Adds `chat.subsessions.inheritPermissions` (`once` / `always` / `never`,
default `once`). Under `once` the host asks through a chat input request
and the tool call blocks on the answer; answering "always"/"never"
persists the setting.

The question — not a tool confirmation — is the consent gate: an elevated
session puts the Copilot SDK into allow-all mode, so it approves tools
internally and never surfaces a confirmation card to extend.

Inheritance is confined to the portable `autoApprove` axis, so providers
that model approvals on their own axis (Claude `permissionMode`, Codex
`permissionsPreset`) never inherit. Enterprise policy forbidding
auto-approval is forwarded to the host and blocks inheritance, and under
`always` the level carries over only into a directory already covered by
the parent roots.

commit_message:
agentHost: multi-root turn changesets and session diff summary

For multi-root Copilot sessions (more than one working folder), aggregate
file changes across all folders. Single-folder and non-Copilot sessions keep

- git-blob content resolution is now repository-aware: the owning repo root is
  derived server-side from the blob's absolute path (Option A), so non-primary
  folder diffs open correctly without trusting a client-held cwd.
- Agents Window 'Last Turn Changes' is filtered to the primary repository root
  so the single-root Changes panel stays consistent.

commit_message:
tunnels: fail over to a dedicated agent host when the gateway rejects a selection

A tunnel-backed connect could stay down for the whole reconnect backoff window
instead of failing over. The CLI's agent-host registry treats an entry as live
purely by PID liveness, so an `editor` entry can outlive the socket it
advertises. The gateway then answers the selection with
`{"ok":false,"error":"Selected agent host became unreachable: ..."}` and closes.
`completeSelection` threw a plain error for that, indistinguishable from the
tunnel being unreachable, so `_connectTunnel` just rescheduled a reconnect —
which resolved the identical stale `editor` endpoint from the still-unchanged
inventory and failed the same way, over and over, until the owning PID finally
died. The editor -> standalone fallback and its notification did eventually
fire, but only minutes later.

Tag the gateway's `{"ok":false}` answer with a distinct `Error.name`
(`TUNNEL_GATEWAY_SELECTION_REJECTED_ERROR_NAME`), carried as a name rather than
a subclass because it crosses the shared-process IPC boundary, which preserves
`name`/`message`/`stack` but not the prototype chain. A rejection is the one
failure that proves the tunnel is healthy and only the chosen endpoint is dead,
so `_completeSelectionWithFallback` re-runs `prepareSelection` and retries once
with `selectGatewayFallbackAfterRejection()` — a dedicated host, never the
instance just rejected. The failover now happens inside a single connect
attempt.

Every other failure means the tunnel itself is down and is rethrown unchanged,
so the contribution keeps retrying the same destination and selection. A
fallback never mutates the stored location preference, so the editor host is
preferred again as soon as it is back.

The substitution also notifies now, including on a user-initiated connect that
explicitly asked for the editor host, since there is no earlier registration for
the tracker to compare against within a single attempt. A stale entry lingers
for as long as its PID does and every later reconnect repeats the same fallback,
so `shouldNotifyTunnelFailover` stays quiet once the address is already recorded
as `standalone`.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: Verify SSH host keys for remote agent host connections

The ssh2 ConnectConfig had no hostVerifier, which makes ssh2 accept any
host key from any server ("Host accepted by default (no verification)").
Every remote agent host SSH connection was therefore open to
impersonation, including harvesting the password typed into our own
keyboard-interactive prompt and, with agentForward, access to the user's
SSH agent. hostVerifier runs during key exchange, before authentication,
so declining now guarantees no credentials ever reach an unverified
server.

Trust is kept in our own IStorageService-backed store; the user's
known_hosts files are read as an additional trust source but are never
written to. A changed or revoked key hard-fails with no click-through,
recoverable only via the new "Forget SSH Host Key" command, and
StrictHostKeyChecking is honored from the user's real SSH config rather
than a parallel setting. Host keys a server proves it owns via OpenSSH's
UpdateHostKeys extension are learned silently, so legitimate rotations
do not surface as failures.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: roblourens

commit_message:
agentHost: Allow time to answer the SSH host key prompt

ssh2's readyTimeout covers the whole handshake and keeps running while
hostVerifier awaits a verdict, so the existing 30s window would abort the
connection out from under a user doing exactly what the host key dialog
asks: going to compare the fingerprint against another source. Verified
against a live server that readyTimeout does fire while a verdict is
pending.

Waiting longer is safe here because these prompts only occur after the
server has proven responsive (we are holding its host key), so this
window is not what guards against an unreachable host. Background
reconnects never prompt, so they keep the short window and still abandon
a stalled handshake promptly.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_message:
agentHost: Harden SSH host key verification after review

Fixes found by code review and confirmed against OpenSSH 9.9:

- Revoked host keys were accepted when StrictHostKeyChecking was no/off,
  because the opt-out was evaluated before the revocation check. Real ssh
  still reports "REVOKED HOST KEY DETECTED" under that setting and
  disables password auth, keyboard-interactive auth and agent
  forwarding. Disabling host key checking means "I accept unknown keys",
  never "I accept keys I have explicitly revoked".

- An UpdateHostKeys announcement could overwrite a genuine stored key
  from a session that was never verified (StrictHostKeyChecking=no), so
  an impostor's key would be trusted once strict checking was restored.
  ssh2 proves announced keys belong to whoever we are talking to, which
  says nothing about whether that party is the real host. Announcements
  are now honored only when the key that authenticated the session is
  itself trusted, matching OpenSSH's documented rule.

- A clean mid-handshake close left the connect promise pending forever:
  ssh2 emits only end/close with no error and clears its own timeout.
  Verified with a server that drops the connection after the banner.

- A connection dying while known_hosts was being read could register a
  verification for an already-dead connect, leaking a pending entry and
  prompting about a connection that was gone.

- Replaces the previous blunt 5 minute readyTimeout, which made an
  unreachable host take minutes to fail. The handshake deadline is now
  ours (ssh2's is disabled, verified that readyTimeout:0 does so) and is
  widened only for the interval a prompt is actually outstanding.

Also corrects doc comments that said "main process" for a service that
runs in the shared process.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
agentHost: Document and cover the stale host key dialog case

IDialogService.confirm accepts no CancellationToken and offers no
programmatic dismissal, so a host key modal opened for a connection that
subsequently dies stays on screen. That is cosmetic rather than unsafe:
the caller re-checks cancellation before acting on the answer, so a late
"Connect" can neither persist trust nor revive a dead connect attempt.
Documents the limitation and adds a test that locks in the safety
property.

commit_message:
agentHost: Dismiss the SSH host key prompt when the connection dies

I previously concluded this was not fixable because IDialogService.confirm
takes no CancellationToken. That was wrong: the token lives on the
options object (IBaseDialogOptions), not the method signature. It only
applies to custom dialogs, which is why the existing precedent for a
dismissable confirmation pairs `custom` with `token`.

So the prompt now tears itself down when the connection drops instead of
stranding the user with a question about a connection that no longer
exists. Answering late was already inert, and the test now asserts both
properties rather than just the latter.

Also fixes doc comments that described the old ordering in the host key
policy and referred to ssh2's readyTimeout, which we no longer use.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_message:
agentHost: Report a refused SSH host key without ssh2 jargon

Declining a host key surfaced "Failed to connect via SSH to macbook-air:
Error: Host denied (verification failed)" — ssh2's internal wording, and
redundant on top of the host key UI, which has already either been
dismissed by the user or shown a specific error with a recovery action.

A refused key now rejects with SSHHostKeyDeniedError, which the connect
UI treats like a cancellation and does not report again. The guard
matches on the error name because the error is raised in the shared
process and inspected in the renderer, where only name/message survive
IPC serialization.

Only a verdict from the renderer is treated this way. Node-side
fail-closed paths (a malformed key, or an error while reading
known_hosts) still surface a visible error, since nothing else would
tell the user the connection went nowhere.

(Written by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: roblourens

commit_message:
agentHost: Refuse a changed SSH host key even when strict checking is off

Review caught a real fail-open. `StrictHostKeyChecking=no`/`off` returned
plain trust for *any* key, including one contradicting a key we already
trust, so a MITM could receive the password we prompt for and get agent
access.

Verified against OpenSSH 9.9: with `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` and a
changed host key it still prints "REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS
CHANGED!" and then disables password auth, keyboard-interactive auth and
agent forwarding, while still permitting a signature-based login. So the
opt-out means "I accept unknown keys", never "I accept a key that
contradicts one I trust".

We refuse outright rather than connecting under those restrictions. That
is stricter than OpenSSH, but it matches the hard-fail contract a changed
key gets everywhere else here, and recovery is the same explicit forget
step. I had previously written a comment and a test asserting the
opposite, which is what made the bug look deliberate; both are corrected.

Also from review:

- Denials now carry where the conflict came from, so "Forget Saved Host
  Key" is only offered when clearing our store can actually unblock the
  user. A known_hosts mismatch or an @revoked line lives in the user's
  own files and would keep winning afterwards, so those messages point at
  the file instead of offering an action that does nothing.
- The interactive deadline now brackets every human prompt. Previously
  only the host key dialog widened it, so a user typing a password or a
  key passphrase still had the 30s network deadline.
- Tests await a real completion signal instead of sleeping 10ms.
- Restored a JSDoc block that I had orphaned from its interface.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_message:
voice: explain why a voice connection failed

Voice Mode collapsed about a dozen distinct failures into three strings,
and presented the one permanent failure - authorization - as a transient
one, retrying it silently before showing a generic toast.

- Add a close-code registry shared by the client and the controller,
  including aliases for the plain codes an older backend still sends.
- Report every terminal close. The 30-minute give-up, clean closes, and a
  missing backend URL each previously exited quietly, which could strand the
  UI on 'Reconnecting...' with nothing reconnecting.
- Stop onopen resetting the reconnect budget. The backend now accepts a
  socket before refusing it so the refusal can carry a close code, so an
  open socket no longer proves the connection works; resetting there pinned
  the fast 2s retry cadence forever and made the give-up unreachable.
- Say why while retrying, via a new onConnectionIssue signal.
- Show a localized reason plus the one action that resolves it: Sign in,
  Retry, or Open Settings.
- Only count a session in telemetry once it survives the staleness guard,
  so a refusal is no longer logged as a session that never ends.

commit_message:
Show a connecting state while the socket retries

The close-code taxonomy made rejections legible, but a retrying socket
still rendered as either idle or connected, so a user watching a failing
connect saw a static UI with no sign anything was happening.

Four gaps, all on the path a rejection now takes:

- The voice pill read `isConnecting` but never `isReconnecting`, so the
  surface people actually click sat idle for the whole retry window.
- The connect watchdog tore down scheduled reconnects: a retry sleeps
  longer than the handshake timeout, so the wait looked like a hang.
- Onboarding suppressed the widget's status line, hiding the reason.
- `isConnected` was committed on socket-open. Rejections are now accepted
  before they are closed so the close frame can carry a reason, so
  `onopen` fires for doomed sockets too and the UI flashed connected on
  every attempt. It now waits for the backend's session ack, with a
  bounded fallback. This also closes the hands-free mic race where a
  refused socket could briefly start capture.

The pill shows a spinner in place of the waveform while connecting, and
drops the inert listen cell so it renders as a single cell rather than a
spinner beside a dead button.

Reconnect budget is 60s (was 30 min); a half-hour of silent retrying is
not a state worth offering.

commit_message:
Ack the session in tests that need a live connection

The omni suite that arrived with main connects by opening the socket and
sending start_session, then never acks it. Since this branch holds
isConnected until the backend acks — an open socket is not proof of
admission, because a rejected connect is accepted first so its close
frame can carry a reason — `_isOmniVoiceInboxActive()` stayed false and
nothing narrated, failing 11 tests on every platform.

The eleven affected sites now fire session_init after the session
command, which is what a real backend does.

Acking inside the double's sendStartSession would have been tidier but is
wrong: the connect handler sends at the top and only assigns
_enterListenOnSessionInit ~350 lines later, so a synchronous ack would
run the session_init handler against a stale flag and break hands-free
auto-listen. There are no awaits in between, so acking after
sessionCommandSent resolves is safe.

commit_message:
Fix active client refresh feedback loop

Agent Host session hydration installed a persistent state-change listener that refreshed the current active client whenever its in-memory payload differed from protocol state. Because wire serialization drops undefined properties, the echoed session/activeClientSet remained structurally unequal and immediately triggered another refresh. This produced a self-sustaining request/echo loop at roughly 1,800 messages and 33 MiB per second, saturating the Agents window renderer, driving repeated major garbage collections, and generating hundreds of megabytes of AHP traffic in seconds.

Make the hydration reconciliation one-shot: wait until this client appears, dispose the listener before dispatching any refresh, and leave subsequent legitimate tool and customization updates to their existing observables. Add regression coverage that simulates the wire-normalized echo and verifies it cannot dispatch a second refresh.

(Written by Copilot)

commit_message:
Check native optional deps against the host, not the build target

The native optional-dependency guard asserted that the *target*
architecture's per-platform package was present in the *host's* root
node_modules. The pipelines set `npm_config_arch`, but that only steers
node-gyp/prebuild downloads -- it does not drive npm's `os`/`cpu`
optional-dependency filtering. On a cross-architecture job npm therefore
installs the host's per-platform package, so the assertion could never
hold and every cross-arch node_modules job failed:

  @openai/codex: required per-platform package '@openai/codex-darwin-x64'
  is missing from node_modules

The step is gated on a cache miss, so this stayed invisible until the
first package-lock.json change produced a fresh cache key. Because the
job then fails before "Create node_modules archive", the cache for that
key is never saved, so every subsequent build re-misses and re-fails.

Check the host platform/arch instead, and drop the argv override so no
call site can reintroduce the target-arch assertion. The per-target
binaries that actually ship are produced separately by
build/agent-sdk/package.ts, which installs into a scratch dir with
`npm_config_os`/`npm_config_cpu` set and validates the result with the

sessions: Refine Show/Hide Editor placement, icons, and Browser-tab fallback

Follow-up to #329384 (merged), addressing feedback on that PR's
Show/Hide Editor Area actions:

- Moves Hide Editor / Show Editor from the full-width editor header's
  trailing layout group to the tab strip's editor-title layout cluster
  (`MenuId.EditorTitleLayout`), immediately after Maximize/Restore
  Editor Area (order 20 vs. 10). Toggle Details remains alone in the
  header's trailing group.
- Both actions now always render regardless of whether the active tab
  has a docked detail panel (drops the `HasDockedDetailsContext` gate),
  matching Maximize/Restore's own always-shown behavior in that
  cluster.
- Switches their icons to the existing `right-panel-hide` /
  `right-panel-show` codicons (previously `chevron-right` /
  `chevron-left`, which are already heavily reused elsewhere in this
  window for tree/list disclosure twisties).

  precondition) and unconditionally reveals the auxiliary bar in

  tab was active would immediately re-hide the just-revealed detail
  panel, since `SinglePaneDetailPanelStrategy`'s "Browser hides the
  detail" rule fired again right away. The strategy now only
  transiently hides the detail for a Browser tab while the editor area
  itself stays visible; once the editor area is hidden (e.g. via Hide
  Editor), the panel shows the same Changes/Files fallback a session
  with no active editor gets, since it would otherwise be the only
  thing left on screen. Revealing the editor area again (Show Editor)
  restores the normal transient-hide behavior.

Updates SINGLE_PANE_SCENARIOS.md and LAYOUT.md to document the new
placement, icons, always-enabled state, and Browser-tab fallback, and
adds/updates targeted tests covering the menu placement, the action's
unconditional reveal, and the strategy's Browser-tab fallback end to

Add EditorInputCapabilities.CannotClose for editors that cannot be closed via standard user actions

Fixes #329370

Introduces a new editor input capability that allows an editor to opt
out of being closed through standard user-initiated actions (tab
close button, middle click, Close Editor / Close All / Close Group
commands and keybindings, and toolbar close/unpin affordances) while
preserving internal/programmatic force-close paths such as shutdown,
window reload, workspace transitions, editor replacement and restore

  out non-closeable editors for user-facing calls, while a new
  `force`/internal option lets lifecycle call sites (state
  reapplication, cross-window group moves, auxiliary window merge)
  bypass the restriction.
- Mixed selections/bulk operations close whatever is closeable and
  leave the rest open rather than failing the whole operation.
- Editor replacement continues to work for CannotClose editors since
  it is considered an internal operation.
- Tab close/unpin actions, context menu items and toolbar items are
  hidden for CannotClose editors via a new
  ActiveEditorCannotCloseContext context key, avoiding misleading
  close affordances.
- Middle-click tab closing is a no-op for CannotClose editors.
- CloseAllEditorGroupsAction only removes a group once it is actually
  empty, so a group containing a CannotClose editor is not disposed.
- Added targeted tests covering individual close, bulk close/close
  all, mixed sets, replacement, and group-close semantics.

commit_message:
agentHost: return every Codex session from thread/list

Codex sessions disappeared from the Agents window: a session pinned the
day before was gone from the list and unfindable by search, while `codex
resume <id>` still opened it. `thread/list` was returning 10 of 768
non-archived threads.

Two independent causes, both verified against the same codex 0.146
binary and thread store by varying only the request:

- Codex reads an omitted `modelProviders` filter as "only the currently
  configured provider" (`thread_processor.rs`: `None =>
  Some(vec![self.config.model_provider_id.clone()])`). VS Code stopped
  passing `-c model_provider="vscode-proxy"` when it gained OpenAI
  subscription support, so the active provider fell back to the built-in
  `openai` and every thread recorded under `vscode-proxy` was hidden —
  645 of 671 in the reporter's store. Passing an explicitly empty array
  is codex's documented "all providers" request, and restored the full
  list.

- The request asked for `limit: 200`, but the server caps a page at 100
  (`THREAD_LIST_MAX_LIMIT`) and the response cursor was ignored, so at
  most 100 sessions could ever surface.

Page through `thread/list` with the cursor and ask for all providers.
The paging loop is extracted as a pure helper so it can be unit-tested
without standing up the whole agent, mirroring `codexForkPlan.ts`. It
stops if the server repeats a cursor and gives up after a bounded number
of pages so a misbehaving server cannot hang startup.

Verified end to end in a dev build against the reporter's thread store:
`thread/list` went from 10 sessions to 672, including the pinned session
that had gone missing.

commit_message:
agentHost: guard Claude model refresh against a mid-flight per-session provider toggle

The refresh stale-write guards captured only the transport token/mode, not the
per-session provider flag. Because `_startModelRefresh` supersedes an in-flight
refresh as the coalescing target but never cancels it, a false-flip of the flag
mid-refresh left the superseded refresh running; when it settled it published a
stale wrong-mode catalog (merged provider-qualified over the bare single-transport
list the flag-off refresh had already published, or vice versa), clobbering the
correct one.

Capture `_perSessionProviderEnabled` at the start of both `_refreshModelsSingle`
and `_refreshModelsMerged` and bail in the stale-write guard when it moved, so the
superseded refresh drops its result.

Tests: a flag-on→off toggle mid-merge (native half parked on a gate so the merged
refresh is provably still in-flight) asserts the bare single catalog survives the
straggler; and a flag-off regression that a forked peer chat still inherits its
never-materialized parent's explicit model (the inheritance in `_resolveParentSession`
is intentionally not flag-gated).

commit_message:
agentHost: simplify Claude per-session transport resolution

Follow-up cleanup on the per-session-provider read-path, now that the
feature is unconditional and the single-catalog path is gone.

- Collapse the cached `_transportMode` and its reactive
  `_resolveTransportMode`/`_applyTransportModeChange` machinery into a
  read-on-demand `_defaultTransportMode()`. The host default is only the
  fallback for model-less / bare-id sessions, so it needs no caching or
  config/sign-in re-resolve — the next session reads live availability.
- `authenticate()`: a Copilot proxy-start failure is now uniformly soft.
  GitHub sign-in still succeeds and both `_githubToken` and `_proxyHandle`
  stay uncommitted, so a retry re-attempts `start()`; a Copilot-routed
  model re-drives sign-in on its first send. Drops the native/proxy
  default special-casing and the mid-flight transport-mode flip.
- Replace `IMaterializeContext.resolveTransport` (a callback the session
  re-invoked on every rebuild) with a `transport` value the agent pins at
  materialize. A per-session provider switch is pushed in through `send`'s
  new `switchTransport` (staged in `_pendingSwitchTransport`); ordinary and
  SDK-recover rebuilds reuse the materialized transport. A throwing guard
  replaces the defensive re-resolve.
- Move cross-transport switch detection into `ClaudeAgentSession.setModel`
  (the session owns it); drop the agent-computed `deferForTransportSwitch`
  option and expose `hasPendingTransportSwitch` in place of `transportKind`.
- Inline the one-off `_settledCatalog` helper into `_refreshModels` and drop
  the `_refreshModels` -> `_refreshModelsMerged` forwarder.
- Drop the now-unused provider-token re-export from `claudeModelSelection`;

commit_message:
tunnels: resume auto-reconnect on desktop and drop dead connections

Auto-reconnect for tunnel-backed agent hosts could pause permanently. After
RECONNECT_MAX_ATTEMPTS consecutive failures `_pauseReconnect` cancels the retry
timer and relies on something later calling `_resumeReconnects`, but its only
triggers were an `online` event and `visibilitychange`, both registered behind
`if (isWeb)`. On desktop the sole remaining caller was an added GitHub auth
session, so a laptop that slept through a network drop stayed paused: the retry
timer was cancelled, and `_handleConnectionChanges` only re-arms it on a fresh
Connected -> Disconnected transition, which can no longer happen once the
connection is already down. The user had to re-run the whole connect workflow by
hand.

Route `IHostService.onDidChangeFocus` into `_resumeReconnects` so both web and
desktop recover on the next window focus, and drop the web-only visibility
listener it subsumes. `_resumeReconnects` is still rate-limited by
RESUME_RATE_LIMIT_MS, so focus churn cannot hammer the relay.

A status check that confirms the host is online now resumes any paused address
rather than only those parked with reason `hostOffline`, which makes the
`_hostOfflinePaused` set redundant. The pause log message claimed recovery
triggers that did not exist on desktop; it now reports the real ones.

Also clear the provider connection when a tunnel transport drops. Only the
SSH/configured-host contribution called `clearConnection()`, so a tunnel
provider kept `_connection` pointing at a dead protocol client and went on
advertising its sessions as openable. Opening one then subscribed over the dead
client and permanently poisoned that editor with "Couldn't open session".
`_wireConnections` must run before `_handleConnectionChanges` for this, since it
reads the previous status to detect the transition; the ordering is commented
and covered by a test that fails if it is reverted.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: connor4312

commit_message:
tunnels: track wired providers instead of inferring from previous status

Detecting a dropped tunnel transport by comparing against `_previousStatuses`
missed a `connected -> connecting -> disconnected` sequence: the intermediate

arrived the predicate no longer saw a previously-connected address and left the
provider bound to the dead client.

Track the addresses whose providers actually hold a connection instead, so the
drop is detected regardless of the states it passes through on the way down.
This also removes the dependency on `_wireConnections` running before

commit_message:
sessions: serve cloud sandbox history when the environment is gone

A managed sandbox's compute can be deleted, and once it is the AHP relay
to it is gone for good. Opening such a session refused to open at all:
the only path to its history ran over that relay, so the user was left
with a session that would not load and no stated reason.

Mission Control mirrors every ActionEnvelope it relays, so the same
history can be rebuilt from `GET /agents/tasks/<id>/events` without the
sandbox. `taskEventReplay` folds those frames back into session and chat
state using the very same reducers the live subscriptions use, so a
replayed session and a live one cannot drift.

Opening a session no longer waits for `/connect` to give up before it can
render. Mission Control blocks on the compute resume before replying, so
that call can occupy its whole budget — measured at ~9s of waiting on a
deleted sandbox while the transcript already sat ready. The connect and
the history fetch now overlap, and whichever lands first decides what the
user sees: the session renders as soon as history arrives (~500ms) and is
settled read-only only once the connect has actually failed. Read-only is
an observable, so a session already on screen loses its composer in place
rather than needing a reopen.

`/connect` is also no longer retried. Mission Control's answer already
reflects the resume it just attempted, so re-asking only repeats the
wait; `202 waking` remains the one polled case, against its own
Retry-After.

`ICloudSandboxCredentialsService` is renamed to `ICloudSandboxApiService`:
it now also reads environment and task records, discovers sessions, and
replays history, so "credentials" no longer described it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Arbitrate introductions through the notice host instead of exclusion groups

The lane host arbitrated between categories, but voice-vs-dictation exclusivity
- arbitration within the onboarding lane - was a second mechanism: a static
process-global exclusion-group map with its own preempt and first-run handback.
Both implemented "put the other one away and give it its showing back", which is
the coupling this PR set out to remove, on exactly the kind of global state that
caused the per-host visibility bug.

A claim now learns when it is the notice actually on screen: the newest claim in
the lowest occupied lane leads, everything else stands down but keeps its claim.
Recency within a category and precedence between categories become one thing.

Introductions claim the space directly and build only once they lead, which
removes the rest of the bookkeeping:

- The first-run key is written when the card is really put in front of the user
  rather than when a card is constructed, so being deferred or put away no
  longer spends the one showing. `_consumedFirstRun`, `_restoredFirstRun` and
  the handback they guarded are gone, and with them the unbounded-restore
  hazard the bound existed to cap.
- Standing down hides the card instead of tearing it down, so in-flight state
  survives and `shown` telemetry is reported once per showing rather than once
  per restore.
- A card put away for a peer now returns when that peer goes away, matching the
  behaviour notifications already had.

ChatInputOnboarding drops from seven interacting pieces of state plus a static
registry to four. Card construction failures are reported rather than rethrown,
since they now run from the host's leading notification and unwinding through it
would strand the claim.

Behaviour note: an explicitly requested introduction now waits for a
higher-precedence notification to clear instead of rendering underneath it.

commit_message:
Settle notice leadership against re-entrant claims

Standing down is a real side effect - it moves focus and hides DOM - so a
claim's callback can change who owns the space while the host is still
announcing. The previous code captured the leader up front and announced it
unconditionally after standing the old one down, so a claim replaced in the
meantime was still told it leads, leaving two notices believing they were on
screen. State is now re-read after every single notification, with a bounded
loop that reports rather than spins if claims never settle.

Also fixes a stranded claim on the failure path: `build()` runs from the host
reporting that we lead, before the lease is in hand, so a card that threw
during construction called `hide()` while `claim.clear()` had nothing to
clear - and the lease was then stored anyway, holding the onboarding lane
forever with no card, silently suppressing tips. The first leading answer is
now held until the lease is stored.

previous code.

commit_message:
editor: don't reindent the line following a pasted block (real-world bug)

The paste range is built as pre-paste cursor to post-paste cursor, so when the
pasted text ends with a line break the range ends at column 1 of the following
line, which holds no pasted characters. AutoIndentOnPaste.trigger applied its
indentation offset up to and including range.endLineNumber, sweeping up that
line.

Skip that line when the paste replaced whole lines only, in which case it is a
pre-existing line pushed down with its indentation intact. When part of a line
was replaced the last line of the range is that line's remainder, which lost its
leading text and does still need reindenting, so it is left as before. Telling
the two apart needs the replaced selection, which IPasteEvent now carries as an
internal field, leaving monaco.d.ts unchanged.

A whitespace only trailing line is skipped as well, since it holds no pasted
characters either; a genuinely empty one is still reindented so the cursor keeps
landing at the pasted block's indentation.

Reported for Ruby in #143573 and for PHP in #221574; the cause is not language
specific.

commit_message:
tunnels: deduplicate dev tunnels and allow managing them

`code tunnel` lowercases the machine name when registering a dev tunnel, but
the in-editor "Allow remote session access" path did not, so a machine named
`Foo-PC` registered as `foo-pc` from the CLI and `Foo-PC` from the editor,
leaving two entries for one machine.

Extract the naming logic both callers had duplicated into a shared
`normalizeTunnelName` that matches the CLI, and have tunnel hosting adopt an
existing idle launcher tunnel of the same name rather than always creating a
new one. Only tunnels we created are deleted on stop, so a tunnel the CLI
persisted is left intact. Adoption is skipped entirely when the tunnel already
carries the right labels and agent host port, and falls back to creating a
tunnel if the service rejects any of the reconciliation.

There was also no way to clean up the duplicates that already exist, so add a
delete button to each entry of the dev tunnel picker, and show whether a tunnel
is online there instead of its protocol version. Add a "Rename Tunnel" command,
linked from the remote session access hover, to set the tunnel name without
having to find the underlying setting.

Fixes #329063

commit_message:
sessions: don't flash sign-in modal at signed-in users during startup

The conditional-auth UI added in #328990 conflated "auth not resolved
yet" with "signed out". IDefaultAccountService.currentDefaultAccount is a
synchronous getter that returns null for everyone until the first async
resolution completes — and that initial resolution fires no change event.
During the startup gap a signed-in user therefore reads as signed-out, so
the sign-in modal and the discovered-config nudge flash. Worse, once auth
finally resolves nothing retires the already-raised modal, so it stays up.

Gate both reactive consumers (sessionsSetUpService and the discovered
config notification) on a resolved-auth signal, learned via a one-shot
getDefaultAccount() await — the only reliable indicator that resolution
happened, since the initial null->account assignment is event-silent.
While unresolved, neither consumer acts, so gap-time Claude native<->proxy
churn is inert and the normal sign-in watch owns the signed-in path.

Consolidate the shared unresolved-vs-signed-out logic both consumers were
duplicating into a unit-tested conditionalAuthState helper. The intended
signed-out conditional-auth behaviour from #328990 is preserved.

commit_message:
sessions: replay usability state once the account resolves

Addresses review feedback: gating _onUsableWithoutGitHubChanged on
_accountResolved dropped any usability transition that landed during the
unresolved window without replaying it. The native paths re-read the
current usability after they await the account (via _showWelcome ->
_mustForceGitHubSignIn), but the web path (_checkWebAuth) has no such
post-resolution re-check, so a genuinely signed-out, opted-in user whose
agent became usable during the gap would stay stranded on the sign-in
dialog that nothing else retires.

When the account resolves, replay the current usability state — scoped to
usable === true, the only transition that was wrongly dropped; a not-usable
state is still owned by the initial setup flow. Signed-in users remain a
no-op (the handler early-returns), so the original fix is unaffected.

commit_message:
Guard model config label against unresolved values

`ModelPickerConfiguration.renderButton` is the single render site every
config-schema producer funnels into — the agent host (via
`AgentHostLanguageModelProvider`), the Copilot CLI sessions, and the LM API.
When a producer cannot resolve a default, the value arrives `undefined` and
was stringified straight into the button as "undefined 272K" (fixed in

Each producer now resolves its own default and is unit-tested for it, but
nothing covered the render site itself, so the user-visible symptom could
regress from any of them.

Add two regression tests for the label:
- a group whose value and schema default are both undefined is dropped from
  the label (and its options stay selectable), and
- when no group resolves a value the button falls back to a generic label
  rather than reading "undefined undefined".

Both fail against the pre-fix guard, reproducing the exact symptom
("undefined 32K"). The per-test setup is hoisted into a `render` helper so
each case is a single snapshot assertion.

commit_message:
Derive the reasoning-effort allow-list from the canonical levels

The Copilot launcher kept its own `ReasoningEfforts` literal, and the model
picker's options are `supportedReasoningEfforts.filter(isCopilotReasoningEffort)`.
When a tier was missing from that private copy it was silently dropped from the
picker — which is how `'max'` went missing (#329167).

The `satisfies readonly ReasoningEffortLevel[]` added there does not prevent a
recurrence: it only verifies each entry is a valid level, not that every level
is present, so omitting a newly-introduced tier still compiles (verified).

Remove the duplication instead: export the canonical `reasoningEffortLevels`
array, derive `ReasoningEffortLevel` from it, and alias the launcher's list to
it so the two cannot drift.

Add tests pinning the invariants a future refactor could break:
- the picker guard recognizes every canonical tier (fails with exactly the
  missing `'max'` when a narrower private allow-list is re-introduced, while
  the pre-existing test still passes), and
- every canonical tier has a localized label and description, so a new tier
  cannot reach the picker raw or undescribed.

commit_message:
agentHost: mirror settings into the host declaratively

Settings that the agent host needs were forwarded by ~15 near-identical
methods in `remoteAgentHostProtocolClient.ts`. Adding one meant editing
four places (a setting-id constant, a config-key constant, a change
handler, and the connect-time forwarder) with nothing enforcing that you
did all four.

A setting now opts in on its own configuration schema, mirroring how
`policy` already works:

    [ChatConfiguration.AutoReply]: {
        type: 'boolean',
        default: false,
        agentHost: { key: AgentHostAutoReplyEnabledConfigKey },
    },

The client drives the whole thing off the configuration registry: it
sends every mirrored setting in a single `RootConfigChanged` action on
connect, and re-sends only the affected key when one changes.

Only globally-scoped values are mirrored - resolution reads `inspect()`
and takes policy, then user, then application, then default, ignoring
workspace and folder values. The host's root config is shared by every
window connected to it, so a workspace value would otherwise leak across
unrelated windows on a last-writer-wins basis. A layer whose value does
not match the declared `type` is skipped, which is what lets the
per-setting `value === true` / `value !== false` coercions go away.

`localOnly: true` restricts mirroring to a local agent host, for values
that describe the client's own machine.

Settings that a single key-plus-transform cannot express stay on the
explicit path: `telemetryLevel` (derived from three settings),
`terminalAutoApproveRules` (two settings, one key), and the
extension-contributed `preferLongContextEnabled` and
`disableRepoInfoTelemetry`. `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove` also
stays explicit on purpose: it is `restricted` and workspace-settable, and
global-only resolution would let a workspace that turned auto-approval
off still have it applied, splitting it from its companion rule set.

Extensions cannot declare `agentHost` from `package.json`; the root
config is shared across windows, so writing to it stays in-code.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
launch skill: add a Windows launcher

`launch.sh` is bash and depends on rsync, curl, and nohup, so the skill
could not be used on Windows. Adds `launch.ps1` alongside it - same
flags, same single-line JSON on stdout, same slim-copy excludes, same
comment-preserving `settings.json` merge, and it still blocks until the
renderer's CDP endpoint answers before printing. `launch.sh` is
unchanged.

The auth model needed rethinking rather than translating. `launch.sh`
assumes auth "comes from the OS keychain (per-app, shared
automatically)", which is a macOS property. Windows has no shared
per-app keychain: the secret material lives inside the user-data-dir, so
it only survives if the copy carries it. The Windows launcher therefore
asserts that `Local State`, `machineid`,
`User/globalStorage/state.vscdb`, and `Network/` all reach the
destination, and fails loudly if any of them do not - `Local State` in
particular has a space in its name and sits at the profile root, which
is easy for a copy implementation to drop silently.

It also warns when the source profile has no stored GitHub session,
since that produces a sign-in prompt in the launched instance that is
otherwise hard to diagnose. The check reads a temporary copy of
`state.vscdb` read-only and looks only for the presence of the key; it
never reads secret values.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
launch skill: address review feedback on the Windows launcher

- Use `ProcessStartInfo.EnvironmentVariables` rather than `Environment`.
  The latter is .NET Core only, so the launcher threw before starting
  Code OSS under Windows PowerShell 5.1 — still the built-in shell, and
  the one the skill tells you to use.

- Detect `files.simpleDialog.enable` against a comment-masked copy of
  `settings.json`. The raw regex also matched a commented-out
  occurrence, so a profile containing
  `// "files.simpleDialog.enable": false` rewrote the comment and
  returned, leaving the launched window on the native file dialog — the
  exact failure the setting exists to prevent. Masking preserves
  offsets, so the value is still rewritten in place, and it respects
  strings so a `//` inside a URL is not treated as a comment. The same
  mask now decides whether the inserted key needs a leading comma,
  which fixes that path for URL-bearing values too.

  `launch.sh` has the same flaw; it is left alone here rather than
  changed untested from Windows.

- Fix Prerequisites still claiming macOS or Linux only, which
  contradicted the Windows instructions further down.

Collapse Voice Mode entitlement gate into a single context key

Negating AGENTS_VOICE_ENABLED for SegmentedVoiceInputModePillInactive

relaunches the workbench to take ~170s and the Electron/Remote/Smoke CI jobs
to time out.

Replace the disjunction with a single agentsVoiceEntitled context key set
imperatively from IChatEntitlementService, so negation no longer expands.

commit_message:
Fix Color Theme picker closing immediately after opening (#329110)

A menu item's onWillRun handler forces focus back to the triggering
element before the item's own command runs. When that command opens
a QuickPick (e.g. Color/File Icon/Product Icon Theme), the picker's
blur-to-close logic can race against that leftover focus churn and
dismiss the picker before the user can interact with it.

Add a one-shot guard that ignores exactly one blur landing in the
same wave as the picker opening, timed to clear one tick after
FocusTracker's own internal blur delay so it can't disarm ahead of
a same-wave blur that's already queued.

Fixes #329110.

commit_message:
Exclude musl os-proxy-resolver binaries from Linux packages

The glibc linux-x64 package was picking up
@vscode/os-proxy-resolver-linux-x64-musl. Its .node links against musl
libc, which has no DT_SONAME, so the linker records the bare filename
and rpm find-requires emits an unsatisfiable 'libc.so()(64bit)'.

os-proxy-resolver 0.3.0 added the musl variants, but they were never
added to the packaging exclusion lists, so nothing stripped them.

Also reverts #329054, which added 'libc.so()(64bit)' to the rpm
reference lists. That unblocked the build but shipped an RPM that no
glibc distro can satisfy, breaking the CentOS and Fedora sanity tests.
author: pwang347

commit_message:
Raise Copilot vitest timeouts to absorb CI agent jitter

The `Run vitest unit tests` step in the Copilot stage has been failing
intermittently on `main` with `Test timed out in 5000ms` across unrelated
suites, taking down the whole build (builds 461369 and 461391 both failed
this way, on different randomly-selected tests).

The tests are not slow — the CI agent is starved. Per-test durations from
the build logs show a *pure synchronous* test (`encodes Cyrillic domain`)
taking 5803ms, a trivial `returns nothing for an empty array` taking
4548ms, and another passing with only 4ms to spare. The run summary
reports 94s wall time against ~1300s of aggregate transform/import/test
CPU time, so forks are being descheduled for seconds at a time and the
5s default fires before a test body is even scheduled.

Neither vitest config set `testTimeout`, so vitest's 5s test / 10s hook
defaults applied. Raise both to 30s, matching the largest per-test
override already in the tree (copilotCLISDKUpgrade.spec.ts). This keeps
enough headroom to absorb agent jitter while still catching genuinely
hung tests.

commit_message:
Agent host owns scoped MCP server enablement

Disabling an MCP server in the agent-host customizations list left the row
showing its previous live state (e.g. "Authentication required") instead of
"Disabled", and the decision did not survive into new sessions.

Enablement was owned client-side and applied to the host only at turn
boundaries, so it raced with MCP server discovery. Move ownership to the host:

- Protocol: `CustomizationEnablement` is a discriminated union over Global /
  Workspace / Session, published sorted by descending specificity so consumers
  can read `enablement[0]` as decisive. `SessionCustomizationToggled` replaces
  the array wholesale.
- Host: a new key/value store persists policy outside the session; a new
  enablement service resolves, persists and propagates it, emitting
  `IContextKeyService`-style predicate-only change events. Disabled servers are
  withheld at launch, and pending auth requests for them are declined
  (interim workaround for github/copilot-mcp-core#2056).
- Client: the local enablement model and per-turn reconcile are gone; the UI
  reads host-published state. Global decisions for VS Code-owned servers only
  gate mirroring, while workspace and session scopes are host-authoritative,
  since those workspaces and sessions exist only on the host.

Three defects surfaced while validating this end to end:

- The publish path resolved only per-session reducer state, so a new session
  published the raw discovered value. Both the row state and the auth-request
  guard read that value, so one cause produced both symptoms.
- `AgentService.createSession` seeds customizations before registering the
  session with the state manager, but the working-directory lookup reads that
  same state manager. It returned undefined, no workspace policy could match,
  and nothing revisited the result. Both resolve paths now fall back to the
  session's customization anchor.
- Policy keys were the customization id, which embeds the materialized plugin
  path including the user-data directory and a content nonce, so a plugin
  change silently orphaned a disable and the server quietly came back. Keys are

commit_message:
Agent host: scope plugin enablement and cascade to children

Plugins already had session-scoped enablement -- the reducer applies a toggle to
any customization, and `SessionPluginController` read the result out of session
state. But `handleToggle` looked its target up with an MCP-only search, so a
plugin toggle silently never persisted. Give plugins the same durable Global and
Workspace scopes MCP servers gained, keyed by the plugin's own id (already its
stable client-published source URI).

A container short-circuits its children: a disabled plugin is now dropped
wholesale from the launch snapshot rather than merely having its `mcpServers`
filtered, so its children reach the SDK at no scope. This also closes the
`pluginDirectories` gap -- a plugin the host never passes cannot have its
`.mcp.json` discovered by the SDK, so plugin-level disable does not depend on
the provider-side API that per-server disable is still waiting on
(github/copilot-mcp-core#2056).

The cascade masks rather than erases. A child of a disabled plugin keeps its own
`enablement` and its own resolved `enabled`, so re-enabling the plugin restores
each child's prior decision instead of silently defaulting it back on. That also
preserves the protocol invariant that `enablement[0]` is decisive for the
customization it appears on: `enabled` answers what that customization's own
scopes decided, and the container gate is applied by consumers and by launch
filtering.

Also fixes a latent bug in the shared resolve path: applying a resolved
enablement spread an object that omits `enablement` when there are no decisions,
which left a stale array on the customization instead of clearing it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Agent host: scoped enable/disable UI for plugins

Adds Enable / Disable, Enable (Workspace) / Disable (Workspace) and
Enable (Session) / Disable (Session) to agent-host plugin rows, each offering the
inverse of the decision currently in effect at that scope. Workspace actions are
hidden when the session has no working directory, matching the MCP rows.

Applies the container cascade on the client: an MCP server child of a disabled
plugin is surfaced as disabled even though its own resolved `enabled` may be
`true`, because the host masks children rather than erasing their decisions.

Fixes plugin toggles never reaching the host from the Agents window. The
sessions-side `setCustomizationEnabled` resolved the incoming id against the
session's MCP servers and dropped it when nothing matched, so a plugin id was
silently discarded. Routing it through a generic `setCustomizationEnablement`
exposed a second issue: the provider unconditionally stripped everything before
the first `/` to remove the `<authority>/` scope MCP ids carry, which corrupted
an unscoped plugin id such as `file:///path/to/plugin` into `//path/to/plugin`
and left the host with no customization to toggle. The scope is now removed only
when the id actually resolved to a known MCP server, via a documented
`unscopeCustomizationId` helper with a regression test.

commit_message:
Agent host: unify customization enablement resolution

Adding plugins to the host-owned enablement model left three separate
resolution paths in `SessionPluginController` -- `_isEnabled`,
`_applyChildEnablement` and `_applyMcpEnablement` -- with `_applyEnablement`
branching on `CustomizationType.Plugin` three times and resolving the container
twice, once directly and once through `_isEnabled`.

Collapse them into a single `_resolveEnablement`. Types that carry durable
policy (MCP servers and plugins) resolve against it with any session decision
layered on top; every other type has only session scope and keeps whatever was
discovered unless the session says otherwise. An absent `enabled` on a leaf
child still stays absent, since absent means enabled.

No behaviour change.
