commit_message:
Negotiate a resource-scoped token when the marketplace gates its index

A Private Marketplace running with authentication enforced refuses its service
index outright unless a token minted for the marketplace itself is presented, so
signing in is not by itself enough to reach it: the sign-in token identifies the
user, but its audience is not the marketplace.

Read the index with the bearer the account already carries. If the marketplace
refuses it, read the Protected Resource Metadata it advertises (RFC 9728) to
learn what a token for it must be minted against, ask the account for one, and
read the index again.

Whether a marketplace needs this is discovered rather than configured: one that
accepts what it is given is never asked what a token for it should look like,
and the GitHub path — which carries no bearer at all — is unaffected.

The resource descriptor is passed to the existing `getAccount`, and the token
comes back on the `accessToken` it already returns, rather than adding a second
way to ask for the same thing. The account is resolved before the token is
minted, so the token belongs to the identity the user chose.

Requests that follow the index are made against the same marketplace and are
gated the same way, so the manifest service exposes the headers to authenticate
them. It decides which origins may receive the bearer, rather than each caller
repeating that rule: a marketplace may serve assets from elsewhere — upstreamed
extensions are fetched from the public marketplace — and those requests must
stay anonymous. The bearer is dropped whenever the marketplace is retracted, so
a sign-out, an account switch or a configuration change cannot leave a usable
one behind.

commit_message:
Consent to the marketplace resource during interactive sign-in

Acquiring the resource-scoped token during a normal access check is silent by
contract, so it cannot ask the user for consent. A user whose tenant has not
already consented to the marketplace's resource scopes would therefore sign in
successfully and still be returned to the sign-in prompt, with nothing in the UI
explaining what was missing.

Ask for that consent while the user is already in an interactive sign-in, using
the resource the marketplace advertised on the request it gated. The silent path
is tried first, so a user who is already consented is not prompted twice.

Failure is not fatal: the identity session stands and the access check reports
whatever the marketplace says next, rather than turning a consent problem into a
failed sign-in.

sessions: decouple BranchPicker from active session via IBranchPickerModel

The BranchPicker was tightly coupled to ICopilotChatSession, requiring
an active session to function. This prevented reuse in contexts without

- IObservable<IBranchPickerModel | undefined> (not concrete class)

- No new service or registry — the model is instance-scoped state

commit_message:
voice: send request_narration only after session context is sent (#325928)

requestNarration only checked that the socket was OPEN, so a focus- or
state-driven narration could be sent in the window between the WebSocket
opening and start_session/resume_session being sent. The backend drops a
request_narration that arrives before the session exists, but the client
still gets a narration id back and treats the audio as inbound: it tears
down listening via _prepareForPlayback, records a solicited narration id,
and arms a safety timer for audio that never comes. The narration is not
queued for replay, so it is lost until the next focus/state event.

commit_message:
Voice: stop passive backend queries from killing auto-listen

Clicking Voice Mode dropped straight to idle instead of staying in listening.
Two independent causes, both fixed here:

- The tool_call handler dispatched every allowed tool the same way, calling
  _finishPtt() and driving the state machine toward idle. The backend fires
  read-only queries (get_session_info/get_session_changes/get_session_thread)
  automatically when it connects, so that probe ended the just-started
  auto-listen the instant it arrived. Answer these passive queries by
  dispatching them and returning the result only, without touching PTT,
  status, awaiting-reply, or voice state.

- _finishPtt() cleared _pttHeld but not _pttToggleMode, so a turn finished
  out-of-band (e.g. by that tool_call mid-listen) left a stale
  `toggle=true, held=false` state. The next auto-listen's synthetic pttDown
  then read as a "second tap" and killed listening immediately. Clear
  _pttToggleMode in _finishPtt so the toggle invariant holds for every
  turn-ending path.

commit_message:
Quick Open: open exact relative paths without waiting for the workspace file search

When a Quick Open query resolves to an existing file relative to a
workspace folder, return it directly instead of waiting for the fuzzy
file search over all workspace files. The search is still started up
front, but a relative-path hit returns without awaiting it, so pasting a
full path (e.g. from a diff or a merge conflict) opens instantly instead
of waiting for a search over the entire workspace.

Previously the relative-path lookup and the fuzzy search ran together via
Promise.all and the result was awaited on both, so the picker always
waited for the workspace search - slow in large repos - even when the
pasted path already pinpointed a single file. Because the search is kept
in flight, a query that does not resolve to a file pays no extra latency.

This mirrors the existing fast path for absolute paths, which already
returns the single stat hit and skips the search. Partial queries that do
not resolve to a file (e.g. `src/foo`) still fall through to the fuzzy
search unchanged.

Behavior change: on an exact relative-path hit the picker now shows only
that file instead of also merging in fuzzy matches.

commit_message:
Fix file handle leak in zip extraction when the source stream errors

extractEntry() pipes the zip entry's read stream into a createWriteStream
target. stream.pipe(istream) does not destroy the destination when the
source errors, so on a corrupt/truncated entry the source 'error' handler
rejected the promise but left istream (the target file handle) open,
leaking the fd and a partially-written file. The cancellation path already
destroys istream; the source-error path did not.

Destroy istream in the source 'error' handler, mirroring the existing
cancellation cleanup.

commit_message:
fix(agentHost): add ECONNRESET/EPIPE/ETIMEDOUT to retry codes (BUG-02); remove forbidden content-length header from fetch path (BUG-06)

BUG-02: AgentHostRequestService had a copy-paste gap in TRANSIENT_ERROR_CODES.
ECONNRESET, EPIPE, and ETIMEDOUT were absent, causing the most common transient
TCP errors to surface as fatal Copilot session failures instead of being silently
retried. Every other component in the codebase (Copilot networking.ts, nodeFetcher.ts,
remoteAgentConnection.ts) already treats all three as retryable.

Also adds three regression tests to agentHostRequestService.test.ts to guard
against the gap being re-introduced.

BUG-06: OtlpHttpForwarder incorrectly set 'content-length' in the Fetch API
branch. Per the Fetch specification (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#forbidden-header-name)
it is a forbidden header name that Node 18+ (undici) and Electron/Chromium
silently discard before the request is sent. The header is kept in the
http.request branch where it is required (Node raw TCP does not auto-compute it).

commit_message:
Break Autopilot handoff auto-fire cycles

Autopilot auto-submits a mode's send:true handoff the instant a response
completes, with no user turn in between (ChatWidget#renderChatSuggestNextWidget).
If a handoff chain cycles back on itself - e.g. agent A's auto-send handoff
lands on agent B, whose response again offers that same handoff back to A -
nothing stops Autopilot from resubmitting it forever. Each cycle is a fully
completed, billed turn, and looks like a normal finished response in the UI
(retry/thumbs icons and all), so there's no visible signal anything is wrong
until a budget cap is hit.

Track the id of the last handoff Autopilot auto-fired and refuse to fire the
same one again immediately after. Legitimate multi-step chains (plan ->
implement -> verify, a different handoff each time) are unaffected; only an
exact repeat is suppressed, falling back to showing the handoff as a normal
clickable suggestion so the user can still drive it manually.

Fixes #325440
author: Alexoswin

commit_message:
Replace handoff-identity cycle guard with a consecutive-attempt cap

Self-review of the previous commit found two real gaps in the id-based
cycle guard:

1. The guard field lived on ChatWidget but was never reset when the same
   widget instance got reattached to a different session (setModel /
   the viewModel setter). A stale "last fired handoff" from one session
   could spuriously suppress a brand new, unrelated session's first
   legitimate auto-handoff.

2. More fundamentally, comparing handoff *identities* (agent + label)
   across turns has a blind spot: two differently-labeled handoffs
   pointing at each other (e.g. "Implement" from plan -> implement,
   "Review" from implement -> plan) never share an id, so an A <-> B
   loop built that way - which is if anything the more natural way to
   author a back-and-forth handoff - would never be detected at all.

Replaced it with a plain counter: how many send:true handoffs Autopilot
has auto-fired in a row with no human turn in between, capped at
AUTOPILOT_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_AUTO_HANDOFFS. This needs no assumption about
handoff ids lining up across hops, so it bounds any unbounded chain -
repeating or not, same ids or different - not just the specific shape
the earlier check happened to catch. It resets on any non-auto-fired
turn, on leaving Autopilot, and on session switch, and still falls back
to showing the handoff as a manual suggestion once suppressed rather
than doing nothing.

Rewrote the unit tests against the new signature and added coverage for
the session-switch reset and the different-id cycle shape the previous
approach would have missed.

commit_message:
agent host e2e: reuse one replay server per suite for Copilot

The agent host e2e replay suite restarted the whole server (and re-spawned
the provider SDK/CLI subprocess) for every test. Profiling showed the
dominant per-test cost is server fork (~0.5s) plus the provider SDK client
cold start (~0.5s, an ~8MB CLI bundle loaded on the Electron-as-node
binary), with session teardown effectively free.

Reuse one server across the suite for providers that can be returned to a
clean state via disposeSession, swapping the per-test replay fixture on the
in-process CapiReplayProxy without restarting (the proxy URL the agent host
was forked against stays fixed):

- CapiReplayProxy: add resetForReplay (re-point at a new fixture, clear
  replay buckets + cache-miss log), assertNoCacheMisses (verify strict
  replay without stopping), and close (drop the socket without the strict
  check). stop() now composes these.
- Add AgentHostE2EServerLease to encapsulate per-test vs shared strategies,
  gated by a new supportsSharedReplayServer provider flag (replay only;
  recording always uses a fresh proxy + fixture per test).
- Enable it for Copilot. Claude stays per-test: its mid-turn dispose can
  wedge the shared agent host process, which per-test kill-and-refork
  isolation guards against.
- Drain the permission test's post-tool continuation to turnComplete in all
  modes so the session ends cleanly before dispose (returning mid-turn would
  wedge the reused client).

Copilot suite drops from ~29s to ~14s mocha time. Claude and Codex are
unchanged (per-test path).

commit_message:
agent host e2e: enable the shared replay server for Claude and Codex

Investigated the long-standing "Claude mid-turn dispose wedges the agent
host" caveat that kept server reuse Copilot-only. It dates from the live
real-SDK era (real streaming turns actually in flight). In today's
deterministic replay suite there is no mid-turn dispose: the abort test is
record-only and every turn drains to `turnComplete` before teardown.

Deliberately reproducing the old failure (reverting the permission test's
drain) showed it is not a process wedge at all but a strict cache miss: an
undrained turn's continuation HTTP call fires after the fixture is swapped
and lands in the next test's window as an unrecorded call. The proxy detects
it loudly. The cure is exactly the drain already in place, so with every turn
drained there is nothing to leak.

Enable `supportsSharedReplayServer` for Claude and Codex (verified green and
stable across repeated runs; Claude ~16s -> ~9s, Codex likewise). Correct the
drain rationale and the README/lease/flag comments to describe the real
mechanism (leaked async traffic) instead of the "wedge" folklore.

commit_message:
agent host e2e: drop supportsSharedReplayServer, share by default in replay

The flag was true for all three providers, so it modeled the wrong thing: a
per-provider capability, when the real requirement is a per-test invariant
(drain your turns) that every provider already meets. Server reuse is really
a property of replay mode, gated only by recording (which needs a fresh proxy
per fixture).

Remove the flag and make the lease share by default in replay
(`_shared = !RECORD`). No behavior change (all three suites already reused the
server); this just deletes dead config and the misleading "some providers
can't share" framing. Single-test isolation for diagnosing a cross-test leak
is still available via `--grep`.

commit_message:
Preserve chat input text typed while a session is loading (#325323)

A chat widget's input editor stays visible and editable while its session
loads asynchronously, but no view model is bound yet. When the model finally
binds, it resets the editor to the session's own (usually empty) draft, which
discarded whatever the user typed in the meantime. The placeholder decoration
also stayed rendered on top of the typed text during loading.

Add a shared `setModelPreservingInputTypedWhileLoading` helper used by the
editor, sessions, and panel chat hosts to carry newly-typed text across the
model bind (without clobbering a persisted draft or a previous session's
leftover draft), and clear the placeholder decoration when there is input text
but no bound view model yet.

commit_message:
chat: flush queued/steering messages when a streamed session turn completes

Contributed chat sessions whose in-progress turn is streamed via
activeResponseCallback (progressObs) — e.g. Copilot cloud sessions —
register a synthetic pending request while streaming. A message sent
mid-turn is therefore queued as a steering/queued message. The
streaming-completion branch in loadRemoteSession deleted that pending
request without flushing the queue, so the queued message was stranded
in the model forever and never sent (steering 'limbo').

Mirror the normal request-completion path by calling
processPendingRequests when the streamed turn completes. It is a no-op
while another request is in flight and returns early for server-managed
(agent-host) queues, so it is safe on every completion tick.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: osortega

commit_message:
chat: true mid-turn steering for cloud sessions

Builds on the queued-message flush fix to inject a steer into a live
cloud turn instead of only sending it after the turn settles, matching
github.com/copilot/agents.

Core (chatServiceImpl): for non-server-managed streamed
(activeResponseCallback) sessions, dispatch a queued Steering message
immediately when the in-flight pending request is the synthetic
streamed-turn tracker (no requestId) — never over a real in-flight
request. Re-establish tracking on the next progress tick so the turn
stays in-progress.

Extension (copilotCloudSessionsProvider):
- Track live TaskTurnStreamer taskIds; when a stream is already active,
  handleTaskFollowUp only POSTs /steer and lets the running stream
  render the injected result (no second streamer).
- Make the follow-up stream yield-aware (mirrors the Copilot CLI
  provider): poll context.yieldRequested and return on yield so the
  chat service flushes the next steer immediately.
- Choose the render mode from the pre-steer task state: a steer into an
  active turn renders mode:'current' (the injection has no new
  task.sessions[] row, so mode:'next' would time out); a steer onto a
  settled task renders mode:'next'.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
MCP: fix infinite sign-in loop for servers that grant scopes but advertise none

`TokenStore._getSessionFromToken` derived a session's scopes with a truthiness
check on `token.scope`. When a session is created for an empty scope request,
`createSession` (and the refresh path) overwrite `token.scope` with the requested
value, i.e. the empty string. Because `''` is falsy, the deriver ignored the
stored value and fell back to the granted scopes embedded in the JWT claims.

For a server that advertises no scopes but still grants some (e.g. Descope-backed
MCP servers), this produced a session whose scopes were non-empty even though the
request — and every subsequent lookup — used empty scopes. `getSessions` filters
by exact scope-array equality, so the session could never be found: each request
re-triggered a full sign-in, looping forever. Servers that advertise scopes, or
that don't embed scopes in the token's JWT, never hit the seam.

Honor an explicitly-set (possibly empty) `token.scope` and only fall back to the
JWT claims when `scope` is genuinely absent (`undefined`).

Adds a TokenStore unit test covering all three cases (empty, absent, non-empty
scope) through the public `sessions` getter.

commit_message:
Voice: fix session-state storm and confirmation narration preemption

Two fixes to voice-mode session narration in the Agents window, both found
via trace logs:

1. Coalesce session state-change emission. Loading/opening a remote session
   replays its history, which briefly re-opens the last response and makes the
   computed agent_state flip thinking<->idle many times within milliseconds.
   Each flip was flushed to the backend as a real agent_state delta, spamming
   it with contradictory transitions. Buffer transitions per session and flush
   once after a short settle window so an oscillation that returns to its prior
   state produces no delta; only a genuine net transition ships.

2. Recover confirmation narration preempted by a competing narration. The
   backend narrates one proactive event at a time. When two sessions reach
   waiting_for_confirmation and one produces a response, focusing the other
   confirmation ships a correct thinking->waiting_for_confirmation transition
   but the backend drops it while narrating the response, and the session never
   transitions again so it is lost. Detect a competing tagged narration for a
   different session and re-assert the still-active/still-awaiting confirmation
   once (guarded, one-shot). Marked as an interim client mitigation; the real
   fix is backend-side narration serialization.

Also add trace diagnostics (per-delta agent_state, activation state, received
tool calls, approve/reject outcome) to aid further voice debugging. The
approve/reject backend result is preserved as 'ok'; only logging is added.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Voice: cache response summary so unfocused completions still narrate

Copilot/remote session models are disposed as soon as the user switches
away. A response that completes while its session is unfocused was therefore
reported to the backend as a summary-less idle, and the eager reload to
recover last_response_summary raced the switch's re-disposal — so the
completion was never narrated (observed with two sessions and rapid
switching: neither response was read).

Cache last_response_summary per session while its model is resident, keyed
by session id and independent of the model's lifetime. The no-model idle
paths now report the cached summary instead of a summary-less idle (and skip
the eager-reload defer when a summary is cached). The cache is refreshed on
every resident idle and cleared when the session starts a new turn
(thinking) so a stale reply is never narrated; falls back to the existing
eager-reload defer when no summary was captured.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

commit_message:
Voice: hold summary-less idle until eager-reloaded model replays response

Fix 3's summary cache only fills when a model is resident at completion. Under
rapid session switching the model is disposed while still thinking and the
completion lands after disposal, so the cache misses and we eagerly reload the
model to recover last_response_summary. That reloaded model is briefly resident
with an EMPTY response while its history is still replaying, and we were
shipping a summary-less idle immediately — consuming the idle transition before
the summary existed. By the time the session was focused the model had the
summary, but agent_state was already idle so the merge-patch wobble-guard
dropped it: the completion was never narrated.

Add _effectiveResidentState: while an eager reload is in flight and the resident
model still reports idle with an empty summary, report the prior state to hold
the idle until it can carry the summary. Applied in processModel,
_buildSessionContext and _checkSessionStateChanges; _pendingIdleNarration is now
cleared only when not holding. The eager load always resolves (its callback
clears _eagerModelLoading), so the hold can never last forever — a genuinely
empty response ships a bare idle once the load completes.

This makes unfocused completions narrate reliably client-side (verified: the
held session ships thinking->idle+summary once replay finishes and is read on
focus), no longer depending on the backend narrating a summary-less idle.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Address review: net-change coalescing, cache eviction, log hygiene

- Track each state-change burst's baseline (fromState/fromDetail) so
  _emitPendingStateChanges only traces/persists true net changes. A net-zero
  wobble (thinking->idle->thinking) no longer persists a phantom coding_event
  (which would replay to the backend on reconnect) and detail changes reached
  via an intermediate state (waiting(old)->thinking->waiting(new)) are now
  correctly treated as detail-only (cache invalidated).
- Don't stage the intermediate (glitching) state via _sendContext while a burst
  is being coalesced; a flushSessionContext() during the settle window (e.g.
  _activateShownSession) would otherwise ship the wobble and bypass coalescing.
- Evict per-session summary cache for sessions no longer tracked (archived/
  removed/disposed) via _pruneSessionCaches, so a long-lived voice connection
  doesn't retain unbounded responses.
- Truncate session ids in the _activateShownSession trace (slice(-32)) to match

commit_message:
Harden Entra marketplace access: cache scoping, race guards, error handling

Address rubber-duck review findings on the Entra ID marketplace path:

- Scope the cached access verdict to the marketplace it was computed against
  (authProvider + accountId + serviceUrl), rejecting stale caches on any mismatch.
- Guard cache application and background validation with a monotonic epoch so a
  session/account/config change mid-validation supersedes an in-flight result.
- Register session/account listeners before applying the cache, and the config
  listener before initial validation, closing startup TOCTOU windows.
- Route transient auth-service and marketplace-fetch failures to Unreachable
  instead of leaving a configured marketplace on a blank Unavailable view.
- Split 401 (missing/expired token -> RequiresSignIn, not cached) from 403

- Never follow redirects on token-bearing requests; only send the Entra token to
  an HTTPS same-origin target; reject non-2xx and non-manifest 200 responses
  before parsing.
- Restore the galleryservice:custom:marketplace telemetry on the GitHub path and
  drop the unused server-provided eligibility reason from persisted cache.

Expand unit coverage to 45 tests across provider routing, eligibility, caching,
error classification, and the epoch race paths.

- extensionGalleryAccessValidator.ts: provider-agnostic orchestrator.

A marketplace can refuse the client outright — for example one enforcing a
minimum supported VS Code version replies 400 "Only VS Code clients version
1.104.2 or later are allowed". That is durable: retrying cannot help.

Such a response was classified as a transient failure and surfaced as
"The Extensions Marketplace is currently unavailable. Check your network
connection", which points the user at something that is not the problem. On main
any failed fetch of a configured marketplace reports AccessDenied ("please
contact your administrator"), so this was also a regression in what the user is
told.

Classify a non-401/403 4xx as a new MarketplaceClientRejectedError and map it to
a denial, restoring the message main gives. 5xx and network failures stay
transient and continue to report Unreachable. The denial is deliberately not
cached: it belongs to the client, not the account, and can change on upgrade.

commit_message:
marketplace: give the account service one job, and the manifest service the rest

Review feedback on the previous split: the account service should answer whether
there is a usable account, and nothing else. It was still fetching the service
index, so its verdict carried a manifest and it needed the marketplace URL —
neither of which is its concern.

Account service now resolves identity and entitlement only:

    readonly accountStatus: ExtensionGalleryAccountStatus;
    readonly onDidChangeAccountStatus: Event<ExtensionGalleryAccountStatus>;
    getAccount(): Promise<IExtensionGalleryAccount | undefined>;
    readonly onDidChangeAccount: Event<void>;
    setPreferredAccount(accountId: string): void;
    connectAuthentication(authenticationService: IAuthenticationService): void;

It no longer takes a serviceUrl or a CancellationToken, returns no manifest, and
owns no index cache. getAccount returns the signed-in account even when it is not
entitled, so callers can scope a durable denial to it; accountStatus says whether
it may be used. The marketplace auth-provider context key moves here too, which
also removes a second call to getEffectiveAuthProvider.

The manifest service now owns the marketplace side: the serviceUrl, the
non-HTTPS token-target check, the index fetch, resolution generations, and the
mapping from outcome to ExtensionGalleryManifestStatus.

The durable access verdict moves to a new ExtensionGalleryAccessCache rather than
into either service, so neither carries storage plumbing and the scoping rules —
a verdict is only honoured for the account, marketplace and auth provider it was
written for — live in one testable place. It resolves the effective auth provider
itself via getEffectiveAuthProvider, a pure function, rather than requiring a new
member on the account service.

Two ordering bugs surfaced while testing this and are fixed here: the
configuration-change listener was registered after the initial resolution, so a
change during a slow index fetch was missed entirely; and a transient failure to
resolve the account discarded the cached verdict that a later retry needs.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged, verified against a deployed private marketplace
and by the existing suite.

commit_message:
Fold the service index fetch back in and drop the access cache

The index fetcher only existed to hold a memo that could never be hit:
resolve() invalidated it immediately before its single read. With no
state left it returns to a private method on the manifest service.

The durable access cache is removed. Its `true` verdict was never read,
and the `false` written for a client-side ineligible account outlived
the condition it recorded - an account later granted entitlement stayed
AccessDenied until sign-out. Covered by a new regression test.

isSafeTokenTarget was called with the same URL for both arguments, so
only its HTTPS check ever ran; it becomes an inline guard. Redirects are
already handled by followRedirects: 0. MarketplaceMisconfiguredError was
never thrown and is gone.

The configuration listener returns to its shape on main, with the auth
provider key added. renderAvailable becomes setAvailable. Comment volume
across these files drops from 24% to 8%, against 4% in the surrounding
extensionManagement code.

commit_message:
Publish the catalog on every successful resolve

A private marketplace is account-scoped, but the success path skipped
publishing whenever the status was already Available. Switching to a
different eligible account therefore fetched that account's catalog and
then discarded it, leaving the previous account's in place until
restart. The manifest is now published on every success; the
custom-marketplace telemetry still fires only on the transition into
Available.

Removing the access cache orphaned IExtensionGalleryAccount.id - it
existed only to scope a cached verdict to an account - so it goes, along
with the comment describing the verdict it scoped.

That removal also took with it the only test asserting that an
already-available marketplace survives a transient failure. Restored for
both the fetch and the account-resolution paths.

commit_message:
sessions: default the single-pane side pane to 60% and persist its width reliably

Make the single-pane side pane (docked editor part) open at a comfortable
60% of the window width and keep its size workbench-wide across session
switches and reloads.

- First reveal of the side pane uses 60% of the window width
  (`INITIAL_EDITOR_WIDTH_RATIO`) instead of a 50% main-area split.
- Side-pane width is workbench-global (`workbench.sessions.partSizes`), so
  switching sessions keeps the same width; hiding the pane in one session no
  longer resets another session's width on return.
- Fix persistence: `_persistedGridViewSize` is a single overridable read for
  all parts, and single-pane returns its docked auxiliary-bar width from the
  docked layout state instead of the grid (the docked aux bar is not a grid
  view, so reading it threw 'View not found' and aborted the whole save,
  losing the editor width).
- Restore-side guards a stale/corrupt sub-minimum saved editor width (e.g. a
  persisted 0) by falling back to the default instead of collapsing to the
  300px minimum on reload.
- `_persistedEditorWidth` subtracts the docked detail width only when the
  detail is visible, mirroring the grid descriptor, so an Editor-only session
  no longer shrinks by the detail width on every reload.
- Double-clicking the chat/side-pane sash resets the side pane to 60% via a
  `preferredWidth` on `SinglePaneMainEditorPart` (single-pane only; the
  classic layout keeps the standard distribute).

commit_message:
sessions: remember Changes editor view state across scenarios

The Agents-window single-pane Changes editor (SessionChangesEditor) extended
plain EditorPane and never persisted its multi-diff view state, so per-file
collapsed state, scroll position, selections and the active file were lost on
window reload, session switch, side-pane toggle, and reopening the editor.

- SessionChangesEditor now extends AbstractEditorWithViewState, keyed by the
  per-session multiDiffSource resource, tracking disposed state so it survives
  the tab being closed/disposed on a session switch. It also persists on hide
  and defers focus until the active diff editor renders.
- Persist the active diff item in IMultiDiffEditorViewState and restore it once
  the (possibly async) diffs load, which suppresses the widget's automatic
  first-change navigation so restored scroll/collapsed state wins.
- Apply the view model and restored view state in a single transaction so the
  first-change navigation sees the restored active item instead of navigating to
  and focusing the first file. This also fixes the same latent ordering bug in
  the standard workbench MultiDiffEditor.

commit_message:
Codex: preserve legacy permission axes on session restore

resolveSessionConfig previously returned only the visible {Mode,
PermissionsPreset} keys. Since that return REPLACES the stored session
config on restore, a pre-preset session that persisted only the raw
sandboxMode/approvalPolicy axes (e.g. read-only) had a materialized
permissionsPreset='default' inserted on top of it and lost its legacy
axes, silently resuming as workspace-write. It also dropped every other
persisted setting (reasoning effort, personality, …) back to defaults.

Fix: preserve the full persisted config and migrate only the permission
axes. An explicit preset is kept; legacy axes that map exactly onto a
preset are migrated to it; legacy axes with no equivalent preset (e.g.
read-only) are preserved verbatim with no preset so resolveCodexPermissions
keeps applying the legacy fallback (no escalation).

Adds presetForResolvedPermissions (common, protocol-free) and
migrateCodexPermissionValues (node) plus regression tests.

commit_message:
MCP: preserve authorization server context on auth re-validation

When AuthenticationService fires onDidChangeSessions for a provider,
MainThreadMcp re-validates every tracked MCP server using that provider. That
re-validation was calling _getSessionForProvider with authorizationServer (and
resource/clientId/audience/clientSecret) dropped, so the silent token request
lost the tenant-specific authority the session was created with and fell back
to the provider default -- e.g. the Microsoft provider's `organizations`
tenant. Depending on the account/tenant relationship this either silently
targets the wrong authority or, for a single-tenant app with a B2B guest,
fails and tears down an otherwise-working MCP server.

Capture the auth context (authorization server, client id, resource, audience,
and the secret-storage key -- not the secret value) when a server's session is
established, and replay it on re-validation. The secret is re-read from storage
by key so a secret rotated via the "Set Client Secret" code lens takes effect
immediately instead of replaying a stale value.

Adds a McpServerAuthTracker unit test covering context round-trip, replacement,
and untracking.

Fixes #324925

commit_message:
Stop session/customizationsChanged log spam in agent host

The agent host was emitting thousands of `session/customizationsChanged`
envelopes (bursts of ~100+/second) during active Claude turns. Two
compounding causes, fixed here:

1. ClaudeCustomizationWatcher recursively watched `~/.claude` and treated
   *any* change under it as a customization change. But the Claude SDK
   constantly rewrites runtime data there (history.jsonl, projects/
   transcripts, tasks/, file-history/, shell-snapshots/, sessions/,
   caches). The recursive watch is kept (cheap on OS watchers), but the
   change *triggers* are now narrowed to an allowlist of the actual
   customization sources (agents, skills, commands, rules, plugins,
   CLAUDE.md, settings.json, settings.local.json) plus the existing
   `.mcp.json` / memory-file triggers.

2. `_publishSessionCustomizations` dispatched unconditionally. A single
   edit under the shared `~/.claude` tree fans out to every open session
   and is republished once per session, so one change emitted O(N^2)
   identical envelopes. Added a per-session dedup guard (mirroring
   `_publishAgentInfos`) that skips the dispatch when the resolved
   customizations are unchanged, with the dedup cache pruned against the
   live session set on each publish cycle.

Verified live via the Agents window: a full Claude turn now emits 1
customizationsChanged (was ~1084/session); heavy runtime churn under
`~/.claude` with 3 active sessions emits 0; and real customization edits
(add/rename/delete) still propagate.

server is `Ready`, the AHP `mcp://` channel is also available at start,

provides one), so the chat UI can mount the MCP App surface for a running
tool instead of waiting for completion.

  "re-emit when the server becomes Ready" machinery

  re-emission that only existed to support it.

  running tool calls; confirmation-gated tools mount on the

commit_message:
Voice: canonicalize deferred-session ids and fix first on-focus read

The voice backend tags a background (unfocused) session's audio with its
bare backend id (e.g. copilotcli:/<id>) in the main window, while focus
tracking, the deferred-response buffer keys, and the sessions-list pending
indicator all operate in the UI agent-host resource space
(agent-host-<provider>:/<id>). A deferred response was therefore keyed by an
id that never matched the resource we flush on focus, so it stayed buffered
forever and was never read when the session became focused.

Maintain a controller-owned backend->UI alias map (rebuilt from the live
session list, cleared on disconnect) and canonicalize each incoming
coding_session_id once so defer/flush/pending keys share one id space.

Also fix _isStaleRenarration wrongly dropping the FIRST narration of a
now-active session. The backend defers a background session's narration
until it becomes active, so that reply legitimately arrives on focus and is
the single on-focus read the user expects. Only drop when a reply for the
session was already heard (recorded in _lastHeardTranscriptById). Without
this the first delivery was swallowed and the state machine never advanced
to speaking/auto-listen, leaving no mic indicator and nothing read.

Downgrade the verbose [voice] diagnostic logs from info to trace.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

commit_message:
Voice: unify re-narration dedup on content, drop _isStaleRenarration

_isStaleRenarration was a content-blind filter that dropped ANY on-focus
reply for a now-active session once any reply had been heard from it. Because
the backend defers a background session's narration server-side until the
session becomes active, a genuinely NEW reply for an unfocused session arrives
as an on-focus narration when the user switches back - and the content-blind
filter swallowed it, so new responses stopped being read after the first.

Replace both re-narration filters with a single content-matched check
(_isRenarration): drop an on-focus reply only when its transcript matches a
reply we recently read for that session AND it arrives within the dedup
window. A new reply (different text) always plays; a later identical reply
plays once the window lapses. The dedup marker is now also armed when a live
reply finishes (not just on buffer-flush/activation), so the immediate backend
re-narration that follows a live reply is still deduped.

commit_message:
git: honor git.detectWorktrees when opening linked worktrees

A linked worktree of an already-open repository was always treated as being
inside the workspace by isRepositoryOutsideWorkspace(), so it was opened as a
separate repository in Source Control regardless of git.detectWorktrees (default
false) or git.openRepositoryInParentFolders. Worktrees discovered via an open
editor, the file system watcher, or the extension API therefore appeared even
when the user had opted out.

Gate the in-workspace treatment of worktrees on git.detectWorktrees so that,
when detection is disabled, a worktree the user did not explicitly open follows
the same git.openRepositoryInParentFolders rules as any other repository outside
the workspace.

commit_message:
Agent host: apply capability overrides to the runtime process and resumed sessions

The `family` alias only re-routed the agent host's own prompt registry, so an
aliased preview model still got the runtime's default per-model config (its
system-prompt parts, capabilities and reasoning-effort profile). The runtime
resolves that from `service.agent.modelFamily`, which is process-scoped and
reachable only through `COPILOT_MODEL_FAMILY` — there is no per-session SDK or
protocol field for it. Lower the `*` entry's family (the only model-independent
one) onto the CLI subprocess env, restarting the client when it changes, and
validate its shape first: the setting is workspace-configurable, and a value
carrying a NUL makes `spawn` throw, which would take down every session in the
window.

Also send a configured reasoning-effort override on session resume. The SDK
forwards `reasoningEffort` on `session.resume` as well as `session.create`, but
the launcher only set it for a create, so the setting did nothing for existing
sessions until their model changed. Only a configured override is sent, so a
session without one still keeps the effort the runtime persisted.

Finally, let a session with no chosen model (server-side "Auto") match the `*`
entry: it has no model-id entry to look up, and exempting it made the wildcard
mean "every model except Auto" for both effort and tool filters.

commit_message:
Add send_message server tool

Adds a send_message tool that starts a new turn on an existing session or chat,
reusing the same startPrompt path create_session/create_chat use to deliver their
first message. Accepts a list_sessions URI or an agent-host-session:// link; a
create_chat link (with ?chat=) targets that specific peer chat, otherwise the
session's default chat. Requires confirmation, refuses messaging the current chat
channel (self-loop guard), and has a process-wide fan-out backstop. Renders the
same 'Open Session' pill (conversation icon when chat-scoped) and is unpinned from
the thinking group like the other session tools.

commit_message:
sessions: add get_session_context tool + list_sessions single-session lookup (#325158)

Add get_session_context tool and list_sessions single-session lookup

Adds a read-only get_session_context server tool that returns a compacted
transcript of an existing session/chat's recent turns, read directly from live
chat state. Three fidelity levels: summary (per-turn message + short reply
gist), digest (full reply text + tool-call names), full (+ tool-call inputs);
bounded by transcriptLimit (default 10, max 50) with hasMoreHistory/truncated
flags and the in-progress turn included. Deterministic only, no plan/todo
heuristics. Targets a session's default chat, or a specific peer chat via a
create_chat open link.

Also extends list_sessions with an optional session argument for a direct
single-session lookup by URI / open link (bypassing the other filters), so
session metadata stays with list_sessions while get_session_context focuses
purely on conversation data.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Add voice mode to the new-session welcome composer

The welcome composer uses a hand-built toolbar (not the standard ChatWidget),
so the shared voice controls never appeared there. Add full voice support:

  `setupVoiceInputDecorations` helper and reuse it in both the active-session

- New `newChatVoice.ts`: a voice toolbar menu for the composer, an

commit_message:
Route agents-window voice by the authoritative active session

The shared voice controller infers the active session from chat-widget focus
and a last-shown heuristic, both of which are unreliable in the Agents window
where multiple chat widgets render at once and DOM focus stays on the sessions
list. This misroutes audio: a deferred response for a session isn't flushed
when the user opens it (the pending-voice indicator click leaves it silent),
and is_active can point at the wrong session so background idle narrations
fire for a session the user is actually viewing.

Add IVoiceSessionController.setActiveSessionShown(resource) as an authoritative
override that takes precedence over the focus/last-shown heuristics, and drive
it from a single sessions-window contribution watching ISessionsService.
activeSession (undefined for a draft welcome session). Setting it flushes any
buffered response and re-sends context so is_active tracks the viewed session
immediately.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

commit_message:
Make agents-window voice the sole source of the active session

The shared voice controller defers a response for any session that isn't the
active one and flushes it when that session is shown/focused. In the main
window a single chat widget makes focus and view-model tracking reliable, but
the Agents window renders many chat widgets at once (including background and
preview slots). Their view-model swaps drove _onSessionShown, which flushed
deferred responses for sessions the user wasn't actually looking at and
thrashed the last-shown/focused active-session heuristics - so pending
responses were read immediately instead of waiting for their session to be
focused again.

Once an embedder calls setActiveSessionShown (the Agents window, a separate
workbench instance with its own controller), switch the controller into an
external-active-session mode: ignore focus- and widget-view-model-driven
activation and compute the active session solely from the explicit target or
the externally-declared session. Deferral and the flush-on-focus now behave
like the main window.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

commit_message:
Fix delayed confirmation narration and stale-reply replay on session switch

When switching to a session awaiting confirmation whose model wasn't
resident, the controller reported 'thinking' and kicked off an async
model load but never re-sent context after it finished, so the pending
confirmation only shipped on the next unrelated context send (minutes
later). Re-send context immediately when an eager model load completes.

Also, switching to an idle session let the backend re-narrate its
already-heard reply (the deferred-buffer dedupe never armed in hands-free
mode). Record each session's last-heard reply transcript and arm the
re-narration dedupe on activation so a matching backend re-read is
dropped instead of replaying stale content.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

commit_message:
Get session-switch voice narration working

Switching between sessions in the agents window now narrates correctly:

- Track the awaited reply per-session (_awaitingReplyForSession) so a reply
  the user solicited for one session is not confused with an unsolicited
  narration surfacing for another session on focus.
- Replace the fragile time-window stale-drop with a deterministic rule: a
  first-chunk narration tagged to the focused session plays only when it is
  solicited (the user just spoke to THAT session) or the session is awaiting
  confirmation; any other on-focus narration (an old reply, or a command that
  was aborted when the user switched away) is stale and dropped, along with
  its continuation chunks.
- Replies produced while a session is not focused are still buffered and
  replayed when that session regains focus.

All gated to the sessions/agents window (_externalActiveSessionMode); the
main window's behavior is untouched.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Fix voice controls hidden while connection stays active

The disconnect/stop/connecting/settings voice controls were gated on a
per-widget agentsVoiceInitiatedHere context key, but the voice connection
is global (one controller/websocket per window). When the initiating chat
widget was recreated or focus moved to another chat/session, none of those
controls appeared even though voice stayed connected and kept narrating the
focused session's activity — so the UI looked disconnected while audio
still played.

Gate the active-voice controls on the global connected/listening/connecting
keys instead, so any Chat input truthfully reflects the live connection and
always offers a way to stop it. Remove the now-unused agentsVoiceInitiatedHere
key and its per-widget set/clear plumbing.

commit_message:
Narrate pending confirmation on first focus in the main window

The on-focus confirmation re-narration split (flip is_active while holding
the session as thinking, then send waiting_for_confirmation so the backend
narrates it) was gated to _externalActiveSessionMode, so only the sessions
window got it. In the main window, focusing an unfocused session that showed
the pending-response indicator shipped the confirmation and is_active in the
same delta; the backend narrated only on the next activation, so it was read
on the second focus rather than the first.

Run the same split in both modes; keep only the embedder-specific dedupe
arming gated to _externalActiveSessionMode.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

commit_message:
Key confirmation phase-2 timers per session so narration isn't stranded

The on-focus confirmation narration split (phase 1: flip is_active while
holding the session as thinking; phase 2: send waiting_for_confirmation so
the backend narrates) used a single shared _confirmationActivateTimer.
Activating a second confirmation session before the first's 250ms phase-2
fired cancelled the first timer via clearTimeout, leaving that session stuck
reporting thinking — so it was narrated only on the next (second) focus, not
the first. This reproduced in the agents window, which already ran the split.

Key the phase-2 timers per session so each activation completes its own
transition independently, and delete only that session's forceThinking flag
on fire. Combined with running the split in both windows, a pending
confirmation is now narrated on the first focus in both the main and agents
windows.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

commit_message:
Suppress pending-voice indicator for the active session, not raw focus

_reconcileConfirmationIndicators hid the sessions-list mic indicator for
_getFocusedSessionId() (chatWidgetService.lastFocusedWidget), which the
controller itself treats as unreliable in embedder-driven mode. In the
agents window this could match a background session awaiting confirmation
and wrongly suppress its indicator, so a second pending session showed no
mic icon.

Use the embedder-aware _getActiveSessionId() instead so only the session the
user is actually viewing is suppressed; it falls back to focus in the main
window, preserving existing behavior there.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
author: meganrogge

commit_message:
Fix over-suppressed pending-voice indicator

The previous fix used _getActiveSessionId() to pick the session whose
indicator to suppress, but its fallback chain (_targetSession /
_lastShownSessionId / focus) can resolve to a session that isn't currently
visible — so a pending session that was merely last-shown had its indicator
hidden, making the indicator vanish when it should show.

Suppress strictly the currently-viewed session: _activeSessionShown in the
agents window (embedder-authoritative) and _getFocusedSessionId() in the
main window (its original source), without the broader fallbacks.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
Voice: don't stop hands-free listening when switching sessions without dictation

The chat view transcript autorun called stopListening() whenever the current
session changed while voiceState was 'listening'. Clicking New Chat while idly
listening hands-free (nothing dictated yet) switched the current session and
immediately dropped the listening indicator. Only stop when there's actual
in-progress dictation to avoid misrouting; otherwise keep listening and follow
the newly focused session.
